items.title: Six objects reported at 480 mph in a declassified military infrared video show brightness flicker at bird wingbeat rates
items.summary: In September 2026 the U.S. Department of War released an infrared video recorded from a military aircraft over the Middle East, with a mission report describing six small spherical objects moving at an estimated 480 miles per hour. We measure the brightness of each object in every frame. All six brighten and dim steadily at 7.1-7.9 times per second, each at its own rate and out of step with the others. Tests with planted constant-brightness objects show that neither compression nor the sensor produces this flicker. The same analysis, applied to the Galileo Project's ground-based infrared cameras near Las Vegas, finds flying animals beating steadily at 3.4-10.0 times per second, within the range of bird wingbeats. A nearly stationary object at 60-80% of the aircraft's height would produce the reported ground-projected speed of 480 miles per hour. The six objects are best explained as a small flock of birds flying nearer to the aircraft than the crew assumed. The same analysis also finds 19 objects with similar beats, at 2.3-11.0 times per second, in nine other released military videos. Releasing the redacted sensor and platform data would provide information that could refute the bird hypothesis

items.title: Suppression of $^{14}\mathrm{C}$ photon hits in large liquid scintillator detectors via spatiotemporal deep learning
items.summary: Liquid scintillator detectors are widely used in neutrino experiments due to their low energy threshold and high energy resolution. Despite the tiny abundance of $^{14}$C in LS, the photons induced by the $β$ decay of the $^{14}$C isotope inevitably contaminate the signal, degrading the energy resolution. In this work, we propose three models to tag $^{14}$C photon hits in e$^+$ events with $^{14}$C pile-up, thereby suppressing its impact on the energy resolution at the hit level: a gated spatiotemporal graph neural network and two Transformer-based models with scalar and vector charge encoding. For a simulated test dataset in which each event contains one $^{14}\mathrm{C}$ and one e$^+$ with kinetic energy below 5 MeV, the models achieve $^{14}\mathrm{C}$ recall rates of 25%-48% while maintaining $\mathrm{e}^{+}$ to $^{14}\mathrm{C}$ misidentification below 1%, leading to a large improvement in the resolution of total charge for events where $\mathrm{e}^{+}$ and $^{14}\mathrm{C}$ photon hits strongly overlap in space and time.

items.title: Foundation-Model Supervision of Distilled Potentials for Million-Atom Molecular Dynamics
items.summary: Machine-learned interatomic potentials distilled from foundation models enable fast large-scale molecular dynamics (MD), but they can fail locally in chemical environments that their training data did not sample. System-averaged error metrics and small random audits often miss such sparse or isolated failures. Here we use an exact equivariant foundation model, MACE-MPA-0, to check every atom of million-atom production simulations. Reorganizing two-layer MACE inference into a receiver-chunked three-pass schedule that keeps no per-edge intermediates resident reduces the marginal memory per atom 340-fold, evaluates up to $2.86\times10^{7}$ atoms on a single H200 GPU, and supervises $10^{6}$-atom trajectories in LAMMPS at 1.3% of the run time. Distilled MACE students run four to nine times slower than NEP89 with 0.95-1.28 times the teacher's force error against density functional theory (DFT). In molten SiO$_2$, whole-system checks uncover a persistent tail of under-coordinated atoms hidden by the system-averaged error and an isolated, unphysical O-O contact that a 1% random audit misses 94% of the time. On-the-fly retraining on teacher-labelled 13-Å clusters, with the force loss restricted to their inner 6 Å, removes three quarters of the failure tail and the kilobar-level pressure biases in SiO$_2$ and compressed water; the repair converges to the teacher, not to DFT.

items.title: Dirac branch-cut modes with relativistic transport
items.summary: Emergent Dirac fields, exhibiting effective relativistic physics, are most commonly associated with bulk and surface states in materials such as graphene and topological insulators. Here we show that phase dislocations of a complex Dirac mass support a distinct family of propagating Dirac defect states that behave as massless or massive one-dimensional relativistic modes. These traveling-wave defect states, termed Dirac branch-cut (DBC) modes, are governed by a one-dimensional Dirac Hamiltonian whose effective mass is controlled by the phase difference across the branch cut. Using acoustic metamaterials, we experimentally demonstrate a range of relativistic phenomena exhibited by DBC modes, including relativistic dispersion, energy-independent confinement, Klein tunnelling, and transport along freeform (e.g., spiral) trajectories. Our results establish branch-cut defects as a distinct platform for realizing propagating Dirac defect states, extending relativistic Dirac physics from bulk and surface states to propagating modes confined to defect boundaries.

items.title: A GENERIC-Informed Neural Network for Generative Rheology
items.summary: We present GINNGER (GENERIC-Informed Neural Network for GEnerative Rheology), a framework for discovering thermodynamically admissible constitutive equations from microstructural flow data. Unlike existing approaches that learn constitutive operators, GINNGER reformulates constitutive discovery as the learning of the underlying thermodynamic generators from which constitutive equations emerge. Embedding the GENERIC formalism into the learning process restricts the search to constitutive models that satisfy the first and second laws of thermodynamics by construction, eliminating the need to prescribe phenomenological constitutive equations a priori. A second conceptual advance is a spectral formulation of constitutive discovery in the intrinsic eigenspace of the polymer conformation tensor. This provides a kinematics-independent thermodynamic state space in which the thermodynamic generators depend only on the instantaneous microstructural state, while flow kinematics acts solely as an external driver transporting the system through this space. Consequently, data from shear, extensional, and mixed flows contribute to the discovery of a single constitutive model that generalizes across deformation protocols and flow geometries. By learning thermodynamic generators rather than high-dimensional constitutive operators, GINNGER substantially reduces the complexity of the discovery problem while preserving thermodynamic consistency, material objectivity, and physical interpretability by construction. The framework is validated using high-fidelity simulations, accurately reconstructing constitutive behavior and predicting complex flow fields across previously unseen geometries. GINNGER establishes a new paradigm for constitutive discovery by combining generative, spectral, and thermodynamically grounded learning within a unified framework for data-driven modeling of complex fluids.

items.title: When Should Team KPIs Be Absolute or Relative for Match-Outcome Prediction?
items.summary: In rugby union and association football, team key performance indicators (KPIs) can be represented in absolute terms or relative to the opponent. Relativisation sometimes improves match-outcome prediction and sometimes harms it. There has been no general account of when each occurs. The answer depends on how much the two teams differ in variability and how strongly their KPI values rise and fall together. We combine these properties into the Paired Efficiency Factor (PEF), which generalises Fisher's paired-efficiency result to the unequal-variance conditions typical of competitive sport. The PEF also connects a KPI's statistical efficiency to how much information its relative form carries about the outcome. Combined KPIs can interact in complex ways, so we analyse each indicator on its own. Across 86 team KPIs from professional rugby union and association football, the PEF places every metric in one of four regimes. Anti-correlation is common among these KPIs, especially for high-volume competitive counts, and absolute measures are then usually preferable. Relativisation can still improve prediction when a noisier difference carries more outcome information. An idealised simulation and one representative KPI from each regime confirm both signs under team-blocked cross-validation. The same pairing geometry appears in healthcare, genomics, finance, and manufacturing. The PEF is a diagnostic for when to relativise a performance metric and when not to.

items.title: How the elastic axis folds the transonic flutter boundary: shock energy transfer and conformally calibrated active learning
items.summary: Isogai's case A, a pitch-plunge aerofoil whose elastic axis lies half a chord ahead of the leading edge, has a folded transonic flutter boundary in inviscid flow: near the bottom of the transonic dip several flutter speeds coexist at one Mach number. We map this boundary, and the family obtained by moving the elastic axis, with coupled unsteady Euler simulations, a Gaussian-process surrogate of the damping coefficient trained by batch active learning, and split conformal prediction on independent random simulations, which turns the surrogate into stability calls with a distribution-free error rate. Three failure modes of time-domain damping labels that leave no trace in the residuals are documented, and the half-degree mean incidence left by the common one-degree start is shown to raise the flutter speed at the dip by 2.8%, more than any numerical setting. With 80 simulations the learned case A boundary labels 64 of 65 independent runs correctly, and calibrated calls are wrong in at most 1.6% of cases. Over Mach number, elastic axis and flutter speed index, 193 simulations and 40 calibration runs show that the fold exists only for elastic axes more than about 0.4 chord ahead of the leading edge; it closes between 0.39 and 0.33 chord ahead, on two meshes. Chordwise energy budgets, closed against the solver loads and the growth rate within a few per cent, explain the boundary. The lower branch is crossed through the reduced frequency at unchanged shock phase. On the upper branch the shock is pinned at the trailing edge, and moving the elastic axis aft brings the pivot of the flutter mode towards the section, so that the damping of the supersonic surface falls faster than the residual shock input and the fold closes.

items.title: Electrochemical Molecular Dynamics within the Finite-Field Framework
items.summary: Electrochemical processes at charged interfaces lie at the heart of modern technologies and their continued improvement depends on insights into the relevant atomistic processes. However, the necessary tools to impose constant-voltage conditions in molecular dynamics (MD) simulations typically directly target the electrode charge, making their extension to methods that go beyond an empirical description of metals more cumbersome. In this work, we propose an MD protocol to realize a thermodynamic ensemble in which voltage control is attained, but which is formulated purely within the framework of finite-field simulations in 3D periodic boundary conditions. We show a derivation and implementation of such a control device, which we coin an electrostat, in the ELECTRODE package within LAMMPS. Our simulations systematically benchmark the derived theory against other established approaches, for example, showing its equivalence to a potentiostat, and quantify the importance of properly accounting for ensemble fluctuations. We find that for systems of several thousands of atoms, one obtains the same equilibrium properties with the electrostat as with a simpler constant-field simulation. The difference between the two methods only manifests itself at smaller length scales, thereby establishing practical limits for the inclusion of voltage fluctuations in atomistic simulations of electrochemical systems. The strength of this framework also lies in its simplicity of extension to first-principles ab initio and reactive machine-learning potentials.

items.title: When Cooling Meets Flow: Advection-Driven Orientation Selection in Phase Separation around a Moving Cooling Source
items.summary: We investigate phase separation in a binary fluid subjected to a moving Gaussian cooling source and externally imposed material flow. Unlike conventional homogeneous quenches, the moving thermal field initiates phase separation at different times across the system, creating a spatially varying thermal history and local age. The interplay of a moving cooling source, phase separation and external flow field introduces directional bias, resulting in anisotropic pattern formation. Using an advective Cahn-Hilliard-Cook model coupled to a spatially and temporally varying temperature field, we examine how front propagation, thermal diffusion, phase separation, and material transport jointly select the evolving morphology. In the absence of flow, increasing the cooling-source velocity drives a transition from nearly symmetric structures to asymmetric spiral-like patterns and, at higher velocities, to narrow elongated domains as the thermal front increasingly lags behind the source. Advection reorganizes the phase-separated domains by transporting, stretching, and reorienting them. At low flow velocities, competing thermal and advective histories produce distinct regions of flow-aligned and vertical layers. A stronger flow aligns the domains predominantly along the flow direction. Our results demonstrate that a moving thermal history can encode a spatial record of non-equilibrium phase separation. This work provides a route to controlled morphology selection through the competition between front propagation, thermal diffusion, and material flow.

items.title: Blinking membrane patterns induced by protein binding/unbinding
items.summary: Nonequilibrium membrane pattern formation is studied using meshless membrane simulation. Bound proteins are considered to have two states that generate different membrane spontaneous curvatures. Protein binding and unbinding occur cyclically owing to chemical potential differences, as an off-lattice active Potts model. It is found that this cyclic binding/unbinding can induce blinking domains, with oscillating size: convex domains of the proteins with a higher spontaneous curvature grow, and subsequently, the proteins change to the other state with a lower spontaneous curvature, resulting in domain shrinkage. These processes repeat. In thermal equilibrium, hexagonal convex domains are formed by the competition between bending and surface tension energies, so that they are stably formed only under positive surface tension. However, blinking domains can form even in tensionless membranes.

items.title: Gabor-Enhanced Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Fast Simulations of Acoustic Wavefields
items.summary: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) have gained attention for solving partial differential equations, including the scattered Helmholtz equation, due to their flexibility and mesh-free formulation. However, their performance suffers from low-frequency bias, particularly in high-frequency wavefield simulations, limiting convergence speed and accuracy. To address this, we propose a novel and simplified PINN framework that incorporates explicit, trainable Gabor basis functions to efficiently capture the localized and oscillatory nature of wavefields. Unlike previous Gabor-based PINNs that rely on multiplicative filters or auxiliary networks to learn Gabor parameters, our approach redefines the network's task as learning a nonlinear mapping from input coordinates to a custom Gabor coordinate system, where a Gabor function captures the dominant oscillatory behavior of the wavefield. This formulation absorbs the effect of two Gabor parameters into the learned mapping, reducing computational complexity and eliminating the need for manual tuning of hyperparameters. We also present an efficient formulation for incorporating a Perfectly Matched Layer (PML) into the training by deriving real-valued loss components and introducing an analytical expression for the background wavefield. Numerical experiments on various velocity models show that our Gabor-PINN achieves faster convergence, higher accuracy, and greater robustness to architectural design and initialization compared to both traditional PINNs and prior Gabor-based methods. The improvement lies not in adding architectural complexity --as is common in enhanced PINNs -- but in absorbing this complexity into the learned coordinate transformation, making the method both simpler and more effective. Our implementation is publicly available to support reproducibility and future research.

items.title: Learning the information contained in the microstructure of data distributions
items.summary: Understanding how much and where information is nested in sets of data obtained using different parameters and metrics is a typical problem in the analysis of high-dimensional datasets. Approaches based on relative data-driven metrics may be poorly quantitative and difficult to interpret, while accurate methods may be computationally expensive and impractical for large datasets. Here, we report an efficient, quantitative, and transferable method useful to this end, which we call "Micro-Information Analysis". Its foundation is based on the tight relationship that exists between the microscopic features of data distributions and the information they contain. The method performs preliminary unsupervised clustering, capturing microstructural features of data distributions such as the dominant Gaussian microdomains (microstates) present in them, their population, separation, and their residual non-Gaussian fraction. Leveraging the principle of clustering-and-minimization of Shannon entropy, this allows quantifying in bit (that is, in absolute metric) the information contained in the microstructure of the data, and how much information is nested in each Gaussian and non-Gaussian microdomain. The output of the analysis is a set of easily interpretable Information-Microstructure plots that allow to readily compare and rank data based on their information content and to graphically map the information breakdown among their various microenvironments in diagrams that are easy to interpret. We prove the efficiency of our method by analyzing and ranking data generated synthetically or from molecular simulations, demonstrating how "Micro-Information Analysis" is a physically-grounded quantitative tool useful for the study of physical systems from their data and for data science in general.

items.title: Path-Degenerate Quantum Interferometry for Loss Resilience in Gravitational-Wave Detectors
items.summary: Optical decoherence degrades quantum correlations in squeezed states of light, severely limiting the quantum-nondemolition (QND) sensitivity of gravitational-wave detectors. Here, we propose the path-degenerate quantum interferometry scheme that obviates the need for entire optical subsystems---including additional filter cavities, auxiliary parametric amplifiers, and Faraday isolators---thereby drastically reducing spatial mode mismatches while inherently integrating variational output, a long-standing theoretical proposal to further deepen the QND regime. We experimentally demonstrate a core aspect of this scheme, achieving a shot-noise-preserving signal enhancement that directly counteracts the detrimental effects of readout loss. By delivering an improved signal-to-quantum-noise ratio solely through the consolidation and reduction of currently considered optical subsystems, our approach offers a highly optimized route toward enhanced quantum-noise reduction in upcoming LIGO upgrades and next-generation gravitational-wave observatories.

items.title: Reliable data clustering with Bayesian community detection
items.summary: From neuroscience and genomics to systems biology and ecology, researchers rely on clustering similarity data to uncover modular structure. Most methods work in two steps: first reduce noise, then cluster. The first step runs without regard to the second: it forces arbitrary choices, discards useful information, and can impose structure where none exists. Here we bring the two steps together. Using established Bayesian community detection methods, we let one minimum description length criterion choose both how much to sparsify the data and how to cluster it. This one-step approach keeps all the samples for inference, removes the arbitrary threshold choice, and returns a single cluster when there is no real structure. On synthetic data, our approach recovers clusters under more noise and with fewer samples than standard methods. On gene co-expression data from the human brain, it finds more coherent and more stable clusters than WGCNA, the standard tool in the field. Uniting sparsification and clustering in a single model-selection step provides a principled, noise-resistant way to uncover modular structure in similarity data across fields.

items.title: Simulation of centrifugal separation of particles with equal sedimentation velocities
items.summary: Conventional centrifugal sedimentation cannot readily separate particles with the same sedimentation velocities. Density gradient centrifugation, although highly selective, exposes delicate particles such as drug delivery system (DDS) nanoparticles and exosomes to high osmotic pressure that can cause shrinkage, rupture, or expansion. To separate particles with equal or similar sedimentation velocities while preserving their properties, we propose two methods that exploit thermal fluctuations (Brownian motion): the centrifugal Brownian ratchet method, which uses asymmetric structures, and the centrifugal wavy-channel method, which uses geometric barriers. Two-dimensional Brownian dynamics simulations combining Stokes-Einstein diffusion with centrifugal sedimentation were performed, and particle transport was analyzed using the Péclet number. In the ratchet method, particles with identical sedimentation velocities but different Péclet numbers showed statistically distinct mean arrival positions and times. In the wavy-channel method, periodic entropic barriers interacting with differences in transport properties produced arrival-time differences, achieving temporal separation even for particles with identical sedimentation velocities or Péclet numbers. Both methods separate particles without relying on sedimentation-velocity differences and are expected to preserve particle properties. Because they neither depend on electrical properties nor require a change of medium, they may also be applicable to particles in liquid metals, oils, organic solvents, and ionic liquids.

items.title: High average flux positron sources driven by a mJ-class laser
items.summary: We report on the production and characterisation of MeV-scale positron populations driven by a high-repetition-rate, mJ-class laser system. The positrons are generated via a two-step Bethe--Heitler process driven by laser-wakefield-accelerated electron beams propagating through a mm-scale lead converter. At 10 Hz, approximately 1000 positrons in the 0.8--1.7 MeV energy range were measured over 100 accumulated shots. Stable electron acceleration was demonstrated at 10 Hz, 100 Hz, and 1 kHz using approximately 9 mJ of laser energy in the focal spot, indicating the potential for substantially higher average positron fluxes for laser systems operating at kHz repetition rates and energies of 10s of mJ. Such a positron source allows generating sufficiently high average fluxes of MeV-scale positrons while maintaining low positron yields per pulse and narrow temporal distributions, a regime of particular interest for novel applications in material science and fundamental physics. The measured positron yields and spectra are in good agreement with Monte Carlo simulations, supporting the modelling of the positron-production process and magnetic transport system.

items.title: Emergence of Correlations Between Records and Maximum in Random Time Series
items.summary: We compute exactly the covariance between the maximum $M$ and the number of records $K$ in a discrete time series of $n$ entries as a quantitative probe of the history leading to an extreme event. For continuous IID series, with a common probability distribution function (PDF) $p(x)$, we find the striking result that $M$ and $K$ are uncorrelated for any $n \geq 1$. We show that this independence is rather fragile and the covariance $C_q(n)$ between $M$ and $K$ becomes nonzero when $p(x)$ becomes discontinuous due to a delta-component at $x=0$ with an amplitude $0< q < 1$. This time series models the occurrence of dry days with probability $q$ in a precipitation time series when there is no rainfall. We show that there is an interesting shape transition at a critical value $q_c$ where the covariance $C_q(n)$, as a function of $n$, changes from monotonic ($q<q_c$) to non monotonic behavior (for $q>q_c$). We compute the critical strength $q_c$ exactly. Furthermore, for large $n$, we show that $C_q(n)$ decays as a power law, with an exponent that depends on the tail of $p(x)$. We then compare our theoretical predictions with real precipitation data from several weather stations across Germany, finding a very good agreement.

items.title: Geometric inflation of deviations challenges neural quantum states in dynamics of quantum Ising models
items.summary: Neural quantum states (NQS) have emerged as a powerful framework for simulating non-equilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated quantum systems, offering scalable variational representations of highly entangled states. Yet, accurate NQS simulations have been found to be surprisingly challenging in some physical regimes of limited complexity. Here, we address paradigmatic quench dynamics of a one-dimensional quantum Ising model as a controlled benchmark. Through supervised state reconstruction we establish substantially tighter empirical upper bounds on the required parameter count than previous estimates, ruling out representational limitations as the key obstruction. Instead, we uncover a geometric inflation of small deviations as a hitherto overlooked challenge for accurate solutions of the infinitesimal time-dependent variational principle (TDVP): the dynamical rotation of the kernel of the quantum geometric tensor (QGT) can suddenly lend physical significance to previously irrelevant parameter deviations. The stability of matrix product state solutions of the same TDVP suggests that the non-linearity of the neural network ansatz is the origin of the sensitivity. These results identify QGT-null-space rotation as a geometric diagnostic of sensitive NQS dynamics and as a concrete target for improving TDVP algorithms.

items.title: Energy-Aware Earth System Science: A Community Roadmap
items.summary: Earth system models underpin the evidence that informs net-zero policy, yet their energy demands are rarely considered when judging model quality. Using archived output from 159 models spanning five generations of the Coupled Model Intercomparison Project (CMIP), we show that model error has fallen at a constant rate of 13.5 per cent per doubling of compute since 1995. Halving CMIP6 error would require 28 times more compute. Improvements are uneven, with sea-level pressure and surface air temperature errors declining 3.5-fold and 2.7-fold since CMIP1, but precipitation error by only 7 per cent. Machine-learning weather models match or exceed operational forecast skill at a fraction of the runtime, but none publishes measured energy, and including training changes how they rank. We propose a skill-energy framework that combines an empirical Pareto front with a ranking score. These findings argue for standardised reporting of energy use and performance ahead of CMIP8.

items.title: Exponential-SWAP gate between bosonic motional modes of trapped ions
items.summary: The exponential-SWAP (eSWAP) gate generates a coherent superposition of identity and SWAP operations, with continuously tunable amplitudes. We experimentally implement this gate between two bosonic motional modes of trapped ions using spin-independent and spin-dependent beam splitter interactions. Measurements of selected slices of the joint characteristic function for distinct input states test the gate and demonstrate continuous control of the identity-SWAP superposition. This implementation provides a tunable interaction for hybrid qubit-bosonic quantum information processing.

items.title: Validating LLM-generated political networks with survey-reported partisan exposure
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to simulate human behavior in social science research, including decisions, interactions, and social relationships. However, in network formation tasks, existing evaluations often focus on aggregate network properties, while networks with plausible structural properties may still fail to reproduce individuals' social and political environments. Here, we generate LLM-based political networks using personas sampled from the nationally representative ANES 2020--2022 Social Media Study and use respondents' survey-reported partisan exposure as an empirical benchmark for the political environments generated for the corresponding personas. We first characterize the structural properties and political assortativity of the generated networks, and then compare ego-level partisan exposure with the survey. We find that the structure and political assortativity of the generated networks vary across experimental configurations. More importantly, when comparing generated partisan exposure with the survey, some models generate stronger separation between Democratic and Republican egos than reported in the survey, with higher same-party and lower cross-party exposure, while others mainly underestimate Republican exposure across ego groups. Moreover, networks with similar political assortativity can still generate different partisan environments around the same personas, including among networks with plausible structural properties. Finally, generated networks show group-specific errors, under- or overestimating exposure to either Democrats or Republicans for specific social groups. These findings show that evaluating LLM-based social simulations only through aggregate outcomes can hide errors in the local environments through which those outcomes emerge, highlighting the importance of validation at both aggregate and individual levels.

items.title: Gauss' law for arbitrarily moving Gaussian surfaces: A revisit
items.summary: We have re-examined the integral form of Gauss' law for arbitrarily moving charges inside and outside an arbitrarily expanding (or contracting) and deforming Gaussian surface. We have explicitly calculated the time-dependent Gauss' flux integral for such a generic non-static case with the Maxwell equations under consideration. We have obtained an evolution equation $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}\text{t}}\oint_{s(t)}\vec{E}\cdot\text{d}\vec{s}(t)=\frac{I^{(s)}_{\text{in}}(t)}{ε_0}$ for the time-dependence of the flux-integral. We have demonstrated pedagogically that while the flux integral is dependent on the expansion/contraction of the surface, it is independent of its deformation.

items.title: On the stability and emittance growth of different particle phase-space distributions in a long magnetic quadrupole channel
items.summary: The behavior of K-V, waterbag, parabolic, conical and Gaussian distributions in periodic quadrupole channels is studied by particle simulations. In the parameter range studied, the response associated with the K-V instabilities becomes progressively less pronounced toward the Gaussian distribution. For the third-order instability studied here, the emittance growth factor of an initially Gaussian beam after a large number of periods is considerably lower than that of an equivalent K-V distribution.\newline\indent In addition, the non-K-V distributions exhibit a rapid initial emittance growth within approximately one period of the channel, which becomes very significant at high beam intensities. This growth is attributed to the homogenization of the space-charge density, resulting in a conversion of electric-field energy into transverse kinetic and potential energy. Two simple analytical formulae based on different energy-partition assumptions are derived as estimates for this effect and are compared with the results obtained from particle simulations. They are not rigorous lower and upper bounds for arbitrary beam evolution. \\[6pt] Original publication in Particle Accelerators {\bf 15}, 47--65 (1984)}

items.title: Influence of Droplet Morphology on Fluid Dynamics and Impact Erosion of Wind Turbine Blades
items.summary: The impact of droplets, such as rain and sea sprays, on wind turbine blade surfaces can cause severe damage through leading-edge erosion (LEE). Current industrial practice has largely relied on empirical fatigue models to predict damage progression and guide maintenance. However, an important limitation of existing models is the assumption on ideal impact conditions, including perfectly spherical droplet and normal incidence, which rarely occur in reality. This study develops a fluid-structure interaction (FSI) model that couples incompressible multiphase flow simulations with finite element (FE) analysis of blade materials. Using this framework, we investigate the impact dynamics of droplets with arbitrary shapes and orientations. The results reveal a positive correlation between the peak impact pressure, the influential area at the pressure peak, and the peak impact force. In contrast, the time of peak force scales inversely due to momentum conservation. From these findings, we propose a $\textit{universal scaling law}$ that relates all key impact loadings to the simple parameter of the droplet $\textit{projection area}$, which can be determined solely from the initial droplet geometry and orientation. This law provides a predictive framework for impact loading dynamics of non-ideal shapes, offering new insights into the mechanisms of LEE and improving the accuracy of erosion predictions for wind turbine blades.

items.title: Theoretical studies of envelope oscillations and instabilities of mismatched intense charged-particle beams in periodic focusing channels
items.summary: The behavior of mismatched intense charged-particle beams in periodic transport channels of the solenoid and quadrupole type is studied theoretically. The envelope-oscillation frequencies of the mismatched beam are obtained by the smooth-approximation method and by numerical evaluation of the linearly perturbed K-V envelope equations. Phase shifts of the envelope oscillations and growth factors per focusing period in the case of instability are calculated for a solenoid and a magnetic quadrupole (FODO) channel using the parameters of the Maryland and GSI beam transport experiments. For comparison and the purpose of illustration, the K-V equations are integrated numerically, and envelope curves as well as single-particle trajectories for mismatched beams are shown in graphical form. In addition, computer simulation studies with the PARMILA code were performed, and results are presented both for K-V and a Gaussian distribution in transverse phase space.\\~\\ Published in: Particle~Accelerators~{\bf 14}, 227--260 (1984)}

items.title: Kinematic Closure of Drop Impact
items.summary: Predicting how far a liquid droplet spreads upon impacting a solid surface is governed by a complex competition between inertia, surface tension, and viscous dissipation. Existing models typically estimate this maximum spreading diameter by prescribing the spreading time or velocity from a decoupled asymptotic limit, restricting predictive accuracy across regimes. Here, we formulate a reduced kinematic description by resolving both the characteristic spreading time and spreading velocity from an energy balance coupling capillary storage and viscous dissipation. Unifying these two asymptotically constrained closures via the kinematic relation $D_{\max} = V_s t_s$ yields a compact, parameter-free approximation for the maximum spreading ratio that bridges the inertio-capillary and inertio-viscous regimes. We quantify the accuracy of this reduced closure against the exact implicit energy relation and demonstrate that it quantitatively collapses our experimental measurements alongside extensive literature data across wide ranges of Weber and Ohnesorge numbers, droplet sizes, and surface wettabilities without adjustable prefactors.

items.title: When is vaccine prioritization worth optimizing?
items.summary: Optimizing vaccine prioritization is often treated as the default policy response when vaccine supply is limited. Yet optimized prioritization carries administrative, ethical and communication costs, motivating an upstream question: whether differences among vaccine allocations can alter epidemic outcomes enough to make optimization epidemiologically necessary. We show that optimization is not always worth pursuing: in some regimes, vaccination markedly reduces epidemic burden, but many feasible allocation rules perform almost equally well, making the necessity of optimization low. We quantify this necessity as the range of epidemic outcomes generated by different allocations under fixed supply and show that it is governed by competition between vaccinating high-contact groups to slow transmission and vaccinating groups that benefit most directly: necessity is low when these protection routes are balanced and high when one dominates. Increasing transmission intensity changes this balance and drives a transition in the optimal allocation from transmission-focused prioritization toward direct protection. Different prevention objectives exhibit distinct transition thresholds, creating regimes in which optimizing one objective substantially compromises another, thereby revealing when the choice of prevention target matters most. This framework reframes vaccine prioritization as a prior decision problem, identifying when optimization is warranted, when simpler rules suffice, and when prevention goals conflict.

items.title: All-optical Lithography for Spatiotemporal Patterning of High-Modulation Azopolymer Microreliefs
items.summary: Microstructured surfaces are central to photonics, biointerfaces, and coating technologies, but they are typically fabricated through multistep workflows involving masks, masters,development, and etching. Azopolymers offer a direct light-driven route to surface structuring, although holographic photopatterning of flat films has largely remained limited to smooth, shallow, and engraving-like reliefs with limited vertical modulation. Here we show that computer-generated holograms with co-designed bright and dark regions can spatially confine inward mass transport and directly generate isolated protruding microstructures with surface modulations of several micrometers from pristine flat azopolymer films. Single exposures produce individual protrusions and arrays, whereas sequential tailored exposures generate flattopped and hierarchical microreliefs. The same workflow produces connected freeform structures and enables optical erasure and rewriting within the same surface region. We further transfer the optically programmed azopolymer morphologies into another transparent polymer and demonstrate replicated microlenses operating at multiple visible wavelengths, with focal response controlled through the master-writing parameters. These results establish an alloptical framework for generating and reconfiguring complex, high-modulation azopolymer microreliefs from flat films through combined control of holographic illumination geometry and exposure history, with replication extending their use to materials selected for their final functional properties.

items.title: Evolution and breakdown of chiral anomaly in Weyl semiconductor tellurium
items.summary: Chiral anomaly in topological materials manifests as negative longitudinal magnetoresistance, yet the tunability and evolution of this effect remain elusive. Here we show that doped tellurium serves as a versatile platform to realize a giant negative longitudinal magnetoresistance that is highly tunable via the Fermi level and magnetic field. By moving the Fermi level towards the Weyl point, we observe a pronounced enhancement of negative magnetoresistance, which arises from chiral anomaly and robustly persists up to ambient temperature. Beyond the quantum limit, the system exhibits positive linear magnetoconductance, serving as a compelling transport signature of the chiral anomaly in the lowest Landau level. Notably, in the extreme quantum limit at cryogenic temperatures, the magnetoresistance undergoes a dramatic reversal from negative to positive. This reversal points to a potential field-induced phase transition into a collective electronic state driven by enhanced electron-electron interactions. Our findings provide valuable insights into the unconventional chiral transport and emergent correlated quantum states under extreme magnetic fields.

items.title: Role of Device Size on Island Divertor Performance of W7-X-like Configurations
items.summary: To examine how the island divertor performs in future low-shear stellarator reactors, we simulate (using EMC3-Eirene [1]) 3 different scales of W7-X: its current size, increased by a factor 2, and increased by a factor 4, where 4 times W7-X corresponds roughly to a reactor-scale device. For a single magnetic configuration, the standard magnetic configuration in W7-X, we examine how increasing the size of W7-X alters the divertor performance of the island divertor. We analyze how device scale shifts the location of the ionization source and the downstream density and temperature trends in the island divertor for achieving detachment. Local field line analysis shows that factor 2 and factor 4 size scalings achieve target densities $>10^{21} \ \mathrm{m}^{-3}$ via plasma ``self-baffling" within the open island divertor geometry. Finally, the heat and particle flux deposition on the scaled-up island divertor configurations are calculated. We observe a separation in the target heat and particle flux distribution with increased machine size in agreement with [2]. The target heat fluxes are $<5 \ \mathrm{MW}/\mathrm{m}^2$ at high separatrix densities. This shows that the separation of the heat and particle flux channels remains to be largely unproblematic. This analysis helps guide how to improve the open island divertor geometries for future stellarator reactors.

items.title: Spatiotemporal Adaptive Eigenspectrum Remapping in Transcranial Ultrasound Localization Microscopy
items.summary: Clutter suppression is a critical preprocessing step in ultrasound blood flow imaging, yet conventional singular value decomposition (SVD) filtering depends on data-specific eigenvalue cutoffs that can remove slow flow along with tissue clutter. Here, we introduce adaptive eigenspectrum remapping (AER), a general framework in which clutter is suppressed by continuously remapping, rather than truncating, the eigenvalue spectrum of the spatiotemporal covariance, and we investigate zero-phase component analysis (ZCA) matrix whitening as an instance of AER for transcranial ultrasound localization microscopy (ULM). Rather than discarding eigenspaces, ZCA-based AER whitens the eigenvalue spectrum, reducing the dominance of coherent clutter, including skull reverberation, while retaining weak flow signals. We evaluate AER on both temporal and spatial covariance matrices in mouse brain datasets acquired with long temporal ensembles. Compared with SVD filtering, ZCA improves microbubble contrast and vascular image quality, increases trajectory density across low- and high-concentration regimes, and reveals more low-velocity trajectories in ULM velocity maps. Spatial AER further maintains reconstruction quality across extended ensembles and enables fuller single capillary reporter (SCaRe) reconstructions, including connected artery-to-capillary-to-vein tracks. These results support AER, here instantiated as ZCA whitening, as a data-adaptive alternative to manually thresholded SVD filtering for high-resolution microvascular imaging.

items.title: Graph-Learned Spring SST Evolution and Land-Ocean Synergy Improve Yangtze Summer Rainfall Prediction
items.summary: Seasonal prediction of Yangtze summer rainfall is challenged by nonstationary oceanic precursors. Here we demonstrate that accounting for the evolution of spring SST and state-dependent land surface information improves predictability. Graph total variation (GTV) is applied to March-May SST fields over the western Pacific, Niño3.4, and tropical Indian Ocean to identify spatially coherent, month-specific SST coefficients for each grid cell and month to form a scalar GTV index. The learned coefficient patterns capture April-to-May ENSO decay and an opposing Indian Ocean adjustment, consistent with coupled Indo-Pacific variability. During 2008-2022, the GTV index prediction outperforms Niño3.4-based and sparse-regression benchmarks. Further improvement is achieved by including interactions of May Indo-China Peninsula soil moisture with Indian Ocean SST, importantly also correcting several underestimated wet summers. Circulation diagnostics associate the learned index with a summer geopotential-height dipole and Yangtze moisture convergence, while dry-Indochina/warm-Indian-Ocean conditions coincide with stronger westward extension of the western Pacific subtropical high.

items.title: Properties and challenges of machine learning closures for ten-moment fluid models in the case of Landau damping
items.summary: Two-fluid ten-moment models for plasma simulations evolve the velocity moments of the Velocity Distribution Function (VDF) up to the pressure tensor and require a closure for the divergence of the next velocity moment, the heat flux. We investigate the use of Machine Learning (ML) models for the discovery of heat flux closures, as an alternative to the typically employed Hammett-Perkins-like analytical closures. As a test case, we investigate Landau damping, which describes a resonant process of energy transfer between particles and waves. We find that fluid simulations with ML closures correctly reproduce both the damping frequency and the non-linear phase of Landau damping, and thereby outperform Hammett-Perkins-like closures, within the parameter ranges seen during training and when interpolating within those ranges. When extrapolating beyond the training data, the performance of the ML closure degrades with increasing distance from known parameters. We then investigate how well offline metrics (i.\,e.\; evaluating the trained model on fully-kinetic reference simulations, without inserting it into two-fluid simulations) can predict online performance, when the model is actually used in the two-fluid simulation. Our results show that offline metrics do not fully explain online performance, highlighting important implications for method evaluation in this field. We further investigate suitable metrics for online performance evaluation in the absence of a fully-kinetic reference simulation, which is often computationally expensive to run. We propose using the temporal evolution of entropy to evaluate the performance of reduced models with ML closures when no or few kinetic reference simulations are available.

items.title: Surface-Normal Electric Spin in Obliquely Excited Parallel-Slit SPP Fields
items.summary: Handedness-dependent light-matter interactions require control of local electric-field rotation, but generating controlled surface-normal spin textures is difficult under oblique illumination. Here, we show that oblique s-polarized illumination of a periodic array of parallel slits produces spatially alternating surface-normal electric spin, with its period tunable by the incidence angle. We further show that the spin texture changes qualitatively between substrate- and air-side excitation depending on whether the SPP field interferes with the excitation field. Under substrate-side excitation, the spin distribution follows the conventional spin-flow relation, whereas under air-side excitation, interference between the SPP and excitation fields produces a distinct spatial periodicity and allows the spin extrema to coincide with the field-intensity maxima. A simple interference model reproduces these contrasting spin textures.

items.title: Wavelength Diversity Expands the Expressive Power of Optical Computing
items.summary: Universal function approximation underpins neural networks' capacity to represent nonlinear relationships, but realizing this capability in optical hardware requires engineering the computational features encoded in light. Here, we show that wavelength diversity enhances optical function-approximation expressivity through wavelength-scaled Fourier features generated by a shared phase encoder, without increasing the number of input-encoded harmonics. Multiple wavelengths contribute to the representation of each output function rather than merely serving as independent computational channels. We establish theoretical scaling laws and approximation-error bounds, revealing that, for nondispersive encoders, the spectral endpoints determine the accessible computational bandwidth, while intermediate illumination wavelengths enrich the available harmonics within that bandwidth. Numerical studies demonstrate improved approximation of real- and complex-valued nonlinear functions, with a representative design achieving more than a 100-fold reduction in mean-squared error relative to tested monochromatic optical processors with the same number of trainable phase features. Experimentally, we validate enhanced approximation accuracy and demonstrate the simultaneous approximation of 4,136 distinct nonlinear functions using a compact, single-layer diffractive processor under five-wavelength illumination. These results establish wavelength diversity as an additional physical resource for scaling the expressive power of optical computing and enhancing the accuracy of parallel nonlinear function approximation.

items.title: Thermalization-induced self-polarization of temporally incoherent light: A nonequilibrium wave turbulence kinetic approach
items.summary: Conservative nonlinear waves generally undergo an irreversible process of thermalization toward the Rayleigh--Jeans (RJ) equilibrium state. Light thermalization has recently been experimentally investigated in the two-dimensional transverse spatial dynamics of multimode waveguides. Here, we consider the one-dimensional temporal dynamics of incoherent light propagating in a weakly birefringent single-mode fiber. We show that light thermalization is responsible for a self-polarization of the incoherent wave during its propagation. Within the framework of wave turbulence theory, we show that this phenomenon originates from a nonequilibrium process of adiabatic cooling: polarization fluctuations are continuously transferred toward the high-frequency tails of a local RJ equilibrium state, whose effective temperature decreases during propagation, thereby increasing the degree of light polarization. Moreover, in the absence of a high-frequency cut-off that would regularize the ultraviolet catastrophe in the temporal domain, the optical wave exhibits an ever-increasing degree of polarization, ultimately approaching unity. These results show that it is thermodynamically advantageous for the optical field to evolve toward a polarized state, which provides new insight into spontaneous self-organization phenomena in conservative Hamiltonian systems operating far from thermodynamic equilibrium.

items.title: Permutationally Invariant Polynomial Descriptors as Colored Multigraphs
items.summary: The combinatorial explosion in monomial counts limits the extension of global permutationally invariant polynomial (PIP) potential energy surfaces to larger molecular systems. We use graph-theoretic language to reformulate PIPs as colored multigraphs and develop a series of theoretical and computational tools. First, we introduce an offline PIP generation algorithm whose cost has an upper bound independent of atom count for a fixed degree cutoff and number of element types. Second, we introduce a new online PIP evaluation algorithm, termed tensor-network descent. For the full PIP set through degree $d$ in a system of $M$ atoms, the evaluation complexity for $1\le d\le14$ is $O\!\left(f(d)M^{\left\lfloor(\sqrt{1+8d}+1)/2\right\rfloor}\right)$. At the commonly used cutoff of $d=5$, the online evaluation complexity decreases from the $M^{10}$ scaling of conventional explicit term-by-term computation to $M^3$. Numerical tests using the full PIP set through degree 5 show that our method achieves speedups of several orders of magnitude on most MD17 systems and remains computationally affordable for systems containing more than one thousand atoms. The method has a native tensor form, supports automatic differentiation, and provides a unified theoretical construction of four classes of PIP descriptors defined consistently across systems---global, atom-centered, bond-centered, and cluster-centered---establishing a representation and computational foundation for PIP potentials for large systems and for transfer across systems. Together, these results show that PIPs are neither inherently restricted to small systems nor intrinsically nontransferable.

items.title: Precision measurement of the ground-state hyperfine constant for $^9Be^+$ in a linear Paul trap via magnetically insensitive hyperfine transitions
items.summary: Direct measurements of the ground-state magnetically insensitive hyperfine transition |F=2,mF=0>->|F=1,mF=0> of $^9Be^+$ ions have been performed using microwave-driven state transfer. The $^9Be^+$ ions are confined and laser-cooled in a linear Paul trap, forming a Coulomb crystal. The transition frequencies have been measured over a magnetic field range of $ \pm 0.5 mT $ centered at zero magnetic field, and the acquired data were fitted accounting for the high-order Zeeman effect. The hyperfine constant A is determined to be -625.008840(35) MHz, achieving a relative precision of $ 5.6 \times 10^{-8}$.

items.title: Stochastic Shockwave Dynamics in First-Order Traffic Flow
items.summary: Moving congestion fronts vary across realizations even when the traffic-flow law is fixed. This paper develops a generator-based formulation of the Lighthill--Whitham--Richards (LWR) model with random initial density and a deterministic fundamental diagram. Randomness enters through the initial spatial density field; every realization follows the same conservation law. For a smooth strictly concave fundamental diagram, we adapt established one-sided spatial Markov closure to traffic variables under the stated spatial-process and regularity assumptions, and derive a kinetic balance for physically normalized front intensities. Evolving the spatial generator provides density laws and congestion-front statistics without solving a road-grid problem for every realization. The formulation is continuous in physical space and time, while its numerical implementation approximates density state and integrates physical time. Four experiments distinguish deterministic consistency from stochastic comparison. Riemann and signal examples recover independently constructed exact LWR solutions. Smooth strictly concave approximations approach the deterministic triangular-diagram signal solution over the tested finite horizons; this does not establish stochastic closure at contacts or the capacity kink. A matched Monte Carlo Godunov ensemble evaluates front counts, sizes, mergers, and density distributions. The evolved generator also yields an instantaneous travel-time distribution for a frozen density field, compared with the same functional of the matched Godunov profiles. This quantity is not experienced travel time through evolving traffic. Resolution checks identify remaining normalization and small-front-loss effects. The contribution is direct evolution and interpretation of traffic-state and front distributions under a fixed first-order traffic law.

items.title: Diffusion-controlled reactions with time-dependent surface reactivity
items.summary: We investigate diffusion-controlled reactions on a reactive surface with time-dependent reactivity. Starting from a conventional formulation via diffusion equation with Robin boundary condition for the macroscopic concentration of particles, we aim at quantifying how temporal variations of reactivity affect the survival probability and the associated first-reaction time (FRT) of a single particle on the reactive surface. Using an adiabatic description, we first identify five long-time regimes of the first-reaction time distribution, ranging from exponential and stretched-exponential to power-law decay. In particular, sufficiently rapid decay of the reactivity leads to a nonzero probability of never reacting, despite diffusion in a bounded domain. Second, we provide a probabilistic reformulation of this problem and compare it with a different scenario of encounter-dependent reactivity. Our theoretical predictions are validated via extensive Monte Carlo simulations.

items.title: Compact Fully Integrated Alignment-Free and Linearly Polarized Ho$^{3+}$ Single-Frequency Waveguide Laser
items.summary: We report, for the first time, a fully integrated Ho$^{3+}$-doped fluoride glass waveguide laser incorporating a femtosecond laser-inscribed waveguide and waveguide Bragg grating. A line-by-line inscription technique was employed to fabricate the Bragg gratings, yielding highly consistent and reproducible grating characteristics with precise control of the Bragg resonance wavelength. A compact 12.4 mm cavity achieves stable single-frequency lasing at 2062.21 nm with a linewidth of less than 5 MHz. The laser exhibits intrinsically linearly polarized emission. This alignment-free architecture provides a compact and robust platform for integrated mid-infrared single-frequency laser sources.

items.title: Deep-learning-based low-energy trigger algorithms for the Hyper-Kamiokande experiment
items.summary: Modern machine learning techniques have become increasingly important in particle physics because of their powerful pattern-recognition capabilities, including in real-time data acquisition where stringent runtime constraints apply. This paper details the performance of deep-learning-based trigger algorithms for a large water Cherenkov detector such as Hyper-Kamiokande, aimed at low-energy neutrino events (below 7 MeV). The performance of custom neural-network supervised classifiers is shown alongside two anomaly-detection approaches trained solely on detector noise: a pure autoencoder and a model based on Manifold Projection-Diffusion Recovery. The supervised model shows signal identification efficiencies of 76.7% for single electrons of 3 MeV kinetic energy, significantly exceeding signal efficiencies obtained from a traditional hit-count-based trigger of 26.4%, while the Manifold Projection-Diffusion Recovery approach reaches 35.4% at the same operating point. Runtime evaluations on GPU yield per-window inference latencies well below the millisecond scale.

items.title: Low-Cost Third-order Algebraic Diagrammatic Construction Method for Excited States Using Tensor Hypercontraction and State-Specific Frozen Natural Orbitals
items.summary: We have developed a reduced-cost framework for excited-state calculations by combining the state-specific frozen natural orbital (SS-FNO) approach with the third-order algebraic diagrammatic construction [ADC(3)] method and tensor hypercontraction (THC). This strategy enables a systematic and controllable truncation of the virtual orbital space, while significantly lowering the computational scaling through the THC representation of the electron repulsion integrals. The method allows black-box application via adjustable thresholds and includes a perturbative correction that compensates for the truncation error. We have used the CIS(D) method to generate the natural orbitals for the excited states. The performance of the SS-FNO-THC-ADC(3) method is assessed for valence, Rydberg, and charge-transfer excitations. Benchmark calculations demonstrate that the combined approach achieves excellent agreement with the canonical ADC(3) results. The efficiency of the present implementation is demonstrated by calculating the excitation energy of a molecule containing 31 atoms and more than one thousand basis functions.

items.title: Streamwise dispersion with interphase mass transfer through a tube
items.summary: Reactive solute transport in shear flows is of broad importance in chemical engineering, liquid--solid chromatography, and environmental mechanics, particularly in flow reactors and fluidic devices involving interphase mass transfer. Based on the recently developed streamwise dispersion theory for inert solutions (Guan & Chen, 2024, J. Fluid Mech., vol. 980, A33), we present an analytical model for reactive dispersion of chemically active solutes characterized by first-order, irreversible surface reactions. The extension is not a simple perturbation because the reactive boundary destroys mass conservation with streamwise and radial derivatives coupled. The model establishes how the microscopic kinetic reactivity and radial eigenmodes combine to determine a newly defined (effective) local exchange rate. We derive rigorous explicit solutions for the local moments, concentration, and phenomenological transport coefficients at arbitrary reactivity, in quantitative agreement with numerical simulations across all regimes. For tube Poiseuille flows, we reveal pre-asymptotic behaviours including sign-changing radial exchange, reactivity-enhanced drift, reactivity-reduced dispersivity, and non-Gaussian concentration profiles. Small- and large-Damköhler-number asymptotics for the local and global transport coefficients identify the reaction-limited and diffusion-limited regimes, connecting the conservative case to the Dirichlet limit at infinite reactivity. This streamwise perspective could advance our understanding of macroscale transport in chemically active systems.

items.title: Residual diagnostics for detecting the breakdown of the single power-law approximation in photoelectron yield spectroscopy: application to doped silicon
items.summary: Our automated analysis of photoelectron yield spectroscopy (PYS) estimates the threshold Ith and the exponent n of a single power law for every spectrum. When this model fits poorly, however, the analysis cannot tell whether the data or the model is at fault. Here we present residual diagnostics that separate the two causes. The exponent is scanned continuously on a 1/n-power fit with an Akaike information criterion (AIC) based on the mean absolute error (MAE), and the spread of the resulting Akaike weights ($P \times Δn$) quantifies the uncertainty of the estimate. The normalized MAE (NMAE) and the RMSE-to-MAE ratio (RMR) assess the data quality, the Durbin-Watson (DW) statistic assesses the model adequacy, and the three checks are reported in parallel. With criteria set from an Au reference, the diagnostics were applied to 60 continuous measurements in air of four HF-treated Si samples. For heavily doped p-type Si, DW fell below its criterion, whereas the means of NMAE and RMR remained within their criteria. Prompted by this flag, we fitted the spectrum with a two-component model with fixed exponents (n = 1 and 2.5); the AIC decreased by 56, DW increased from 0.86 to 1.99, and the two components set in at 4.70 and 5.28 eV. For heavily doped n-type Si, the change during air exposure was consistent with a single component. The diagnostics thus identify the spectra that require a multi-component analysis without assuming an emission mechanism.

items.title: Designing an AI Agent That Does Not Tutor: Design Rules for Socratic Probing in Introductory Physics
items.summary: Instructors need to know whether a student understands a concept, not only whether the student can produce a correct answer, and the two have come apart: a student can paste a physics question into a chatbot and submit a fluent, correct answer without understanding it. We built a conversational AI agent for introductory mechanics that only probes. It is designed as an instrument that a correct answer alone should not pass. Its key measure is cave detection: identifying a correct first idea that the student abandons when a single variable of the scenario is changed. A single right-or-wrong item cannot see this. The agent asks a student to commit to a prediction about an everyday situation, explain it without physics vocabulary, and defend that explanation against a changed case built from the student's own words. It does not teach, hint, confirm, or correct, and it reports nothing until the end. Such an instrument works only if its replies give nothing away. LLM agents tend to leak evaluation: praise, word choice, reply length, and pacing reveal whether an answer was right, and a student who knows stops reasoning. We report design rules that suppress this leakage, derived from eight versions of the agent and more than 40 scripted simulation runs. The obvious fixes often made leakage worse: listing forbidden praise phrases increased praise, and a single worked example in the prompt spread into unrelated conversations. Each changed case had to alter exactly one variable; otherwise a changed answer could not be traced to a single idea. The evidence is simulation evidence only: no real students have used the agent, and the author wrote both the personas and the scoring rules. This paper reports design findings, not learning outcomes.

items.title: Implementing the EIT complete electrode model through Robin boundary conditions
items.summary: Objective. Medical electrical impedance tomography systems prescribe electrode currents. Accurate voltages, even on passive electrodes, require the complete electrode model (CEM), the most accurate model known for skin electrodes. Its current constraints specify total electrode currents, whereas standard finite element boundary interfaces impose local conditions. We describe how to implement the CEM through Robin boundary conditions, which are available in standard FEM packages. Approach. Prescribed electrode potentials give Robin problems whose unit-potential responses define an electrode transadmittance matrix. We prove equivalence to the conventional augmented CEM and formalise the discrete energy, equivalence and reference arguments in Lean 4. Numerical comparisons use two-dimensional P1 finite elements in DOLFINx, FreeFEM, GetFEM, MFEM and NGSolve, with the same nodal reference potential as EIDORS. Main results. For identical assembled blocks, the two procedures have the same solution set whenever the Robin matrix is invertible. Across the five packages in dimensionless test cases, maximum absolute electrode-potential differences from EIDORS were below $5\times10^{-13}$ (2692 nodes), and errors against an exact rational-arithmetic reference were below $1.1\times10^{-13}$ (2535 nodes). Significance. Standard Robin solves and consistent electrode-current integration provide a portable route to the current-driven CEM, with current constraints enforced through a small electrode system.

items.title: Transverse momentum as the counter-diabatic generator in bent waveguide couplers
items.summary: Bending the axis of a mode-evolution coupler suppresses the nonadiabatic coupling between its supermodes, and bent couplers of this kind were recently shown to realize the counter-diabatic (CD) protocol. Here we identify the operator responsible. Rigid lateral displacement of a waveguide structure is generated by the transverse momentum $\hat p_x$, whose diagonal matrix elements vanish in a real supermode basis and whose off-diagonal element is purely imaginary; in a two-mode system such an operator is proportional to $\sy$. The CD term of a two-waveguide coupler is itself proportional to $\sy$, while the detuning and the coupling, the two parameters set by the waveguide widths and spacing, lie in the $σ_z$--$σ_x$ plane and cannot produce it. The transverse momentum is therefore the CD generator of the bent coupler, by necessity rather than by design. Equating the term it supplies to the nonadiabatic coupling gives the axis slope in closed form as a ratio of two matrix elements of the unperturbed supermodes at a single cross section, which a commutator identity recasts in coupled-mode variables as $\dot{\xo}=\dotθ/(γ\dbeta^{2})$. The expression agrees with the numerical offset search to $0.3\%$ and requires no search. Beam propagation simulations confirm the design and compare it, for the first time, with the CD protocol realized by unitary transformation in a straight coupler built from the same reference structure. The two devices reach $0.994$ and $1.000$ supermode fidelity where the untreated coupler reaches $0.886$, and agree in bandwidth and fabrication tolerance, while their internal trajectories differ by exactly the frame transformation that relates them.

items.title: PINN-LPCDD: Physics-Informed Neural Network with Learnable and Physically Consistent Domain Decomposition for Compressible Multi-Medium Flows
items.summary: The physics-informed neural network (PINN) faces significant challenges when solving compressible multi-medium flows, including the inability to locate interface positions, poor approximation of discontinuities, and difficulty in handling high-pressure-ratio problems between media with large stiffness differences. To address these issues, we propose PINN with Learnable and Physically Consistent Domain Decomposition (PINN-LPCDD), a framework that incorporates the sharp interface method (SIM) into PINNs for solving compressible multi-medium flows. Firstly, we design separate sub-networks for each medium with learnable parameters to automatically learn interface positions, so that the domain decomposition is physically consistent, and the contact discontinuity at the interface is naturally sharp. Secondly, the Euler equations with artificial viscosity are solved to enhance robustness when handling problems involving shock waves. Lastly, the scaling invariance of the Euler equations is exploited to facilitate the solution of high pressure ratio problems. Numerical experiments on air-air, air-helium, air-water, and air-R22 problems demonstrate the acceptable accuracy of the proposed method in simulating multi-medium flows.

items.title: On the foundations of anthropic reasoning: Implications for life across the universe
items.summary: With only one confirmed example, namely the Earth, the abundance of life across the universe remains deeply uncertain, and local evidence about Earth's particular circumstances can significantly shape our knowledge of life elsewhere. Such extrapolation is difficult not only because of this sample size of one, but also due to observer selection effects discussed under the Anthropic Principle. In this paper, we describe and apply a framework called Full Indexical Conditioning (FIC) for performing Bayesian inference in this situation. Inspired by, but distinct from, Full Non-Indexical Conditioning, FIC conditions on all evidence available to the reasoner while considering that this evidence could have been otherwise. We address the reference class problem associated with such reasoning, demonstrating that substantive conclusions are unaffected by the choice of reference class provided it is sufficiently large. We apply FIC to several problems in astrobiology, including the Doomsday argument, the early abiogenesis time, and our location around a G-type rather than M-type star, clarifying the foundations of these arguments. We conclude that the early abiogenesis time does not rule out pessimistic possibilities for life's abundance, and that while life around M stars may be uncommon, its temporal distribution could extend far into the future. Ultimately, FIC offers a clear conceptual framework, grounded in straightforward probability theory, for tackling problems involving anthropic selection effects.

items.title: First measurement of flux of the neutron background induced by accelerated neutrinos at the J-PARC facility
items.summary: This article reports the measurement of the neutron background flux accidentally induced by the neutrino beam at the J-PARC facility in Japan. In particular, neutrino-nucleus neutral-current quasi-elastic (NCQE) scattering events, $ν~(\barν)+\rm{N}\toν~(\barν)+\rm{N'}$, can be obscured by a massive background of neutron-nucleus scattering events. The neutrons are produced within the materials (such as sand and concrete) located between the beam dump and the experimental area where the detectors are placed. We measured the accidental neutron events at the J-PARC neutrino facility using BGO and liquid scintillation detectors, with a plastic scintillation detector serving as an active veto counter. Based on a neutrino-mode data set of $2.972 \times 10^{20}$ POT, we observed 88 neutron-induced recoil proton events within an electron-equivalent recoil energy range of 0.98-11.60 $\rm MeV_{ee}$, selected via pulse-shape discrimination in the liquid scintillation detector. Accounting for the detection efficiency and resolution, and through comparison with simulations, the neutron flux was determined to be$[1.45^{+0.22}_{-0.24}~\rm{(stat.)} \pm 0.55~\rm{(sys.)}] \times 10^{-7}~\rm{cm}^{-2} \rm{s}^{-1}\rm{POT}^{-1}$,assuming an exponential neutron energy spectrum. This result will contribute to the evaluation of neutron backgrounds for neutrino experiments at the J-PARC facility.

items.title: Frequency comb stability, bistability, and self-starting in normal dispersion microresonators
items.summary: Recent work has demonstrated that it is possible to generate frequency combs in normal dispersion microresonators by taking advantage of fabricated mode coupling that induces a mode split. In particular, photonic crystal resonators periodically modulate the microresonator's width, which geometrically creates mode coupling. In contrast to frequency combs generated by microresonators in the anomalous dispersion regime, which are typically generated using bright solitons, the frequency combs generated by normal dispersion regime microresonators are dark pulses that are commonly referred to as dark solitons or platicons. In this work, we examine the linear stability of platicons in the pump-detuning and pump-power parameter space as the mode split strength and cavity dispersion is varied. Our work reveals a broad region of stability for platicons. Our work also reveals the existence of fingers at high power at whose boundaries a sharp transition occurs and inside of which platicon solutions are bistable. Finally, we investigate the overlap of the region where platicons are stable with the region where continuous waves are modulationally unstable, and it is possible for a platicon to self-start. Simulations show that platicons consistently self-start inside this region.

items.title: Offset Dual Microcombs in a Single Microresonator: Kerr-Raman Interleaved Combs
items.summary: Integrated Kerr microcombs have emerged as a central platform for chip-scale nonlinear photonics. One of their most compelling applications is dual-comb technology, which enables fast, high-resolution, coherent optical spectroscopy, precision metrology, ranging, and ultrasensitive sensing by interfering two frequency combs with slightly different repetition rates. However, no effective strategy yet exists to synergistically excite multiple spatial mode families, manage mode competition and energy partitioning, and precisely engineer dispersion, leaving offset co-propagating dual-microcombs in a single resonator elusive. Here we demonstrate a new mechanism for offset dual microcombs formation via Kerr-Raman interleaving for the first time, by leveraging single Raman-active thin-film lithium niobate microrings. Two spatial mode families with high loaded Q factors up to 5 million are dispersion engineered to have nearly identical free-spectral-ranges but a designed relative frequency offset. Stimulated Raman scattering efficiently generates a Raman comb in one family alongside a Kerr comb in the other. The two combs interleave with a fractional offset to form a broadband, densely interleaved spectrum. Pumping the microring at only 320 mW yields Kerr-Raman interleaved dual combs both featuring nearly identical repetition rates around 102 GHz with a small difference of 675 MHz, a relatively flat envelope exceeding 29 nm and an intrinsic comb-line linewidth of 410 Hz. Our results establish offset dual-comb generation in a single microresonator, enabling compact dual-comb sources for chip-scale precision spectroscopy, Vernier-enhanced sensing, and advanced quantum photonics.

items.title: Missed Detections and False Alarms in a CNN Technosignature Detector on Breakthrough Listen Data
items.summary: Radio technosignature searches rely on machine learning detectors to shrink the candidate pool before a human looks at it. They are validated on held-out data from the training distribution, which excludes the cases where they are most likely to fail: a technosignature has unknown morphology, and terrestrial interference is unbounded in variety. I trained a standard competition detector once, froze it, and probed it with 15,000 injections across ten morphologies and five amplitudes, placed into real Green Bank backgrounds. Two directions were tested: genuine signals with morphologies other than a straight narrowband line, and interference resembling the training data. Recall did not follow the predicted ordering, and it fell as signals brightened, even for a needle of the kind the detector was trained on (from 0.590 to 0.090). One interference morphology reached a false positive rate of 0.627, comparable to the detector's own baseline recall of 0.5525 on genuine signals. Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) showed attention along the injected path in one missed family by a pre-specified test, and visually in a second. A pre-specified, time-averaged ON-OFF filter removed false alarms and genuine detections at the same rate. The detector reads only the ON panels. Since the only evidence distinguishing a genuine candidate from terrestrial interference lies in the discarded OFF panels, it cannot tell if a signal originates from the target star; it can only tell if it resembles the training data. This explains the false alarm directly; the missed signals reflect what the detector learned to recognise, which reading the OFF panels would not by itself change.

items.title: Chirality-resolved imaging of spin waves with a quantum spin
items.summary: Spin waves carry their propagation direction in the handedness of their circularly polarized stray field, a property inaccessible to scalar magnetometers. In the Damon-Eshbach surface wave of an in-plane magnetized film, the dipolar field above the film rotates with a handedness fixed by the direction of travel.
