First, we construct an equivalent norm on $\ell^2$ with no three-dimensional Hornich-Hlawka subspace. Second, we present a Nakano space that is not Hornich-Hlawka. Third, we show that the $α$-power generalization of the Hornich-Hlawka inequality fails to hold on nonzero normed spaces when $α\in (1, 2) \cup (2, \infty)$. This implies that on every nonzero inner product space, the $α$-power generalization of the Hornich-Hlawka inequality holds for all triples precisely when $α\in (0,1] \cup \{2\}$. For the remaining two problems, we establish reductions. We prove that $\ell^p(N)$ is Hornich-Hlawka for all $N \geq 3$ and $2 < p \leq \log 3 /(\log 3 - \log 2)$ if and only if it is Hornich-Hlawka at $N = 3$ and $p = \log 3 /(\log 3 - \log 2)$. Finally, for $p(\cdot): (0, 1) \to [1, 2]$ measurable and integers $k \geq 0$, we establish a Sobolev-Nakano equivalence: we prove that $W^{k,p(\cdot)}(0,1)$, equipped with the sum of the Luxemburg norms of its derivatives of orders $0, \ldots, k$, is Hornich-Hlawka if and only if $L^{p(\cdot)}(0,1)$ is Hornich-Hlawka.

items.title: Error analysis of a backward L2 method on graded meshes for linear and semilinear subdiffusion equations
items.summary: Time-fractional linear and semilinear parabolic equations with a Caputo time derivative of order $α\in(0,1)$ are considered. Their solutions exhibit an initial singularity of type $t^σ$ for any fixed $σ\in (0,1) \cup (1,2)$. A backward L2-type discrete fractional-derivative operator of order $3-α$ is considered on nonuniform temporal meshes. Sufficient conditions for inverse monotonicity of this operator areestablished. Hence, sharp pointwise-in-time error bounds are obtained on graded temporal meshes with arbitrary degree of grading. The theoretical findings are illustrated by numerical experiments.

items.title: Dg models for derived differential operators
items.summary: We show that for any algebra $R$ that is essentially of finite type over a field $k$, the derived functors of Smith-Van den Bergh admit a dg enhancement. In particular, for any $R$-module $M$ one can associate a dg algebra of differential operators $E_M$ whose cohomology is a nilpotent thickening of the (classical) ring of $k$-linear differential operators on $M$. We show that these dg algebras fit into a framework of Koszul duality due to Dwyer-Greenlees and specializes to a derived ring of differential operators studied by Yang when $M=R$ and $k=\mathbb{C}$. In particular, upon fixing a presentation $R=S/I$ with $S$ essentially smooth, we show a derived Kashiwara's equivalence, namely that whenever $\mathrm{supp}_S(M)=\mathrm{V}(I)$ then there is an equivalence of triangulated categories between the derived category of dg ${E}_M$-modules and the derived category of $D$-modules on $S$ that are set-theoretically supported on $I$. Finally, in the case of positive characteristic, we show that the dg algebra ${E}_M$ admits a description in terms of the Frobenius endomorphism akin to the classical description of differential operators, and the proof employs simplicial techniques to obtain a result of independent interest in commutative algebra.

items.title: Rapid mixing within a phase for Ising models
items.summary: We study Glauber dynamics for Ising measures conditioned to have a sufficiently large majority of $+1$ spins. Under a sparse spectral width condition on the interaction matrix, we derive a Poincaré inequality for the conditioned measures from a magnetization drift condition, and a modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality from a stronger, entropy weighted condition. As applications, we obtain approximate posterior sampling in total variation distance for $\mathbb{Z}_2$ synchronization at high enough signal-to-noise ratio using $O(n\log n)$ Glauber updates from a spectral initialization. For ferromagnetic Ising models on random $d$-regular graphs, we prove rapid phase ordering down to inverse temperatures of order $1/d$, extending the temperature range of Gheissari, Sly, and Sohn (2025). Finally, we extend these inequalities to unconditioned Ising measures under an inward drift condition outside the conditioned region. This yields $O(n\log n)$ mixing of Glauber dynamics for the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model at every fixed inverse temperature when the external field is sufficiently large.

items.title: Totally elliptic surface group representations
items.summary: A surface group representation into a Lie group is called totally elliptic if every simple closed curve on the surface is mapped to an elliptic element of the target group. In this note, we characterize all totally elliptic surface group representations into $\mathrm{PSL}_2\mathbb{R}$ and $\mathrm{PSL}_2\mathbb{C}$ by showing that they are either representations into a compact subgroup or Deroin--Tholozan representations.

items.title: Polytope Sampling at the Speed of Isoperimetry
items.summary: We give faster algorithms for sampling from the uniform distribution over a polytope. Our main result is an algorithm that, when applied to a polytope with $m$ constraints in $n$ dimensions, uses $m \cdot \mathrm{poly}\log(\frac m δ)$ iterations, each running in time $O(mn^{ω- 1})$, to return a sample within total variation distance $δ$ to the uniform distribution. When $m =O(n)$ and $δ= \mathrm{poly}(\frac 1 n)$, our runtime improves upon all prior works by an $Ω(n^{2/3})$ factor. Our sampler is based on the recent \emph{functional stochastic localization} framework of [GST26], and achieves an iteration count nearly matching the Poincaré constant of the uniform distribution with respect to the logarithmic barrier.

items.title: GRAFT-ATHENA: Self-Improving Agentic Teams for Autonomous Discovery and Evolutionary Numerical Algorithms
items.summary: Language-model agents plan, execute, and evaluate scientific workflows. However, the problem--method relationships guiding their choices remain implicit, so plausible outputs can violate the assumptions of the scientific problem. We introduce Graph Reduction to Adaptive Factored Trees (GRAFT), which makes this problem-to-method map explicit as an expandable probabilistic structure of admissible problems, methods, and dependencies. Because this structure follows scientific semantics, knowledge from documentation, papers, and domain experts can be encoded, while factorization keeps the structure tractable. Semantic fingerprints of encoded problems measure their similarity, so expertise and experience guide related problems. GRAFT-guided workflows exceeded published expert baselines in physics-informed learning, recovered blood-rheology trends, predicted Apollo Command Module hypersonic loading within 1.8\% of experiment, and established machine-checked error bounds for regularized brain-flow reconstruction and a spectral physics-informed architecture. The representation retains evaluated outcomes and incorporates new methods, allowing scientific knowledge and experience to accumulate.

items.title: Billiards and Hofer's Geometry
items.summary: We present a link between billiards in convex plane domains and Hofer's geometry, an area of symplectic topology. For smooth strictly convex billiard tables, we prove that the Hofer distance between the corresponding billiard ball maps admits an upper bound in terms of a simple geometric distance between the tables. We use this result to show that the billiard ball map of a convex polygon lies in the completion, with respect to Hofer's metric, of the group of smooth area-preserving maps of the annulus. Finally, we discuss related connections to dynamics and pose several open problems.

items.title: Finite Root Sums in Symmetrizable Kac-Moody Algebras
items.summary: Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a symmetrizable Kac-Moody algebra with root system $Φ$. A subset $S\subseteqΦ$ is \emph{closed} if $α,β\in S$ and $α+β\inΦ$ imply $α+β\in S$. For finite and affine Kac-Moody algebras, this closure property is known to extend from pairs to arbitrary finite sums that are roots. We prove that every closed subset of the root system of any symmetrizable Kac-Moody algebra is closed under arbitrary finite sums that are roots. The proof uses real-root strings and simultaneous separation of positive imaginary roots, together with an addition lemma for fundamental imaginary roots. As an application, we extend a necessary condition for wideness of regular subalgebras from finite and affine types to all symmetrizable Kac-Moody algebras: the symmetric closure of the roots associated to a wide regular subalgebra is the entire root system.

items.title: Herbrand Game Complexity
items.summary: The Student-Teacher game is an extension of Herbrand's theorem. In the game, Student and Teacher take turns giving values for existentially and universally quantified variables, and Student is allowed to backtrack to propose other values for existentially quantified variables. The game has become increasingly important for proving lower bounds on provability in theories of bounded arithmetic. In those applications, the game is played in an arithmetical theory; however, this paper studies the Student-Teacher game in the setting of pure first-order logic, so it is more closely related to Herbrand's theorem and the midsequent theorem. When played in pure first-order logic, a prenex formula $φ$ is logically valid if and only if there is a Student-Teacher game with a winning strategy for Student for establishing $φ$. We present a refined version of the Student-Teacher game in arbitrary first-order universal theories and include a proof of the validity of Student-Teacher games from the sequent calculus midsequent theorem in an appendix. The game is presented as a finite tree with vertices and edges labeled by terms, and with a total order on the nodes. The totally ordered tree represents the players' interaction. Our main results show that minimal trees in the Student-Teacher game can be arbitrarily complex. Specifically, for every totally ordered tree $T$, we construct a valid prenex formula $φ$ such that every winning Student-Teacher game for $φ$ contains $T$ as a substructure. Using formulas parameterized by numerals, we prove similar results for computable and partial computable sequences of totally ordered trees. It follows not only that there is no computable bound on the size of Herbrand disjunctions, which is a well-known fact, but also that there is no computable bound on their complexity.

items.title: Parametrised functor calculus: excision, spheres, and semiadditivity
items.summary: We lay down the foundations of a theory of parametrised functor calculus, generalising parts of the functor calculus of Goodwillie. We introduce the notion of excisable posets and develop a theory of excisive approximations in this context. As an application, we introduce two different excisable posets when parametrising over an atomic orbital category. By comparing the notions of excisiveness for these two posets, we relate the invertibility of certain spheres with Nardin's notion of parametrised semiadditivity, generalising Wirthmüller's classical result in equivariant homotopy theory for finite groups.

items.title: Operations on $G$-sets and the Dress map
items.summary: We study versions of binomial and multichoose coefficients for finite $G$-sets, extending a result of Siebeneicher from the 1970s concerning the duality between these operations. If the group $G$ comes from a finite Galois extension of fields, the Dress map provides a bridge from $G$-sets to quadratic forms over the base field. We show that this Dress map is compatible with binomial coefficients of finite $G$-sets and a particular operation on quadratic forms we define. This allows us to extend the definition of Brugallé and Wickelgren's quadratically enriched binomial coefficients to arbitrary Grothendieck--Witt classes. This allows for a new proof that quadratically enriched binomial coefficients depend only on the trace form of the inputted étale algebra, as well as an elegant reproof of a result of Chen and Wickelgren about binomial coefficients over finite fields.

items.title: Stability for a formally determined Lorentzian inverse problem
items.summary: We consider the inverse problem of recovering a potential $q$, depending on space and time, in the wave equation $(\Box_g+q)u=0$ on a Lorentzian manifold. We prove Lipschitz stability for a formally determined version of this problem under a \textit{null-cone foliation} assumption. As a consequence, we obtain uniqueness for the Lorentzian Calderón problem in a fixed conformal class. Our approach uses distorted spherical waves.

items.title: Robust Local Fréchet Regression: Nonasymptotic Theory and Minimax Optimality
items.summary: We develop robust local Fréchet regression for heavy-tailed responses in a general metric space and propose a distance-based median-of-means estimator. We derive nonasymptotic pointwise high-probability bounds separately under local second-order smoothness and local $1$-Wasserstein Hölder continuity, and show that the corresponding optimized rates match the classical pointwise rates for nonparametric regression. We also establish matching pointwise minimax lower bounds over embedded Gaussian regression subclasses. Remarkably, our results do not require an entropy condition on the response space. Simulation studies with positive-definite matrix-valued responses, together with a real-data application involving Wasserstein-valued responses, illustrate the robustness--efficiency tradeoff and practical performance of the proposed estimator.

items.title: The maximum number of Hamiltonian cycles in tournaments
items.summary: Let $C(n)$ denote the maximum number of directed Hamiltonian cycles in a tournament on $n$ vertices. We prove that, as $n\to\infty$, $$ C(n) = \left(\frac{\cosh 1}{\cos 1}\pm o(1)\right)\frac{(n-1)!}{2^n}. $$ The bound is asymptotically attained by the regular tournament with vertices $\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z$ where $(i,j)$ is a directed edge if $j - i \pmod n< n/2$. This answers a question of Alon and proves a conjecture of Wormald. Among the other implications of these results is asymptotically determining the maximum number of Hamiltonian paths in a tournament on $n$ vertices. We provide our own exposition of these proofs, which were originally found by GPT-5.6.

items.title: Asymptotic stability of a Bloch skyrmion for the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation
items.summary: We prove the asymptotic stability of isolated skyrmions under the flow of the two-dimensional Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation. We consider a micromagnetic energy functional involving the exchange energy, the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction, and the Zeeman interaction. We are interested in the stability of chiral Bloch skyrmions, which are local minimizers of this energy. We prove that data in H2 which are near in the skyrmion in a slighlty stronger than H1 sense, converge with exponential rate, in H2, to the skyrmion, up to a change of gauge.

items.title: Spectral networks, finite webs, and the $T_3$ cubic differential
items.summary: We describe spectral networks for cubic differentials on $\mathbf{P}^1$ with exactly three poles all of order two, following observations of Hollands-Neitzke. To do so, we give a precise definition and establish some basic properties of a class of finite webs (corresponding to BPS states in physics) in the cubic differential setting, including their non-vanishing central charge. Turning to the example, we prove that at rational angles the network is totally degenerate; the number of walls and Stokes regions is explicitly computed and depends on an arithmetic criterion. At all other angles, the spectral network is dense in the surface and contains no finite webs, as expected. Physically, this example corresponds to a fundamental building block for a large class of four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=2$ QFTs with gauge group $\mathrm{SU}(3)$.

items.title: Exact Tail Laws for Nonlinear SGD with Infinite-Variance Gradients
items.summary: With infinite-variance gradient noise, SGD can have infinite expected excess objective even when most iterates are close to the optimum. We characterize its accuracy through exact first-order tail probabilities for the last iterate of nonlinear, constant-stepsize SGD. For regularly varying innovations of index $t\in(1,2)$, the leading measure transports one large gradient shock through the local Hessian flow. This is the same measure that governs the central stable Ornstein--Uhlenbeck limit; we prove its relative accuracy at shrinking tolerances above the central scale, with state-dependent noise and a growing observation horizon. The admissible window is nonempty for every available gradient moment $p>1$. The main technical step is a moment bound at the central fluctuation scale and a lower-moment control of the nonlinear error. The result yields explicit projection and excess-objective tails, extreme quantiles, and a factor $b^{1-t}$ for fixed batch size $b$. For affine population gradients, a sharper comparison gives the same law at fixed tolerances, including random sample Hessians. Coupled simulations in dimensions one to one hundred examine relative calibration, objective quantiles, batch effects, and the error due to random curvature.

items.title: From Alpha to Execution: Trading Horizons, Regimes, and Schedules under Concave Impact and Hurst Scaling
items.summary: Classical execution models assume linear impact, diffusive prices, and an exogenous horizon. We study execution under concave power-law impact and Hurst-scaled price fluctuations, and make two contributions. First, we choose the execution horizon by maximizing the Sharpe ratio of the trade's realized P&L. Price moves during the execution window are part of that P&L, so executing more slowly reduces its variance, and because impact is concave it can also lower cost per share. Urgency comes only from alpha realized while the order is being worked. The problem is governed by the signs of two quantities: (i) the duration elasticity of impact $a$, which under a structural prior equals the impact-persistence gap $β- H$ and can take either sign; and (ii) the net urgency $ν$, the rate of alpha realization net of exposure relief. When $ν$ keeps its sign over the window, an interior optimum exists, to leading order in $T/t_f$, only when both are positive; otherwise the order should be worked at the fastest or slowest admissible pace. In the interior regime the first-order condition involves no impact coefficient, order size or volume, and the objective is flat: for a large-cap example, the window within 1% of maximal Sharpe spans more than an order of magnitude. Second, given the window, we derive the schedule shape by convex programming under an envelope cost. For any increasing per-share cost of delay $w(t)$, the KKT solution is $φ\propto (λ- w(t))_+^{1/β}$. For a Hurst-scaled envelope $w \propto t^H$, the normalized schedule depends only on $(β, H)$, has a closed form via the incomplete beta function, is front-loaded, and tapers smoothly to zero, saving 10-17% of envelope cost relative to a constant-rate (TWAP) schedule of equal duration. Whether it uses the whole window depends on a single dimensionless robustness level, for which we give a calibration.

items.title: The distribution of $αp$ modulo one in real quadratic function fields
items.summary: Matomäki proved that if $α\in\R$ is irrational, then there are infinitely many primes $p$ such that $|α-a/p|\le p^{-4/3+\varepsilon}$ for a suitable integer $a$. In \cite{BaMo}, Baier and the author established analogues of this result for $\F_q(T)$ and its imaginary quadratic extensions. In this paper, we extend it to all real quadratic extensions of $\F_q(T)$.

items.title: Non-radial solutions for the quasi-linear Hénon type $N$-Laplacian Liouville equation
items.summary: In this paper, we investigate the following quasi-linear weighted $N$-Laplacian Liouville equation \begin{equation*}\label{0} -Δ_N u=|x|^{Nα}e^{u}, \qquad x\in \R^N, \end{equation*} where $N \geq 2$. For $\al>0$, by carefully studying the linearized problem and applying the approximation method and bifurcation theory, we prove that, when the parameter $α$ equals to the critical values $α(k):=\frac{\sqrt{k(N-1)(k+N-2)}}{N-1}-1$ for $k \geq 2$, there exist non-radial solutions $u$ (bifurcating from $U_{α(k)}$) to the above quasi-linear Hénon type Liouville equation such that $u\sim \ln|x|$, $|\nabla u|= O(|x|^{-1})$ at $\infty$ and $\int_{\R^N}|x|^{Nα}e^{u}\md x=N\left(\frac{N^2}{N-1}\right)^{N-1}(α+1)^{N-1}ω_N$. One should note that, $α(k)=k-1$ for $k\geq2$ when $N=2$. Our results successfully extend the existence result of J. Prajapat and G. Tarantello in \cite{PT} concerning the $2$-dimension and Laplacian case (i.e., $N=2$) to the more general $N$-dimension and $N$-Laplacian cases ($N\geq 2$), and extend the results of F. Gladiali, M. Grossi, and S. L. N. Neves in \cite{GGN} and the authors in \cite{DDGL} from $1<p<N$ to the much more complicated limiting case $p=N$. We introduced some new ideas and overcame a series of crucial difficulties, including the nonlinearity nature of the $N$-Laplacian $Δ_N$, the lack of Green integral representation formula and critical weighted Sobolev embedding inequality, the absence of Kelvin type transforms for linearized/difference equations, the invariance of the total mass under scalings of $u$, and the signs-changing and divergence (to $-\infty$) at $\infty$ of the solutions, which makes the suitable choices of the approximate problems, the (normalized) approximate function sequences and the working space to be quite difficult.

items.title: Equivariant localizing motives and multiplicative norms on algebraic K-theory
items.summary: We construct multiplicative norms on equivariant nonconnective algebraic $K$-theory for finite groups $G$. We also construct a genuine equivariant version of THH equipped with a Dennis trace map from K-theory compatible with the multiplicative norms. To do so, we follow the general strategy of Blumberg-Gepner-Tabuada in the nonequivariant case by generalizing their category of localizing motives to the genuine equivariant context, building upon the theory of perfect $G$-stable categories of the first-named author. Crucially, we proceed using the recent perspective on noncommutative motives by the second-named author with Sosnilo and Winges which allows us to deal with non-exact functors on this category of motives. Together with an isotropy separation argument for equivariant cubes, we prove our main theorem that norms of stable categories preserve equivariant motivic equivalences. As an immediate consequence, we obtain a unique equivariant multiplicative refinement of nonconnective algebraic $K$-theory. From these constructions and results, we draw several applications, namely: (1) that the endofunctor of (equivariant) tensor powers on ordinary perfect stable categories preserve motivic equivalences; (2) that the multiplicative norms also preserve the additive motivic equivalences, thus yielding a motivic refinement of a result of Elmanto-Haugseng and Cnossen-Haugseng-Lenz-Linskens that connective algebraic K-theory admits multiplicative norms; (3) we construct a genuine equivariant version of topological Hochschild homology equipped with a Dennis trace map that is compatible with multiplicative norms; and (4) we prove that every genuine $G$-spectrum is the K-theory of a perfect $G$-stable category.

items.title: Plancherel Decompositions and Distinctions for $\mathrm{Sp}_{2n}\backslash \mathrm{Gl}_{2n+1}$ and $P(\mathrm{Sp}_{2n})\backslash \mathrm{Gl}_{2n}$
items.summary: Let $F$ be a non-Archimedean local field of characteristic zero. We determine the Plancherel decompositions of $\mathrm{Sp}_{2n}(F)\backslash\mathrm{GL}_{2n+1}(F)$ and $P(\mathrm{Sp}_{2n})(F)\backslash\mathrm{GL}_{2n}(F)$, where $P(\mathrm{Sp}_{2n})$ denotes the mirabolic subgroup of $\mathrm{Sp}_{2n}$, and study smooth distinction for both spaces. We carry out the local unfolding procedure of arXiv:1203.0039, Section 9.5, constructing unitary isomorphisms with degenerate Whittaker models by successive Fourier transforms. The isomorphism for the even model is already stated there in Example 9.5.17. The resulting Plancherel formulas are direct integrals of normalized parabolic inductions from the tempered duals of $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)\times\mathrm{GL}_{n+1}(F)$ and $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)\times\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$, respectively, with product Whittaker-Plancherel measures. In the odd case, the parameter map agrees with the prediction of arXiv:2409.04677. Using closed parabolic orbits and local Rankin-Selberg integrals, we prove that all representations induced from these tempered data are distinguished for the corresponding model. We also prove that essentially square-integrable representations are not distinguished for the odd model, and that supercuspidal representations are not distinguished for the even model. For the even model with $n=1,2$, we construct distinguished square-integrable representations outside the Plancherel support. Thus, the smooth tempered distinguished spectrum can be strictly larger than the corresponding $L^2$-spectrum. For $\mathrm{GL}_5(F)$, however, we prove that an irreducible tempered representation is $\mathrm{Sp}_4(F)$-distinguished if and only if it is induced from tempered representations of $\mathrm{GL}_2(F)$ and $\mathrm{GL}_3(F)$.

items.title: Order relations for the near geometric and near spectral geometric curves
Diffusion-Based Stochastic Operator Networks for Uncertainty Quantification in Stochastic Partial Differential Equations
items.summary: We introduce a novel framework for uncertainty quantification of solution operators associated with stochastic partial differential equations (SPDEs). Although SPDEs play a central role in modeling complex physical systems under uncertainty, their practical use typically requires specifying the magnitude and structure of model uncertainties that are often unknown and difficult to infer from noisy measurements. To address this challenge, we develop a stochastic operator-learning framework that learns directly from noisy data and outputs both a mean solution field and a quantification of uncertainty. The proposed method, namely the Stochastic Operator Network (SON), is constructed by combining the structure of the Deep Operator Network (DeepONet) with Stochastic Neural Networks (SNNs) to model stochasticity and enable probabilistic prediction. The training procedure is carried out by minimizing a Hamiltonian-type loss and optimizing the resulting objective using the Stochastic Maximum Principle. Numerical experiments on benchmark SPDEs under multiple uncertainty sources demonstrate the accuracy and robustness of the proposed method in capturing solution structure and quantifying predictive uncertainty.

items.title: Two-bridge knot epimorphisms and intersections in the character variety
items.summary: We study the SL(2,C) character varieties of hyperbolic two-bridge knot groups admitting epimorphisms onto the trefoil knot group. Ohtsuki, Riley, and Sakuma give a systematic construction of an infinite family of such knots. The character varieties of these knot groups contain a component of irreducible representations arising from the epimorphism, which is distinct from the canonical component. We prove that every affine point of intersection between this component and any other component is algebraic non-integral, and therefore detects an essential surface in the knot complement. We also determine the boundary slope of each detected surface explicitly in terms of the continued fraction expansion of the two-bridge knot.

items.title: Confluence relations, Hoffman basis over \mathbb{Z}_{(2)}, and the Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture
items.summary: We express every admissible word as a $\mathbb{Z}_{(2)}$-linear combination of Hoffman words and explicit confluence relations. This implies that every multiple zeta value is a linear combination of elements of the Hoffman basis with coefficients having odd denominators, as conjectured by Hirose and Sato. Combined with Brown's theorem and Furusho's characterization of the Grothendieck--Teichmüller group $\mathrm{GRT}$ by confluence relations, our result identifies the de Rham motivic Galois group of mixed Tate motives over $\mathbb{Z}$ with $\mathrm{GRT}$ and gives an alternative proof of the Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture, for which a proof was previously presented in the OpenAI Math Release.

items.title: Dissipative solutions for fibred Wasserstein gradient flows of Cahn-Hilliard-type energies
items.summary: We study fourth-order evolution equations with a fibred Wasserstein gradient-flow structure, describing spatial transport of finitely many or a continuum of types. The driving Cahn-Hilliard-like energy combines a diagonal gradient contribution with nonlinear interactions between types. We prove subsequential convergence of the fibred Jordan-Kinderlehrer-Otto scheme to solutions satisfying an energy-dissipation inequality. For general type distributions, the absence of compactness in the type variable is addressed through defect-based solution concepts. On $\mathbb R^d, d\le 3$, we construct dissipative solutions satisfying an additional entropy-dissipation inequality. On smooth bounded domains in any space dimension, a coercivity estimate for the metric slope allows us to construct energy-dissipating solutions without relying on flow interchange, thereby covering non-convex domains endowed with the intrinsic length distance. In both cases, a variational comparison of the piecewise constant and De Giorgi interpolants yields a common limiting energy and strong convergence of the difference to zero without requiring strong compactness. For finitely many types, the defects vanish and the construction yields weak solutions. We further establish weak-strong uniqueness of dissipative solutions in every space dimension and of energy-dissipating solutions in dimensions $d\le5$. Combined with the respective existence results, this yields strong convergence of the variational approximations whenever a sufficiently regular, strictly positive solution exists.

items.title: A polynomial time algorithm for almost bounded denumerant
items.summary: Sylvester's denumerant $d(t; \boldsymbol{A})$ counts the number of nonnegative integer solutions to $\sum_{i=1}^{N} a_i x_i = t$, where $\boldsymbol{A} = (a_1, \dots, a_N)$ is a sequence of positive integers with $\gcd(\boldsymbol{A}) = 1$. In 2025, Xin and Zhang gave a polynomial time algorithm in $N$ for computing $d(t; \boldsymbol{A})$ when the entries of $\boldsymbol{A}$ are bounded by a constant. In this paper, we extend this algorithm by incorporating Barvinok's algorithm, enabling it to handle the case where a fixed number of entries of $\boldsymbol{A}$ are allowed to be unbounded.

items.title: An Alternative Framework for Irreducibility and Primitivity of Nonnegative Tensors
items.summary: Motivated by some recent studies on higher order Markov chains and well-known characterizations for irreducibility and primitivity of nonnegative matrices, we propose in this paper an alternative framework for irreducibility and primitivity of nonnegative tensors, giving rise to two new notions: s-irreducibility and s-primitivity. Our framework includes the relevant results on nonnegative matrices as its special cases, yet it expands existing results regarding irreducibility and primitivity of nonnegative tensors. In addition to its tensor theoretic significance, such a framework has important implications for applied problems such as higher order Markov chains.

items.title: Involutions on $(\infty,n)$-categories of bordisms and reflection TQFTs
items.summary: We construct a strict involution, that is, a strict $\mathbb{Z}/2$-action, on the $(\infty,n)$-category $\mathbf{Bord}_n(H_n)$ of bordisms with $H_n$-structure, where $H_n$ is the symmetry type of a TQFT, using the complete $n$-fold Segal space model. Using this involution, we develop an appropriate definition of reflection TQFTs in this setting and show that they correspond to certain homotopy fixed point spaces. Finally, we apply the machinery to the example of super algebras, where, depending on the symmetry type, the homotopy fixed point data corresponds to either a stellar structure or a real structure on the algebra that the reflection theory assigns to the point.

items.title: Finite Cyclic Fundamental Groups and Exotic Universal Covers from the Cartwright--Steger Surface
items.summary: We use a particular nodal curve on the Cartwright-Steger surface to construct minimal symplectic four-manifolds with arbitrary nontrivial finite cyclic fundamental group and fixed topological invariants $(e,σ,χ_h,c_1^2)=(43,1,11,89)$. Using these symplectic four-manifolds as building blocks, we construct a symplectic 4-manifold that is homeomorphic to $(22m-1)\mathbb{CP}^2\#(21m-1)\overline{\mathbb{CP}}^{\,2}$ for any integer $m\geq 2$.

items.title: The Restricted Inverse Optimal Value Problem on Shortest Path under $l_\infty$ Norm on Trees
items.summary: We study the restricted inverse optimal value problem on shortest paths under the weighted $l_\infty$ norm on trees (RIOVSPT$_\infty$): adjust edge weights at minimum worst-link cost so that the shortest root--leaf path is lower-bounded by a given value $D$, a restriction on a prescribed path $P_0$. Unlike the $l_1$ version minimizing total adjustment cost, the $l_\infty$ objective controls the worst link, the criterion relevant in bandwidth pricing. We characterize feasibility through the minimum cost shortest path interdiction problem (MCSPIT$_\infty$), whose optimal solution $\hat w$ splits the instance at the first edge of $P_0$ into two independent subproblems. Relative to $\hat w$, three cases arise. The first two admit closed-form optimal solutions. The third reduces to a parametric subproblem SPIT$^0_\infty(M)$: minimize the length of $P_0$ on the gate subtree under the budget $C(\hat w)+M$ with all other root--leaf paths kept at least $D$. It is solved exactly by an iterative greedy procedure. On its value function $V(M)$, the predicate $V(M)\leq D$ is equivalent to the nonnegativity of truncated-bound margins, which are monotone, continuous and piecewise affine; the smallest such $M$ gives the optimal value, located by binary search over the edge-bound breakpoints with an exact affine threshold evaluation. The same margin test on the full tree gives a uniform algorithm for all cases. Both algorithms run in $O(n\log n)$ time. Experiments on synthetic trees agree with a linear programming baseline and illustrate the two algorithms' distinct runtime profiles.

items.title: A Poincaré-Lefschetz Theorem for Cellular Cosheaves and an Application to the Tropical Homology of Orbifold Toric Varieties
items.summary: We begin by presenting a version of the Poincaré-Lefschetz theorem for certain cellular cosheaves on a particular subdivision of a CW-complex K. To that end we construct a cellular sheaf on K whose cohomology with compact support is isomorphic to the homology of the initial cosheaf. Thereafter we use the first result to generalise the tropical version of the Lefschetz Hyperplane Section Theorem to some singular tropical toric varieties and singular tropical hypersurfaces.

items.title: The Statistical Fairness-Accuracy Frontier
items.summary: We study fairness-accuracy tradeoffs when a single predictive model must serve multiple demographic groups. A useful tool for understanding this tradeoff is the fairness-accuracy (FA) Pareto frontier, which characterizes the set of models that cannot be improved in either fairness or accuracy without worsening the other. While characterizing the FA frontier requires full knowledge of the data distribution, we focus on the finite-sample regime, quantifying how well a designer can approximate any point on the frontier from limited data and bounding the worst-case gap. In particular, we derive worst-case-optimal estimators that depend on the designer's knowledge of the covariate distribution. For each estimator, we characterize how finite-sample effects asymmetrically impact each group's welfare and identify optimal sample allocation strategies. Finally, we provide uniform finite-sample bounds along the entire FA frontier, quantifying finite-sample deviations across alternative fairness-accuracy tradeoffs.

items.title: A Multidimensional Birkhoff Theorem for some $C^0$ Lagrangians
items.summary: We prove a multidimensional Birkhoff theorem for a new class of "$C^0$ Lagrangian subsets" in cotangent bundles, obtained as Hausdorff limits of compact exact Lagrangian submanifolds with control on their Liouville primitives. If the successive images of such a subset $L$ under the flow of a Tonelli Hamiltonian admit convergent subsequences in both positive and negative time, then $L$ and all its images are Lipschitz graphs over the base. This extends Birkhoff's celebrated theorem for twist maps of the annulus and its known higher-dimensional generalizations, and provides a first version of such results for merely continuous objects. The proof combines Floer-theoretic graph selectors, variational solutions of the Hamilton-Jacobi equation, and weak KAM theory. We also investigate the rigidity and uniqueness of limiting primitives for this new class of singular Lagrangian subsets, which may be of independent interest in $C^0$ symplectic topology.

items.title: Universality of Annealed Complexity in the Spherical Pure $p$-Spin Model
items.summary: In an influential work, Auffinger, Ben Arous, and Černý (2013) investigated the limiting annealed complexity in the spherical pure $p$-spin model associated to the Gaussian disorder. Their results, in particular, included an explicit expression for the total number of critical points of the Hamiltonian below any given energy level. In this paper, we consider the same anneal complexity associated to a disorder interpolating between an arbitrary random variable and its Gaussian counterpart. Assuming strict subgaussianity of the former, our result shows that the annealed complexity shares the same limit as in the Gaussian case.

items.title: Higher-order sum rules for zeros of the planar Gaussian entire function
items.summary: We establish marginal sum rules for the truncated correlation functions of zeros of the planar Gaussian entire function (GEF). For each fixed integer $k\ge2$, the integral in one coordinate converges absolutely and equals $-(k-1)$ times the truncated correlation of order $k-1$. This answers the marginal-identity question posed by Krishnapur and Yogeshwaran for the planar GEF. We also prove a criterion for simple point processes under local moment and absolute integrability assumptions. Suppose there is a sequence of compactly supported cutoffs between zero and one that are eventually equal to one on each compact set. If the variances of their linear statistics tend to zero, the marginal identities hold almost everywhere. Strong clustering and variance bounds for smooth linear statistics verify these assumptions for GEF zeros. The proof uses mixed cumulants and the partition formula relating ordinary and factorial cumulants.

items.title: Recursive Operator Localization and Spectral Gap Descent via the Geometry of Local Spectral Expansion
items.summary: We introduce Recursive Operator Localization (ROL), a framework for constructing hierarchies of local energy problems linked by linear maps between Hilbert spaces. To address spectral-gap problems, including those arising in quantum systems, we study a realization of ROL by nested subspaces indexed by a weighted simplicial complex. Using spectral gaps of auxiliary classical random walks on links, we propagate geometric estimates upward and use them to turn local spectral gaps at the bottom of the hierarchy into a spectral-gap bound for the global operator. For weighted scalar-valued functions on facets, the ROL decomposition becomes the law of total variance, recovering classical spectral-gap bounds from local link expansion (Alev and Lau, STOC 2020). Moreover, for positive binary spin distributions, conditional influence describes the overlap of the corresponding subspaces, yielding known heat-bath gap bounds from spectral independence (Anari, Liu, and Oveis Gharan, FOCS 2020). The framework also offers a route toward quantum Gibbs sampling, with applications requiring model-specific geometric estimates and energy comparisons.

items.title: On one relaxation of the bounded-length-distortion condition in the context of metric measure spaces
items.summary: We reformulate the bounded-length-distortion condition for maps between metric spaces in a certain relaxed form that requires the presence of a reference measure on the source space, which makes the new approach more natural from the perspective of maps from metric measure spaces to metric spaces. Within this framework, we establish some mapping results in an entirely singular setting of the following general structure: a metric measure space of finite Hausdorff dimension admits a map with the relaxed bounded-length-distortion condition into a finite-dimensional normed space.

items.title: Toward Spectral Deferred Correction Methods for Stochastic Differential Equations
items.summary: The numerical solution of stochastic differential equations is computationally very demanding. Often it is of interest to evaluate certain moments, e.g., the expectation, by Monte Carlo sampling, thus requiring the computation of numerous realizations. The discretization error of the numerical scheme induces bias in the computed Monte Carlo estimator. As popular numerical schemes, like Euler-Maruyama or Milstein, are low-order, even reasonably coarse error bounds for the simulation are costly to achieve. While the evaluation of moments requires only weak convergence, in other applications like parameter estimation, strong convergence is important, but higher-order is typically harder to obtain in the strong than in the weak sense. In this paper we develop an efficient method with the potential of achieving higher strong and weak convergence order. It is based on the smooth approximation of Brownian bridges combined with spectral deferred correction methods well known for the numerical solution of ordinary differential equations. We discuss convergence, and present numerical results.

items.title: Cuspidal Class Number Formulae for Intermediate Modular Curves of Prime Level
items.summary: Let $X$ be a modular curve lying between $X_{0}(p)$ and $X_{1}(p)$, where $p \ge 13$ is prime. The cuspidal group of $X$ is the subgroup of its Jacobian generated by the equivalence classes of differences of cusps. In this paper, we give explicit formulae for the order of the cuspidal group, and two subgroups of it defined over the rationals.

items.title: Local topological zeta functions of generic symmetric and catalecticant determinantal varieties
items.summary: We give explicit formulas for the local topological zeta functions at the origin of generic symmetric determinantal varieties and catalecticant determinantal varieties associated with generic Hankel matrices. In the symmetric determinant hypersurface case, the formula simplifies to a closed product expression and implies the Strong Monodromy Conjecture. For catalecticant determinantal varieties, we establish a simultaneous local reduction of the determinantal ideals and obtain a closed product formula for their local topological zeta functions. Together with the known Bernstein-Sato polynomial of the Hankel determinant, this also implies the Strong Monodromy Conjecture in the square catalecticant determinant case. The method used in this paper also gives short proofs of Chen-Zuo/Docamposs formula in the generic determinantal case and Chen-Shi-Xu-Zuo's formula in the skew-symmetric case.

items.title: The semiring of spectral duality skeletons: cancellation, characters and factorization
items.summary: Weighted dual skeletons are the combinatorial core of spectral duality structures. Their isomorphism classes, under Cartesian product and disjoint union, form a semiring graded by the degree. We identify it completely: a class is determined by its degree, a symmetric element of the group semiring N_0[R] and its number of fixed points. Equivalently, skeletons of a given degree are finite C_2-sets over the C_2-monoid (R,+), these data are their marks, and the semiring is an infinite-monoid analogue of a crossed Burnside semiring. The multiplicative monoid is not cancellative, the only obstruction being that multiplication by a skeleton without fixed points forgets the fixed points; accordingly, the Grothendieck ring has explicit zero divisors. A continuous family of semiring characters, with the degree and the number of fixed points, is a complete invariant, and for commensurable ratios the multiplicative Grothendieck group is described by Pólya's theorem. The main subject is factorization. The reduced monoid is atomic with bounded lengths, but factorization is not unique, the elasticity is infinite, and even the divisor-closed submonoid with one fixed point is not half-factorial. Without fixed points, every reducible skeleton splits off a single orbit, which gives a criterion by centers, exactly when the number of orbits is 8, 16, a prime or twice a prime. Irreducibility is generic in almost every type. Progression skeletons factor according to mixed-radix number systems, with all factorizations of equal length. Finally, orbit counting gives the dimension of the separatrix and the response rank of products.

items.title: Asymptotic gradient regularity for degenerate or singular fully nonlinear parabolic equations
items.summary: This is a continuation of our recent work~\cite{WZJ26} on asymptotic gradient regularity for nonlinear parabolic equations. In this paper, we consider bounded viscosity solutions of the degenerate or singular fully nonlinear parabolic equation \begin{equation*} u_t-|Du|^γF(D^2u)=f \quad \text{in } Q_1, \end{equation*} where $ γ>-1 $, $ F $ is uniformly $ (λ, Λ)$-elliptic with $0<λ\leqΛ$, $F(0)=0$, and $f\in C^0(Q_1)\cap L^\infty(Q_1)$. Given any prescribed $α\in(0,1)$, we prove that there exists $ \varepsilon=\varepsilon(n,α)>0 $ such that \[ |γ|+\left(\fracΛλ-1\right) \leq \varepsilon \quad \Longrightarrow \quad u \in C_{\mathrm{loc}}^{1+α,\frac{1+α}{2}}(Q_1). \] In particular, the spatial gradient Hölder exponent can be chosen arbitrarily close to $1$ as $ (γ, \fracΛλ) \to (0,1) $. This provides a fully nonlinear counterpart to the asymptotic gradient regularity result established in~\cite{WZJ26}.

items.title: Fourier dimension for exactly approximable matrices
items.summary: We determine the Fourier dimension of exactly approximation set for all dimensions. More precisely, let $m,n\ge1$, $\boldsymbolθ\in\mathbb R^m$, and $ψ:\mathbb N\to \mathbb R^+$ be a non-increasing approximate function. Denote by $\textrm{Exact}_{m,n}(ψ,\boldsymbolθ)$ the set of $m\times n$ matrices which are inhomogeneously $ψ$-approximable with shift $\boldsymbolθ$, but not $cψ$-approximable for any fixed $0<c<1$. We prove that $$\dim_{\text{F}} \textrm{Exact}_{m,n}(ψ,\boldsymbolθ)=\frac{2n}{1+τ_ψ},\ \text{whenever }τ_ψ>\frac{n}{m},$$ where $τ_ψ$ is the lower order of $ψ$ at infinity.

items.title: Sharp $L^6$ Fourier moments and (3,$δ$)-energy estimates for fractal measures on the truncated cone in $\R^3$
items.summary: For a $δ$-separated $(δ,d)$-Katz--Tao set $P$ on the truncated cone in $\R^3$, $1<d\le 2$, we prove the sharp energy bound \[ \E_{3,δ}(P)\lesssim_{\varepsilon} δ^{-\varepsilon} \max\{δ^{-(3d+2)},δ^{-(5d-1)}\}. \] The proof applies the Fu--Ren incidence theorem to triples with a fixed sum. As a corollary we also deduce a sharp $L^6$ moment estimate for the Fourier transform of Frostman measures supported on the cone.

items.title: Non-linear Dirichlet Functionals: Markovianity, Locality, Invariance
items.summary: We present in a unified setting the foundations for a theory of non-linear Dirichlet functionals on Hilbert spaces. We prove known and new equivalences between non-linear semigroups, non-linear resolvents, non-linear generators, and their energy functionals, including a complete characterization of Markovianity. We introduce and characterize strong notions of invariance for general lower semicontinuous convex functionals, and notions of locality and strong locality for non-linear Dirichlet functionals. Contrary to many partial results in the literature, these characterizations are complete under minimal natural assumptions, and reduce to the classical ones in the bilinear case. Our definitions and proofs simplify and clarify the analogous facts in the linear theory, showing in particular that (the equality defining) locality is a saturation of (the inequality defining) Markovianity.

items.title: The price of a weak shadow variable: inference under nonignorable missingness as relevance vanishes
items.summary: When an outcome is missing not at random, identification is commonly restored by a shadow variable: a covariate that predicts the outcome but is excluded from the response mechanism. The literature treats the first requirement, relevance, as a yes-or-no condition. We make it continuous, parametrizing it by a scalar that scales the shadow variable's entire contribution to the moment conditions, and ask what inference costs as that scalar vanishes. One functional of the inverse weight governs the answer. We characterize it exactly, show that it fixes the effective sample size, and use it to sharpen the rates of the estimator that avoids the weight. The characterization is concrete. Whether the functional saturates or diverges turns not on boundedness of the outcome but on whether the tilting variable has an atom at its essential supremum: a binary outcome saturates, a uniform one does not. It also bounds how far a scanned set reaches, and that reach grows only as the square root of the logarithm of the sample size, so a thousandfold increase buys one unit of tilt while the set to be scanned widens. A reanalyzed credit-scoring study shows the cost: a characteristic an optimizing selector uses cannot satisfy exclusion.

items.title: On the possibilities and limitations of LLM-based multi-agent systems for multi-criteria decision-making in healthcare operations management
items.summary: Multi-criteria models for healthcare operations need weights that express how stakeholders trade off patient waiting time, provider workload, and operating cost, but these weights are difficult to quantify. Teams of large language model (LLM) agents, each prompted to represent a stakeholder, have been used to supply them. We propose a framework for assessing the reliability of LLM-generated preferences as inputs to multi-objective optimization and quantifying how their uncertainty affects decisions. We study explicit preferences by asking agents to rate the importance of the criteria in an outpatient appointment scheduling problem, and implicit preferences by inferring trade-offs from the agents' pairwise choices between emergency department configurations. The computational experiments show that the explicit preferences respond to the clinic's operating conditions and differ across roles, but deliberation among the agents can erase these differences, whereas simple averaging preserves them. The pairwise choices used to reveal the agents' implicit preferences depend largely on which option is presented first, and we find limited evidence that a statistical model using contextual information alongside presentation order predicts the agents' choices on new comparison pairs better than a model using presentation order alone. We then formulate robust weighted-sum optimization models to account for preference uncertainty. In most cases, these models select different schedules or configurations from those obtained using average preference weights. These results indicate that LLM-generated preferences need an audit of this kind before they are used as optimization weights in healthcare decision support.

items.title: Homology and carrier faces of simplicial distributions
items.summary: We study the facial structure of simplicial distribution polytopes using topological and algebraic methods. In the theory of simplicial distributions, measurement and event spaces are represented by simplicial sets, and compatible probability assignments form a convex polytope. Given a simplicial distribution, it is known that its supports determine its carrier face. Moreover, the supports form a simplicial subset of the event space. This naturally raises the question of how the topology of this simplicial subset is related to the corresponding carrier face. Our main objective is to relate the dimension of the carrier face to the topology and combinatorial structure of the space of supports. For $n$-facet-paired measurement spaces, we first express the carrier dimension in terms of the nullity of an associated facet matrix. When the measurement space is additionally orientable, we show that the carrier dimension is determined by the top-dimensional homology of the space of supports, yielding, in particular, a homological criterion for detecting vertices. We then develop an algebraic reduction based on a strong connectivity relation on the generating simplices of the space of supports. This construction yields a reduced facet matrix, indexed by the strongly connected components, whose null space is isomorphic to that of the original facet matrix. As a consequence, both the carrier dimension and extremality can be determined from the topology of the support and the way its strongly connected components are glued together.

items.title: Random Sampling of Almost Periodic Stochastic Processes
items.summary: We study the effect of random sampling on stochastic processes whose finite-dimensional distributions are Bohr almost periodic under time shifts. The sampling times are generated independently by a two-sided random walk with positive increments or by a two-sided subordinator. Under a non-degeneracy condition we show that the shifted finite-dimensional distributions of the sampled process converge to those of a strictly stationary process. Consequently, if the sampled process is itself almost periodic in distribution, then it must already be strictly stationary. We further prove an $L^2$-law of large numbers for sampled averages under covariance decay and a uniform second-moment bound, and identify its limit with the mean of the stationary limit process. Finally, for $m$-dependent, $L^2$-uniformly integrable almost periodic processes, we establish a central limit theorem for the centered sampled sums, whose asymptotic variance is given by the autocovariance series of the stationary limit.

items.title: Class field theory for function fields and finite abelian torsors
items.summary: Let $U$ be a smooth and connected curve over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic, with smooth compactification $X$. We generalize classical Geometric Class Field theory to provide a classification of fppf $G$-torsors over $U$ in terms of isogenies of generalized Jacobians, for any finite abelian group scheme $G$. We then apply this classification to give a novel description of the abelianized Nori fundamental group scheme of $U$ in terms of the Serre--Oort fundamental groups of generalized Jacobians of $X$; when $U=X$ is projective, we recover a well known description of the abelianized fundamental group scheme of $X$ as the projective limit of all torsion subgroup schemes of its Jacobian.

items.title: On the asymptotic growth of the norm of the partial sum operator on $\mathscr H^1$
items.summary: We show that the norm of the partial sum operator $S_N$ on the Hardy space $\mathscr H^1$ of Dirichlet series satisfies $$\liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac{\log\log N}{\log N}\lVert S_N\rVert_{\mathscr H^1\to\mathscr H^1}\geq\frac{1-\log 2}{2π}.$$ Combined with an upper bound of Bondarenko, Brevig, Saksman and Seip, this shows that $$\lVert S_N\rVert_{\mathscr H^1\to\mathscr H^1}\asymp\frac{\log N}{\log\log N}$$ as $N\to\infty$.

items.title: Equivalued affine springer fibers in mixed characteristic
items.summary: We study Witt-vector affine Springer fibers for tame equi-valued conjugacy classes in tamely ramified groups. Following the approach of Goresky-Kottwitz-MacPherson in the equal characteristic setting, we show that they admit pavings by iterations of perfections of affine space bundles whose base are smooth Hessenberg varieties. Along the way we revisit a version of the Chevalley restriction theorem for the dual of Lie algebras.

items.title: Line spreads of W(2n-1, q), q even
items.summary: Let q be an even prime power and n \ge 2. We construct line spreads of the symplectic polar space W(2n-1,q) by replacing pairwise disjoint reguli in a Desarguesian line spread. The construction is based on partitions of the points of PG(n-1,q^2) into points of a nondegenerate Hermitian variety and Baer sublines meeting that variety in exactly one point. In the plane case, the partition is invariant under a cyclic group of order q^2-q+ 1.

items.title: Bilinear forms with trace functions
items.summary: We obtain non-trivial bounds for bilinear sums of trace functions below the Pólya-Vinogradov range assuming only that the geometric monodromy group of the underlying ell-adic sheaf satisfies certain simple structural properties, in contrast to previous works which handled only special cases of Kloosterman and hypergeometric sheaves. Our approach builds on a general "soft" stratification theorem for sums of products of trace functions, based on an idea of Junyan Xu, combined with a new robust version of the Goursat-Kolchin-Ribet criterion.

items.title: A Mizohata--Takeuchi-type estimate for the hyperbolic paraboloid
items.summary: We prove Mizohata--Takeuchi-type estimates for the Fourier extension operator associated with the truncated hyperbolic paraboloid in $\R^3$. Our main result controls the weighted $L^2$ norm of the extension operator by the $L^2$ mass of the weight over a multiscale family of parallelepipeds arising from $\ell^2$ decoupling for the hyperbolic paraboloid. We deduce this result from a weighted $L^2$ estimate for functions whose Fourier transforms are supported in a small neighborhood of the hyperbolic paraboloid, which we establish using a bilinear refined decoupling estimate.

items.title: On a series related to the Möbius function
items.summary: For a natural number $n>1$ let $P^-(n)$ denote its smallest prime divisor. Alladi and Johnson proved that $\sum_{P^{-}(n)\equiv l \Mod{k}} \frac{μ(n)ω(n)}{n} = 0$ for $(l,k)=1$, and Tenenbaum showed that the partial sums of this series up to $X$ are $O_\varepsilon\bigl((\log\log X)^{5/3+\varepsilon}/\log X\bigr)$. In this article, we prove that these partial sums are in fact equal to $C(k,l)/\log X + O\bigl((\log\log X)^4/(\log X)^2\bigr)$, with an explicit constant $C(k,l)$. We also investigate the behaviour of these constants. In particular, we show under GRH that the number of reduced classes $l\Mod{k}$ for which $C(k,l)<0$ is $\varphi(k)(1- o(1))$ as $k\to\infty$.

items.title: DisCo Algebra: Why Disintegration and Combination Are Not Inverses
items.summary: We present DisCo algebra---a compositional framework for joint probability built from a symmetric cooperad (disintegration) and a non-unital partial symmetric operad (combination restricted to the image of disintegration) on the bare family $\mathcal{P}_n=\mathrm{Prob}([0,1]^n)$. No probability integral transform, no external summary functions, no enrichment of objects with conditional kernels. The disintegration side uses block-wise joint CDFs as intrinsic, measure-determined 1D summaries, yielding a lossy compression. The combination side reads the same summaries and reconstructs via regular conditional measures, yielding a lossless embedding on admissible inputs. We prove that combination followed by disintegration is the identity on admissible inputs, but disintegration followed by combination is not---it defines a renormalization operator $R_{\mathcal{I}}=\text{Combine}\circ\text{Disintegrate}$. The information loss of this operator is exactly the probability curvature $\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{I}}(μ)$---the conditional KL divergence between the true conditional distribution and the conditionally independent product. This curvature measures the obstruction to lossless decomposition and reveals a hard limit on how much cross-block dependence can be captured by CDF-based scalar block summaries.

items.title: Isothermal hydrodynamic limit for kinetic flocking models with nonlinear velocity alignment
items.summary: We study the hydrodynamic limit of kinetic flocking models with nonlinear velocity alignment and strong local Fokker--Planck forcing. In the limit of small Knudsen number the kinetic densities converge to a local Maxwellian centered around macroscopic quantities satisfying the compressible Euler system with isothermal pressure $p = \s ρ$, while macroscopic alignment is obtained by convolution of the microscopic velocity law with the standard Gaussian, resulting in a different nonlinearity. Such discrepancy has been observed already in \cite{black2025hydrodynamic}. In this note we rigorously justify the limit for admissible weak kinetic solutions and non-vacuous limiting macroscopic solution. Our analysis provides a quantitative rate of convergence in terms of relative entropy: $\cH(f_\e | μ) \lesssim \e$ provided initially $\cH(f_\e(0) | μ(0)) \leq \e$. In the linear case we recover the known result \cite{karper2015hydrodynamic}.

items.title: An $\widetilde{O}(n^3)$-time FPRAS for the Permanent
items.summary: We give an FPRAS for the permanent of an $n\times n$ $0/1$ matrix with running time $\widetilde O(n^3)$. Our algorithm extends to a strongly polynomial FPRAS for arbitrary nonnegative matrices with the same running-time bound (but in the unit-cost arithmetic model). Jerrum, Sinclair, and Vigoda (2004) gave the first FPRAS for the permanent of a nonnegative matrix. The running time was subsequently improved to $\widetilde{O}(n^7)$ by Bezáková, Štefankovič, Vazirani, and Vigoda (2008), and recently to $\widetilde{O}(n^6)$ by Chen, Vigoda, and Yang (2026). We introduce a multicommodity-flow bound inspired by electrical flows, replacing the usual path-length factor by routing energy. For the classical JSV chain with perfect-matching weights multiplied by $n^2$, we prove a relaxation-time bound of $O(n^3\log n)$ and obtain comparable bounds for estimating the stationary probabilities of having a specified pair of unmatched vertices. We use a separate chain on assignments to generate a warm start at any given temperature, avoiding the long initialization of the JSV chain. Finally, we replace the JSV chain with a new chain that uses only $n$ hole weights and speeds up hole-weight learning by a factor of $n$.

items.title: Rationality fields of CM modular forms
items.summary: We formulate a conjecture on the finitude of rationality fields (i.e., Fourier coefficient fields) of newforms of bounded degree, and prove this for CM forms assuming a generalized Riemann hypothesis. Then we explicitly determine what quadratic and cubic rationality fields occur for weight 2 CM forms, which is related to classifications of CM abelian varieties of GL(2) type. Several of these fields do not appear in the existing tables of newforms in the LMFDB.

items.title: On conservativity of multitype continuous-state branching processes
items.summary: In [4], Grey gives a condition on the branching mechanism $ψ$ of a continuous- state branching process Z ensuring that the process is conservative. This condition is obtained from the expression of the solution of the differential equation satisfied by the Laplace exponent of Z. In higher dimensions, it is generally no longer possible to make this solution explicit and very few conditions ensuring the conservativity of the process are known. In this paper, we provide necessary conditions and sufficient conditions for conservativity. For dimension 2, when types cannot regenerate themselves, we give a necessary and sufficient condition and we invert the Lamperti representation of the multitype branching process.

items.title: Uniform logarithmic Sobolev inequalities for the 2D Coulomb gas at the diffusive temperature scale
items.summary: For $N\ge2$ and $β>0$, consider the canonical 2D Coulomb gas ensemble \begin{equation} \mathrm{d}\mathbb{P}_{N,β}(Z) =\mathsf{Z}_{N,β}^{-1}e^{-β|Z|^2/2} \prod_{i<j}|z_i-z_j|^{β/N}\mathrm{d} Z \qquad\text{on }\mathbb{C}^N. \end{equation} The factor $N^{-1}$ in the pair exponent places the ensemble at the diffusive, or high-temperature, scale. We prove that, for every fixed inverse temperature $β>0$, this Gibbs measure satisfies a logarithmic Sobolev inequality (LSI) on the closed Dirichlet-form domain generated by collision-free compactly supported smooth functions, with a positive constant independent of $N$. The LSI constant may be chosen uniformly when $β$ ranges over a compact subset of $(0,\infty)$. A second main result establishes Poincaré and logarithmic Sobolev inequalities for planar Gaussian measures weighted by finite products of positive powers of distances to points, with constants depending only on the total variance of the underlying Gaussian measure and the total exponent, not on the number or locations of the points. To prove the full labeled Poincaré inequality, we decompose variance into permutation-invariant and label-dependent parts, controlled respectively by a weighted $\bar\partial$ estimate and by relative-coordinate conditioning with random transpositions; separately, one-site logarithmic Sobolev inequalities, a conditional entropy inequality, and a repulsive partition estimate give a defective logarithmic Sobolev inequality. Rothaus tightening combines the resulting full labeled Poincaré inequality with the defective logarithmic Sobolev inequality. The two main theorems on their stated closed form domains and all results used in their formal proofs, including those from the literature, have been formalized in Lean 4.

items.title: Three-circle inequalities for almost harmonic functions on cylinders
items.summary: The three-circle method was introduced into the blow-up analysis of harmonic maps by Qing and Tian [Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 1997]. We extend this method to a class of $(τ,ε)$-almost harmonic functions on long cylinders and establish three-circle inequalities for their weighted energies. These inequalities yield a dichotomy between exponential energy decay and asymptotic dominance of a critical Fourier mode, together with a characterization of the corresponding normalized limiting profiles. In the unweighted case, we prove convergence of the averaged neck curves and identify their limiting equations under additional structural assumptions. Applications include neck analysis and energy identities for harmonic maps, solutions of Rivière's equation, $α$-harmonic maps, biharmonic approximations of harmonic maps, and Willmore surfaces.

items.title: Maximal estimates of the Schrödinger operators with quadratic potential for orthonormal systems
items.summary: We establish an equivalence principle for local mixed-norm estimates for generalized Schrödinger propagators acting on orthonormal systems. Under suitable mixed-norm conditions, estimates for generalized propagators follow from the corresponding free Schrödinger estimates for every summability exponent $1\leβ\le2$. Applications include maximal estimates for Schrödinger equations with time-dependent quadratic potentials and for the special Hermite operator, as well as almost everywhere convergence of the associated densities. For the special Hermite operator, we also obtain a single-function maximal estimate that is sharp up to the endpoint. We construct counterexamples for the Schrödinger operator, by combining single particle and many particle constructions in complementary dimensions, yielding new necessary conditions in an intermediate range of summability exponents.

items.title: A Topological Quantum Field Theory for Representation Varieties of Torus Links
items.summary: We construct a Topological Quantum Field Theory (TQFT) that computes the virtual classes of $G$-representation varieties associated with the fundamental group of a torus link complement. Following the framework established by González-Prieto, Logares and Muñoz for $G$-representation varieties of surface groups, we introduce a suitable bordism whose iteration enables a recursive topological evaluation of these virtual classes. Via this TQFT, we explicitly compute the virtual class of these varieties for the groups $G=\mathrm{AGL}_1(\mathbb{C})$ and $G=\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})$.

items.title: Proof of Barry's Four Hankel Determinant Conjectures
items.summary: Barry introduced a central transform of integer sequences and proposed four conjectures concerning the Hankel transforms of central transform of four rational families. We prove these four conjectures. The proofs are unified within a common algebraic framework: we interpret the Hankel determinants as Gram determinants and use a basis of shifted monic Chebyshev polynomials to reveal the finite-band structure of the associated Gram matrices.

items.title: Two-generator presentations with a relation gap
items.summary: We exhibit two-generator two-relator group presentations that have cyclic relation modules but do not present one-relator groups; this resolves the relation gap problem. By attaching a single 3-cell to each of the corresponding presentation 2-complexes, one obtains counterexamples to Wall's D2 problem.

items.title: On the Length of Maximum Sum-Rank Distance Codes
items.summary: The classical theory of arcs in finite projective spaces provides a powerful geometric framework for studying maximum distance separable (MDS) codes and their possible lengths. In this paper, we investigate how this perspective extends to maximum sum-rank distance (MSRD) codes, whose geometric description involves systems of linear sets rather than individual projective points. Our main goal is to understand how the block structure of an MSRD code constrains its length. In dimension three, we determine the possible intersection patterns of lines with the associated linear sets and obtain explicit formulas for their characters and the weight distribution of the corresponding codes. These results lead to new length bounds and show that the block structure comes at a cost: the presence of a block of rank at least two reduces the maximum possible total length by at least $q-1$, and sufficiently long MSRD codes must be classical, that is, MDS codes over $\mathbb F_{q^m}$. We also prove that three-dimensional one-weight MSRD codes do not exist. In arbitrary dimension, we interpret shortening geometrically as projection and establish a general projection bound that extends classical counting arguments for arcs. This yields restrictions depending explicitly on the block profile and, for full-length blocks, identifies parameter ranges in which linearized Reed--Solomon codes attain the maximum possible number of blocks. Finally, we construct an exceptional three-dimensional MSRD code over $\mathbb F_9$ with three blocks of length two and propose a sum-rank analogue of the MDS conjecture.

items.title: Exact oracle complexity for function-value suboptimality under weighted initial conditions
items.summary: We determine the exact worst-case function-value suboptimality after $N$ first-order oracle calls on $L$-smooth, $μ$-strongly convex functions under a nonnegative weighted combination of the initial squared distance, function-value suboptimality, and squared gradient norm. Excluding the case where no strict improvement in function-value suboptimality can be guaranteed, the exact deterministic minimax risk in dimension $d\geq2N+1$ is characterized by the unique solution of a single scalar equation involving an $N$-step recurrence. The proof constructs an explicit hard instance for the lower bound and a constant-memory first-order method, ITEM-wf (previously called ITEM-w), whose worst-case performance matches this lower bound. On the standard initial conditions, the result recovers the exact convex bound attained by the Optimized Gradient Method of Kim and Fessler, and establishes the minimax optimality of the recently introduced ITEM-f method of Kim, Ryu, and Das Gupta for the initial function-value condition.

items.title: Height of minimal surfaces: sharp thresholds
items.summary: The confinement theorem of [CM1] gives Euclidean volume growth for a proper minimal submanifold whose height over a plane is sublinear. Such volume growth places strong restrictions on the geometry. This leaves linear height as the natural borderline and raises the question of which, if any, linearly growing cones still force Euclidean growth. Here we determine this borderline sharply for proper holomorphic curves in $C^2$. There are two sharp thresholds for the aperture depending on the Kähler angle $θ$ of the two-plane $Π$: $\tan(θ/2)$ and $\cot(θ/2)$. No proper holomorphic curve exists below the first, every such curve is algebraic below the second, and superquadratic proper holomorphic disks exist above the second. These conclusions extend to holomorphic submanifolds of arbitrary dimension and codimension. For stationary integral varifolds there are again three regimes: sublinear height forces Euclidean growth, narrow cones of aperture $\varepsilon$ force polynomial growth with exponent $n+O(\varepsilon^2)$, and wide cones allow arbitrarily fast growth. The order $\varepsilon^2$ is sharp: already in $R^3$, for every small $\varepsilon>0$ there are examples in a cone of aperture $\varepsilon$ whose volume grows at least like $r^{2+\frac45\varepsilon^2}$.

items.title: Four New Single-Error-Correcting Binary Codes
items.summary: We construct a $(16, 3072, 3)$-code, a $(17,6144,3)$-code, an $(18,12288,3)$-code and a $(19,24576,3)$-code. Consequently, we get four new lower bounds: $A(16,3) \geq 3072$, $A(17,3) \geq 6144$, $A(18,3) \geq 12288$ and $A(19,3) \geq~24576$. Each of the codes consists of a union of cosets of a linear code. The constructions are the result of a computer search executing a tabu search algorithm.

items.title: The compact double category $\mathbf{Int}(\mathbf{Poly}_*)$ models control flow and data transformations
items.summary: Hasegawa showed that control flow in programming languages---while loops and if-then-else statements---can be modeled using traced cocartesian categories, such as the category Set_* of pointed sets. In this paper we define an operad W of wiring diagrams that provides syntax for categories whose control flow moreover includes data transformations, including deleting, duplicating, permuting, and applying pre-specified functions to variables. In the most basic version, the operad underlies Int(Poly_*), where Int(T) denotes the free compact category on a traced category T, as defined by Joyal, Street, and Verity; to do so, we show that Poly_*, as well as any multivariate version of it, is traced. We show moreover that whenever T is uniform---a condition also defined by Hasegawa and satisfied by Poly_*---the resulting Int-construction extends to a double category IInt(T), which is compact in the sense of Patterson. Finally, we construct an operational structure on the double categories IInt(Poly_*) and IInt(Set_*) by which one can track trajectories as they move through the control flow associated to a wiring diagram, and we prove that the resulting operational semantics is computationally adequate, in the sense of Plotkin, for the denotational semantics in which a filled wiring diagram evaluates to a partial function.

items.title: On divisor sums due to Erdős and Ramanujan
items.summary: Let $d(n)$ denote the number of divisors of a positive integer $n$. A classical problem in analytic number theory is given by the asymptotic behavior of the divisor sum $\sum_{n \leq x} \frac{1}{d(n)}$, with Ramanujan having introduced an asymptotic formula for this sum with an explicit evaluation for the constant $A_1$ for the leading term $A_1 \frac{x}{\sqrt{\log x}}$. Gabdullin et al. recently considered a hybrid of this problem and the Titchmarsh divisor problem concerning $\sum_{p\leq x} d(p-1)$, proving that $\sum_{p\leq x} \frac{1}{d(p-1)} \asymp \frac{x}{(\log x)^{3/2}}$. This result and Erdős's asymptotic formula $ \sum_{n \leq x} d(d(n)) \sim c_1 \, x \log \log x $ for a constant $c_1 \in (0, \infty)$ lead us to consider the hybrid $\sum_{n \leq x} \frac{1}{d(d(n))}$ of the Erdős and Ramanujan divisor sums. In this paper, we prove that there exists a constant $c_3 \in (0, \infty)$ such that $$\sum_{n \leq x} \frac{1}{d(d(n))} \sim c_3 \frac{x}{ \log \log x}, $$ through a combined application of Golomb's estimate for powerful numbers, Turán's quantitative form of the Hardy-Ramanujan theorem, and a fourth-moment estimate for the number of distinct prime divisors due to Granville and Soundararajan. Moreover, an explicit formula for the constant $c_3$ is given.

items.title: Hankel Transform and $(α,β)$ Somos-4 Sequences
items.summary: An $(α,β)$ Somos-$4$ sequence $S_n$ is defined by the recurrence $S_nS_{n-4}=αS_{n-1}S_{n-3}+βS_{n-2}^2$ ($n\geq 4$), with suitable initial values, where $α$ and $β$ are constant parameters. A widely studied question is the following: When does the Hankel transform of a generating function become an $(α,β)$ Somos-4 sequence? In particular, how can $α$ and $β$ be derived for such a function? A sufficient condition for this problem has been established by Wang and Zhang. In this paper, we obtain the following three main results. (i): We extend the Wang--Zhang sufficient condition by working over the rational function field. Then we combine this result with the Sulanke--Xin quadratic transformation to resolve all of Barry's currently unsolved $(α,β)$ Somos-4 conjectures, which arise in diverse contexts, including generalized Catalan recurrences, Riordan arrays, generalized Bernstein arrays, and elliptic curves. (ii): We show that the odd and even subsequences of an $(α,β)$ Somos-4 sequence are again $(α,β)$ Somos-4 sequences with transformed parameters. This is employed to establish Barry's Hurwitz transform conjecture. (iii): Using the theory of orthogonal polynomials, we prove a Hankel determinant formula and thereby prove a conjecture related to the $(α,β)$ Somos-4 sequence. In addition, we prove some conjectures on formulas for periodic Hankel determinants.

items.title: Counterexamples to the Minimum Period Conjecture for Restricted Partition Functions
items.summary: For a finite sequence of positive integers $\boldsymbol{a}=(a_1,\dots,a_n)$, the restricted partition function $q_{\boldsymbol{a}}(k)$ denote the number of nonnegative integer solutions to the equation $a_1x_1+a_2x_2+\cdots +a_nx_n=k$. It is proved to be a quasi-polynomial of degree $n-1$. Write $q_{\boldsymbol{a}}(k)=\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}c_j(k)k^j$ with periodic coefficient functions $c_j$, and set $b_m=\#\{i:m\mid a_i\}$. In 2008, Beck, Sam, and Woods conjectured that the minimum period of $c_j(k)$ is $\mathrm{lcm}\{m:b_m>j\}$. In this paper, we derive an exact root-of-unity formula for every coefficient function $c_j(k)$. The formula proves the conjectured divisibility upper bound, but it also reveals a lower bound for the period of $c_j(k)$. Both divisibility bounds are sharp. This leads us to construct a family of counterexamples to this conjecture.
