We give formulae for ED and GD degrees of geometrically meaningful subvarieties of the Grassmannian, namely, products of smaller Grassmannians, matroid realization varieties, and Schubert varieties.

items.title: Accelerated Gradient Methods for Nonconvex Optimization: Escape Trajectories From Strict Saddle Points and Convergence to Local Minima
items.summary: This paper considers the problem of understanding the behavior of a general class of accelerated gradient methods on smooth nonconvex functions. Motivated by some recent works that have proposed effective algorithms, based on Polyak's heavy ball method and the Nesterov accelerated gradient method, to achieve convergence to a local minimum of nonconvex functions, this work proposes a broad class of Nesterov-type accelerated methods and puts forth a rigorous study of these methods encompassing the escape from saddle points and convergence to local minima through both an asymptotic and a non-asymptotic analysis. In the asymptotic regime, this paper answers an open question of whether Nesterov's accelerated gradient method (NAG) with variable momentum parameter avoids strict saddle points almost surely. This work also develops two metrics of asymptotic rates of convergence and divergence, and evaluates these two metrics for several popular standard accelerated methods such as the NAG and Nesterov's accelerated gradient with constant momentum (NCM) near strict saddle points. In the non-asymptotic regime, this work provides an analysis that leads to the "linear" exit time estimates from strict saddle neighborhoods for trajectories of these accelerated methods as well the necessary conditions for the existence of such trajectories. Finally, this work studies a sub-class of accelerated methods that can converge in convex neighborhoods of nonconvex functions with a near optimal rate to a local minimum and at the same time this sub-class offers superior saddle-escape behavior compared to that of NAG.

items.title: Differentiability of the Leading Lyapunov Exponent of a linear differential equation with random coefficients Application to the Calculation of the Selection Gradient in Random Environments
items.summary: The study of evolution in temporally fluctuating environments often relies on the analysis of Lyapunov exponents, which quantify the exponential growth of populations. However, when model parameters depend on a stochastic process, calculating the selection gradient, a key tool for predicting the evolution of phenotypic traits, becomes a mathematical challenge. While the periodic case has been resolved, a general approach for random environments remains to be developed. This article proposes a rigorous method to: Establish the differentiability of the leading Lyapunov exponent with respect to a parameter, providing an explicit integral formula for its derivative. Develop a numerical algorithm to approximate the derivative by solving an extended differential equation. Apply these results to the analysis of mutant invasion in a resident population at equilibrium, identifying the selection gradient as the derivative of the top Lyapunov exponent.

items.title: A Generating Polynomial for Convex Subsets of Posets
items.summary: For any finite poset we define a generating polynomial counting upsets, downsets, and their intersection. We investigate the behaviour of this polynomial with respect to poset operations and show that it distinguishes certain posets constructed with the operations of ordinal sum and disjoint union, including Series-Parallel posets as a special case. Lastly, we comment on connections to the causal set approach to quantum gravity.

items.title: Testing Treatment Effect Heterogeneity with Functional Outcomes
items.summary: Assessing treatment-effect heterogeneity is important in causal inference, particularly for functional outcomes where effects may vary over time and the common effect is unknown. We propose a nonparametric procedure that assesses treatment-effect homogeneity through a testable marginal implication. By comparing within-arm difference distributions, the construction removes the unknown common functional effect without estimating it. We measure departures between these distributions through an integrated squared discrepancy of their characteristic functionals. A full-support Gaussian integrating measure yields an explicit bounded-kernel representation and identifies equality of the difference laws without requiring moment conditions on the outcomes. We construct an unbiased generalized U-statistic that accounts for dependence among overlapping differences, derive its null, fixed-alternative, and local-alternative limits, and develop a centered multiplier bootstrap for inference. The framework extends to multiple treatment arms with a shared control. For computation, a random-direction approximation combined with a nine-state recursion reduces the cost to linear order in the sample size for fixed numerical settings. Simulation studies assess the finite-sample performance of the proposed procedure relative to several benchmark methods. An application to the Irish gas smart-metering trial illustrates its use for assessing heterogeneity in functional treatment responses.

items.title: A monoid-theoretical approach to infinite direct-sum decompositions of modules
items.summary: Let $\mathcal C$ be a class of modules over a ring $R$, closed under direct sums over index sets of cardinality $κ$ and isomorphisms, and such that the isomorphism classes form a set. The monoid of modules $V(\mathcal C)$ encodes the behavior of finite direct-sum decompositions of modules in $\mathcal C$. We endow $V(\mathcal C)$ with an additional operation reflecting $κ$-indexed direct sums, and study the resulting $κ$-monoid $V^κ(\mathcal C)$. The braiding-property and an equivalent universal property, allow us to show: if every module in $\mathcal C$ is a direct sum of at most $κ$ many modules generated by strictly fewer than $λ$ many elements, then all relations on $V^κ(\mathcal C)$ are induced by relations between direct sums indexed by sets of cardinality strictly less than $λ$. A theorem of Kaplansky states that every projective module is a direct sum of countably generated modules. We show that also all relations between infinite direct sums of projective modules are induced from those between countable direct sums of countably generated projective modules. If every projective module over a ring $R$ is a direct sum of finitely generated projective modules, then the monoid of finitely generated projective modules $V(R)$ completely determines the $κ$-monoid $V^κ(R)$. Together with the realization result of Bergman and Dicks, this characterizes the $κ$-monoids appearing as $V^κ(R)$ for a hereditary ring. In general, the $\aleph_0$-monoid $V^{\aleph_0}(R)$ fully determines $V^κ(R)$. Herbera and Příhoda's characterization of monoids of countably generated projective modules $V^*(R)$ over semilocal noetherian rings, yields a characterization of $V^κ(R)$ for these rings. We also characterize two-generated $\aleph_0$-monoids that appear as $V^{\aleph_0}(R)$ for hereditary rings $R$.

items.title: Strong Invariance Principle for Random Dirichlet Series
items.summary: It is shown that the random prime Dirichlet series $ X(s)=\sum_{p\in \mathcal{P}}\frac{ξ_p}{p^{s+1/2}} $ can be almost surely approximated by a Brownian motion, where $ \{ξ_p\}_{p\ge 1} $ are independent and identically distributed random variables with zero mean and finite variance, and $ \mathcal{P} $ is the set of prime numbers. As a consequence, the functional law of the iterated logarithm, limit laws of the iterated logarithm, and Chung's law of the iterated logarithm for $ X(s) $ are obtained. It is also shown that the random Dirichlet series $ Y(s)=\sum_{k=2}^{\infty} \frac{(\log k)^α}{k^{s+1/2}} $ with $ α=-1/2 $ admits the same approximation as $ X(s) $, and a direct relationship between $ X(s) $ and $ Y(s) $ with $ α=-1/2 $ is established. The strong invariance principle for $ Y(s) $ with $ α>-1/2 $ is also obtained.

items.title: Nonlocal-to-local variational limits of energies on partitions
items.summary: We study, through a $Γ$-convergence procedure, the asymptotic behaviour of a general class of nonlocal energies defined on functions taking values in a finite set $Y=\{y_1,\dots,y_N\}\subset\mathbb R^m$. These energies are written in terms of double integrals accounting for pairwise interactions in an open set $Ω$, weighted by a kernel $K_\varepsilon$. If the latter is controlled from above and below by suitable non-negative radial kernels with unit mass concentrating at the origin, then, up to subsequences, the $Γ$-limit has domain $BV(Ω;Y)$ and is given by a local surface energy. We show that the locality of the $Γ$-limit is not guaranteed if the concentration of mass fails. For a class of reference energies, we obtain a more explicit representation of the limit energy, also for non-radial kernels, recovering the limits of isotropic and anisotropic fractional perimeters. We also prove a homogenization result for periodic kernels.

items.title: Convergence rate of stochastic gradient descent under Łojasiewicz type condition and polynomially controlled noise
items.summary: Stochastic gradient methods are widely used for solving optimization problems in many scientific fields. Recently, their popularity has risen due to the increase in machine learning's prominence. Their convergence is often studied under the convexity assumption, which is too restrictive in modern applications. In this paper, we investigate the almost sure convergence rate and expectation under a Łojasiewicz-type gradient domination condition. This framework includes both bounded and decaying noise, as well as noise with controlled polynomial growth. The obtained results extend existing convergence by allowing a broader class of noise sequences and explicitly capturing the effect of their asymptotic behavior on the convergence rate and applicability.

items.title: Wave Packet Density in Local Smoothing: Refinements and Limitations
items.summary: We study wave packet density estimates in the local smoothing problem for the wave equation. Building on the framework of Gan, He, Li, and Wu, we refine the broad-incidence argument to obtain an improved local smoothing range in even dimensions. We then investigate the limitations of wave packet density methods, showing that genuine geometric obstructions already arise in the Euclidean setting.

items.title: Quasi-derivations of the (extended) Schrödinger--Witt algebras
items.summary: The Schrödinger--Witt algebras are infinite-dimensional Lie algebras of local dynamical symmetries of the free Schrödinger equation; they contain the Witt algebra of conformal transformations of the time line and appear in non-equilibrium statistical physics and in non-relativistic conformal field theory. We describe all quasi-derivations of the original and the twisted Schrödinger--Witt algebras. We prove that every quasi-derivation is the sum of a derivation, a trivial $\frac12$-derivation, a linear map with values in the center, and a finite linear combination of maps from three new families of quasi-derivations. As corollaries, we describe all $δ$-derivations, all $δ$-biderivations and all transposed $δ$-Poisson structures of the Schrödinger--Witt algebras. Finally, we prove that every quasi-derivation of the (original or twisted) extended Schrödinger--Witt algebra is the sum of an inner derivation and a multiple of the identity map. As a consequence, there are no nontrivial $δ$-derivations (for $δ\notin \{\frac12,1\}$), $δ$-biderivations (for $δ\neq1$), and transposed $δ$-Poisson structures on these algebras.

items.title: New examples of non-unique enhancements for triangulated categories
items.summary: We present a general procedure for constructing triangulated categories, linear over a field, with distinct enhancements. Some of our examples can be equipped with a (non-degenerate) t-structure, thereby showing that the existence of a t-structure does not imply uniqueness of enhancements, whether in the strong or weak sense (depending on the example).

items.title: Improved $L^p$ maximal estimates for higher-degree Weyl sums
items.summary: For each integer $k\ge3$, we establish the following estimate for all $1\le p<\infty$ and $\varepsilon>0$: \[ \left\|\sup_{t\in\mathbb{T}}\left|\sum_{n=1}^N e(nx+n^kt)\right|\right\|_{L^p(\mathbb{T})} \ll_{k,p,\varepsilon} N^{\max\{1-1/K_k,\,1-1/p\}+\varepsilon}, \] where $K_k=\min\{2^{k-1},k(k+1)/2\}$, $e(z)=e^{2πiz}$, and $\mathbb{T}=\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$. For $k\ge5$, this improves our earlier bound \cite{chen-miao-yuan-zhao} for $1\le p<D_k$, where $D_k=\min\{2^{k-1},k(k-1)\}$, and, together with the corresponding lower bound, extends the sharp range up to $N^\varepsilon$ from $p\ge D_k$ to $p\ge K_k$. The main new ingredient is a mixed minor-arc moment estimate obtained before taking the time supremum. The minor-arc maximal estimate then follows from a smooth reproducing kernel argument, while the major arcs are handled directly by Poisson summation and classical complete exponential-sum estimates. The reduction from suprema to mean values also yields a short and direct proof of improved $L^p$ estimates for maximal operators on Weyl sums with general polynomial phases, strengthening \cite[Theorem 1.1]{baker-chen-shparlinski}.

items.title: Ambient Chow Rings of Debarre--Voisin Fourfolds and the Beauville--Voisin Conjecture
items.summary: We prove the Beauville--Voisin conjecture for a very general Debarre--Voisin hyperkähler fourfold \(Y\subset\Gr(6,10)\) associated with a trivector \(σ\) on a ten-dimensional complex vector space \(V_{10}\). Namely, the cycle class map is injective on the subalgebra of the Chow ring generated by divisor classes and the Chern classes of the tangent bundle.

items.title: Finite power image families and automorphism actions in linear groups
items.summary: Let $k/\mathbb{Q}$ be a finitely generated field extension. We characterize the subgroups $G\leq GL_n(k)$ for which the power images $P_m(G)=\{g^m:g\in G\}$ form a finite family: this holds precisely when $G=N\rtimes F$, where $F$ is finite and $N$ is a uniquely divisible subgroup consisting of unipotent matrices. The subgroup $N$ is canonical and fully invariant.For $e=\exp(G/N)$, we obtain $P_m(G)=P_{\gcd(m,e)}(G)$, exactly $τ(e)$ distinct power images, and least positive period $e$, where $τ(e)$ is the number of positive divisors of $e$.Over $\mathbb{Q}$, the group coincides with the full group of rational points of its Zariski closure. Since finite automorphism-orbit count implies finiteness of the power-image family, an affirmative answer to Problem~21.40 of the Kourovka Notebook\cite{Kourovka} follows as a corollary. We further prove that a rational linear group $G$ admits a decomposition $G\cong(\mathbb{Q}^d,+)\rtimes F$, with $d\geq0$ finite and $F$ finite, whenever a virtually nilpotent subgroup of $\operatorname{Aut}(G)$ has finitely many orbits on $G$.The latter argument uses nonconstant invariant rational functions arising from nonzero Lie brackets to obstruct dense orbits. A metabelian action with five orbits on the rational Heisenberg group shows that solubility of the acting group is insufficient.

items.title: Classical Yang-Baxter equations and Nijenhuis operators for Lie algebras
items.summary: In this paper the conditions that when a Lie algebra is Nijenhuis are investigated. Furthermore all the Nijenhuis operators on $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ under the standard Cartan-Weyl basis are given. On the other hand, the relations between the classical Yang-Baxter equation and Nijenhuis operators $N$ on a Lie algebra and $P$ on a Lie coalgebra are derived by means of the bialgebraic theory for Nijenhuis Lie algebras.

items.title: Derivations of Lie $p$-rings with applications on ring extensions and computational methods
items.summary: Derivations are a well-known concept in the theory of Lie algebras. Here we investigate them for Lie $p$-rings. We show how they apply in the construction of cyclic extensions and in computational methods; in particular, we demonstrate that a consistency test for Lie $p$-presentations can be facilitated using derivations. The consistency test generalizes inspecific cases to parametrised Lie $p$-presentations and, further, to the construction of Lie $p$-covers. These provide a first building block towards a symbolic Lie $p$-ring generation algorithm.

items.title: A technical note on universal formula pcas
items.summary: We record some interesting technical caveats found when using universal formulae to formulate pcas -- namely, that there are different ways to extract a (partial) function from a definable collection of pairs, and these choices have an impact on formula complexity.

items.title: Explicit Oblique Inverses of the Approximate Discrete Radon Transform
items.summary: The approximate discrete Radon transform (ADRT) is a fast, hierarchical approximation of the Radon transform whose levels have explicit spectral decompositions, but its Moore-Penrose inverse, needed for data outside the range, has no closed form. We construct explicit left inverses of the ADRT, oblique projections onto its range, that are exact for every choice of their parameters and amplify noise by a constant factor relative to the Moore-Penrose inverse. Realized with polynomial filters on the butterfly structure of the levels, they are fixed linear maps of cost $O(N^{5/2}\log^{3/2}N/σ_{\min})$ for an $N\times N$ image, where $σ_{\min}$ is the smallest singular value of the ADRT; with the measured growth $σ_{\min}\sim N^{1/4}$ this is $O(N^{2.25}\log^{3/2}N)$. A hybrid that keeps the explicit inverse of the cross-quadrant level is cheaper and closer to the Moore-Penrose inverse. In compiled implementations both outperform a polynomial solver of the normal equations from $N=256$ on, and their conditioning is traced to the aliasing of integer-sampled lines.

items.title: On the depth of depth-weighted trees
items.summary: The depth-weighted tree DWT($f$) with weight function $f:\{0,1,2,\ldots\}\to (0,\infty)$ is a dynamic random tree grown from a root $r$ where vertices arrive consecutively and every new vertex attaches to a parent $u$ with probability proportional to $f$(distance between $u$ and $r$). This work is dedicated to a systematic analysis of the depth of DWT($f$). Namely, we provide precise analytic expressions of the typical depth of DWT($f$) for convergent, periodic, slowly growing, and (super-)exponentially growing weight functions. Furthermore, for bounded or exponentially growing $f$, we determine the typical depth up to a multiplicative constant, thus confirming and strengthening a conjecture of Leckey, Mitsche and Wormald.

items.title: Quantitative maximal $\mathrm{L}^p$-regularity for generators of real contraction semigroups
items.summary: Let $-A$ be the generator of a real, symmetric contraction semigroup on a $σ$-finite measure space. We prove a universal bound for maximal $\mathrm{L}^p$-regularity: In space-time norms $$\|Au\|_p \leq \big(p^* + \tfrac{p^*}{2(p^*-1)}\big) \|f\|_p,$$ where $p^* = \max(p,p/(p-1))$ and $u$ is the mild solution to the Cauchy problem with right-hand side $f$ starting at $u(0)=0$. Linear growth of the constant in $p^*$ is optimal. Our proof introduces an elementary approach to maximal regularity that avoids both vector-valued harmonic analysis and dilation theory. We also obtain quantitative maximal regularity estimates for real, non-symmetric semigroups that are contractive on a sector.

items.title: Computing Extinction Barriers in a Quorum-Sensing Reaction Network
items.summary: We introduce a simple reaction-network model of a quorum-sensing population that couples the cell density $x$ to the signal density $w$. In the four-channel cell-signal network studied here, scaling signal production and removal by the same factor $r$ leaves all deterministic equilibria, and their stability types, unchanged. Nevertheless, we show that $r$ shifts the quasipotential barrier $ΔV(r)$ for rare transitions towards extinction, and thus, under metastable exit assumptions, the mean time to reach a fixed neighbourhood of the extinction state on the exponential scale $e^{NΔV(r)}$. We compute the barrier by minimization of the path action with the signal retained as a fluctuating coordinate, and we check it against mean extinction times obtained without the action solver, i.e., from the backward equation of the jump process on a truncated lattice and from exact stochastic simulation. Over a range of $r$, the minimum-action barriers satisfy $ΔV(r)=ΔV_\infty+O(1/r)$, where $ΔV_\infty$ is obtained by eliminating the signal first, and at $r=1$ the barrier is 55% larger than $ΔV_\infty$. A formal first-order expansion attributes this increase to the lag of the signal, of which the fluctuations of the signal remove a quarter. The saddle barrier $ΔV(r)$ is also the least action needed to enter the basin of extinction, whereas the density threshold can be crossed more cheaply, by paths which keep the signal high and are usually followed by recovery. The mean extinction times of the backward equation, which include failed attempts, have a prefactor which tends to a constant, and they grow at a rate within $10^{-5}$ of $ΔV(r)$ at every tested rate.

items.title: The largest sets of non-opposite chambers in spherical buildings of type $B$
items.summary: The investigation into large families of non-opposite flags in finite spherical buildings has been a recent addition to a long line of research in extremal combinatorics, extending classical results in vector and polar spaces. This line of research falls under the umbrella of Erdős-Ko-Rado (EKR) problems, but poses some extra difficulty on the algebraic level compared to aforementioned classical results. From the building theory point of view, it can be seen as a variation of the center conjecture for spherical buildings due to Tits, where we replace the convexity assumption by a maximality condition. In previous work, general upper bounds on the size of families of non-opposite flags were obtained by applying eigenvalue and representation-theoretic techniques to the Iwahori-Hecke algebras of non-exceptional buildings. More recently, the classification of families reaching this upper bound in type $A_n$, for $n$ odd, was accomplished by Heering, Lansdown, and Metsch. For buildings of type $B$, the corresponding Iwahori-Hecke algebra is more complicated and depends non-trivially on the type and rank of the underlying polar space. Nevertheless, we are able to find a uniform method based on antidesigns and obtain classification results for chambers (i.e.\ maximal flags) in most cases.

items.title: The algebraic and geometric classification of semi-alternative superalgebras
items.summary: The algebraic and geometric classifications of complex $3$-dimensional semi-alternative superalgebras are given. As corollaries, we obtain the algebraic and geometric classifications of complex $3$-dimensional $\mathfrak{perm}$, associative, and assosymmetric superalgebras.

items.title: Combinatorial bounds for the v-number of binomial edge ideals
items.summary: We study the local $\mathrm v$-numbers of binomial edge ideals from a combinatorial perspective. For each minimal prime $P_{\mathcal S}$ of $J_G$, indexed by a cutset $\mathcal S$ of $G$, we consider two combinatorial invariants, $\mathrm v^-_{\mathcal S}(G)$ and $\mathrm v^+_{\mathcal S}(G)$, defined in terms of transversals of suitable hypergraphs, and show that the local $\mathrm v$-number $\mathrm v_{P_{\mathcal S}}(J_G)$ satisfies $\mathrm v^-_{\mathcal S}(G)\leq \mathrm v_{P_{\mathcal S}}(J_G)\leq \mathrm v^+_{\mathcal S}(G)$. Under a suitable hypothesis on the connected components, we provide explicit graph-theoretic descriptions of these invariants and analyze when they coincide, giving a combinatorial way to determine the local $\mathrm v$-numbers. As an application, we derive a sufficient condition for this coincidence, which applies to a broad class of graphs. Furthermore, we identify a constant that controls the gap between $\mathrm v^-_{\mathcal S}(G)$ and $\mathrm v^+_{\mathcal S}(G)$, thereby showing that the local $\mathrm{v}$-number lies within a bounded interval. Applications to cycles and trees illustrate both the equality criterion and the resulting bounds.

items.title: Uniform transport processes and the Brownian sheet:the one-parameter rate of convergence is preserved
items.summary: In~\cite{BFR} we constructed processes $W_n$, built from a family of independent standard Poisson processes, that converge almost surely to the Brownian sheet uniformly on $[0,1]^2$, and in~\cite{Rov} we proved that $P(\max_{[0,1]^2}|W_n-W|>αn^{-β})=o(n^{-q})$ for every $β<λ/2$, where $λ\in(0,\tfrac{1}{5})$ is the parameter of the construction; this gives rates $n^{-β}$ with $β<\tfrac{1}{10}$. In this paper, we show that the same construction, with $λ\geq 1$, satisfies \[ P\!\left(\max_{(s,t)\in[0,1]^2} |W_n(s,t)-W(s,t)| > α\, n^{-1/2}(\log n)^3\right) = o(n^{-q}) \quad\text{for every }q>0, \] which is the one-parameter rate of Gorostiza and Griego~\cite{GG} up to a factor $(\log n)^{1/2}$. In particular the restriction $λ<\tfrac{1}{5}$ is not needed.

items.title: Continuous Comparison of Free Simplicial Prounipotent and Pro-$p$ Resolutions
items.summary: We give a continuous version of the comparison theorem for free simplicial resolutions in the categories of prounipotent groups over a field of characteristic zero and of pro-$p$ groups. The resolutions carry free bases compatible with degeneracies; their ranks may be infinite. In characteristic zero the lifting step follows from continuous linear splittings and the universal property of completed free Lie algebras. In the pro-$p$ case it follows from the classical projectivity of free pro-$p$ groups. A relative lifting argument and an explicit simplicial cylinder establish homotopy uniqueness. We formulate the free bases using actual surjections in the simplex category, so degeneracy words related by simplicial identities are identified from the outset, and we spell out the full matching objects used in the lifting argument. The question arose naturally in our preceding work on Bousfield--Kan completions of subcontractible presentations.

items.title: Random independent sets in uncrowded hypergraphs
items.summary: Given any fixed integer $k \ge 2$ and sufficiently large $d$, we show that the largest possible fractional chromatic number of a $k$-uniform $d$-degenerate uncrowded hypergraph $H$ (i.e., with girth at least $5$) satisfies \[ χ_f(H) = (1 + o_d(1)) \left((k-1)\,\frac{d}{\log d}\right)^{\frac{1}{k-1}}. \] In fact, we prove that this holds for $k$-uniform $d$-degenerate hypergraphs of girth at least $g$, for any given $g \ge 5$. As a corollary, we obtain improved bounds on the fractional chromatic number of $d$-degenerate linear hypergraphs. This work builds upon a recent result by Allen, Dhawan, and Noel, extending it from graphs to hypergraphs. In addition to overcoming the new difficulties that arise in the hypergraph setting, our approach yields a simpler proof even in the original graph case. Our proof of the upper bound uses a simpler iterative procedure for sampling independent sets. We also establish bounds for fractional colorings with local demands, a framework introduced by Kelly and Postle, verifying a recent conjecture of Yu and Zhang. As a consequence, we obtain a degree-sequence bound on the independence number of uncrowded hypergraphs with a leading constant matching the shattering threshold. For the matching lower bound, we use a hypergraph variant of the uniform attachment model and harmonic vertex weights to bound the fractional chromatic number via linear programming duality, then remove all short cycles by deleting vertices of negligible total weight. We also replace the Catalan-number argument used in the graph case with a matrix-norm estimate, simplifying the analysis.

items.title: Quasi-Monte Carlo based meshfree methods for parabolic equations on parameterized Riemannian manifolds
items.summary: We develop and analyze a randomized path sampling framework for the pointwise approximation of linear parabolic equations on parameterized Riemannian manifolds, treating both closed manifolds and manifolds with Dirichlet boundary. Based on the Feynman-Kac representation, we construct a parameter-coordinate retraction-based discretization, referred to as the p-Ret scheme, for the manifold diffusion generated by the uniformly elliptic operator, and use it to formulate the Monte Carlo (MC) and randomized quasi-Monte Carlo (RQMC) methods. We derive the local weak consistency of the p-Ret transition and first-order weak convergence of the temporal discretization on closed manifolds. For fixed $h$, we show that RQMC sampling yields asymptotically faster variance decay than standard MC. On closed manifolds, the variance is $o(n^{-1})$ and, under additional regularity, satisfies the sharper bound $O(n^{-2+\varepsilon})$ for any $\varepsilon>0$. For Dirichlet problems, despite the discontinuities induced by numerical first exit, nested-uniformly scrambled Sobol' sampling attains $O(n^{-1-1/s+\varepsilon})$ variance for any $\varepsilon>0$ under suitable regularity assumptions, where $s$ denotes the nominal path-space dimension. More notably, we further develop an Array-RQMC strategy based on stepwise low-dimensional randomized point sets and a Hilbert space-filling curve that maps high-dimensional particle states to a one-dimensional ordering, and establish a variance rate of $o(n^{-1})$ under suitable assumptions. Numerical results demonstrate that both RQMC methods reduce variance and root mean square error (RMSE) relative to standard MC and remain effective for manifolds with intrinsic dimension up to $50$.

items.title: Finiteness of planar central configurations of six bodies for all positive masses: Part I, exceptional-mass first limits
items.summary: We separate the generic positive-mass finiteness problem for planar six-body central configurations from finiteness on exceptional mass loci. The Chang--Chen diagram enumeration has 117 graphs. The arguments below confine 40 first-limit diagram obligations to proper necessary mass loci. In particular, a direct function-field argument establishes the No.~66 mass condition for both zero and nonzero drift. We establish the algebraic reduction from an infinite positive family to a germ with an unbounded seven-product, and use the stated diagram rules and computational certificates to confine its mass vector to the union of these loci. Finiteness on the exceptional positive mass loci, the proposed subject of Part II, will be discussed in another paper.

items.title: On the quotient matrix and its distinct eigenvalues
items.summary: Let $M$ be an $n\times n$ matrix partitioned into blocks according to a partition $P=\{C_{1},\dots,C_{\ell}\}$ of its index set, and let $Q$ be the corresponding equitable quotient. We study when $Q$ contains every distinct eigenvalue of $M$, so that the distinct spectral data of a large structured matrix can be recovered from a lower-order quotient. We first correct the distinction between a coarsest equitable partition and a minimum-order quotient that captures all distinct eigenvalues. We then establish an exact block-lifting construction with characteristic polynomial $χ_M(x)=χ_Q(x)\prod_i(x-θ_i)^{|C_i|-1}$, derive multiplicity-design consequences, and give a necessary and sufficient eigenspace criterion for quotient capture. Further results quantify automatic capture through geometric multiplicity and describe exact spectral factors generated by twin cells in graph matrices. Applications to adjacency, weighted adjacency, Laplacian, signless Laplacian, distance, and distance-based Laplacian matrices are validated, including minimal one-cell refinements that recover eigenvalues hidden by collapsed twin classes.

items.title: Bousfield--Kan Completions of Subcontractible Presentations
items.summary: We study Bousfield--Kan completions through the interaction of free simplicial resolutions, their filtration spectral sequences, and a noncommutative arithmetic square. For every free discrete simplicial group of finite type, we express its integral pronilpotent completion as the homotopy pullback of its rational prounipotent completion and the product of its pro-$p$ completions over an explicit adelic simplicial group. The adelic entry is formed by taking restricted products at finite nilpotent stages and then their inverse limit; no nilpotency assumption on the original group of components is required. Finite subpresentations of contractible presentations provide an explicit application of this construction. Independence of the specified relators makes the positive-degree terms of the rational and mod-$p$ filtration spectral sequences vanish, with convergence verified on the quotient towers. Continuous comparison of free simplicial resolutions then realizes, in characteristic zero, the equivalence with a constant free prounipotent group by morphisms and homotopies in that category. For the corresponding presentation complex $K$ we obtain $R_\infty K\simeq K(F_R(Z),1)$ for $R=\mathbb Q,\mathbb F_p,\mathbb Z$, where $Z$ indexes a complementary basis and $F_R(Z)$ denotes, respectively, the rational points of a free prounipotent group, a free pro-$p$ group, or a free pronilpotent group. Compatible contractions at the nilpotent stages identify all four entries of the arithmetic square in this case.

items.title: On the center of the Clifford Algebra
items.summary: The center of a Clifford algebra associated to a non-degenerate quadratic form over a field is described in the existing literature, but an elementary proof of the result seems lacking. The aim of this paper is to provide such an elementary proof.

items.title: Anomalies for compact simple Lie groups via $G$-kernels for loop group nets
items.summary: Let $G$ be a compact simply connected simple Lie group and $k \geq 1$. Jump loops give an outer homomorphism $θ_k$ from $G$ to the outer automorphisms of the local factor of the level-$k$ loop group net, which is the hyperfinite type $\mathrm{III}_1$ factor. We show that its Sutherland obstruction is $k$ times the positive basic class in $H^3_{\mathrm{Borel}}(G, \mathbb{T}) \cong H^{4}(BG, \mathbb{Z})$ and that $θ_k$ is faithful, so it is a $G$-kernel. Central elements act by the outer automorphisms of the simple currents. In types A, D, E the level-one class is computed by comparing maximal-torus jump loops with the lattice $α$-induction construction of the companion paper on both current and charged generators, followed by integral degree-four Cartan restriction. Higher levels follow by tensor additivity, and the remaining types by restriction along index-one embeddings into simply laced groups. As a consequence, for every compact simply connected semisimple $G$, every class in $H^4(BG, \mathbb{Z})$ is the obstruction of a $G$-kernel on the hyperfinite type $\mathrm{III}_1$ factor.

items.title: Folding to the Bessel-Clifford system, and Equivariant Topological Recursion
items.summary: We study the interplay between symmetry reductions of meromorphic connections, folding, and topological recursion. As a motivating example, we realize the Bessel-Clifford system as a folding of a symmetry-invariant subspace of the $0-$member of the Painlevé IV hierarchy. We introduce equivariant topological recursion for spectral curves with a Klein four-group $\mathbb Z_2\times\mathbb Z_2$ symmetry and prove that the corresponding equivariant correlators can be folded to the ordinary topological recursion correlators on the quotient spectral curve. We further establish the compatibility of this folding with the associated wave functions and quantum curves. In the Bessel-Clifford example, this yields an explicit relation between the equivariant and folded wave functions and recovers the corresponding quantum curve reduction. These results provide a framework for relating symmetry reductions of integrable systems to folding operations in topological recursion.

items.title: Untrained CNN and coefficient-space regularization for joint reconstruction in photoacoustic tomography
items.summary: The joint reconstruction of the initial pressure and spatially varying sound speed in photoacoustic tomography from boundary measurements is considered. A regularized data-driven framework is proposed in which the unknown fields are represented in finite-dimensional wavelet spaces and fixed nonlinear features generated by an untrained convolutional neural network (CNN) are used to reconstruct the initial-pressure coefficients through Tikhonov-regularized least squares. A learned coefficient-space prior is subsequently used to infer the squared sound-speed coefficients. Numerical experiments demonstrate accurate reconstruction on held-out data and strong generalization to previously unseen phantom geometries. The frozen reconstruction map also remains stable under measurement noise not represented during training, with only minor changes in reconstruction accuracy for noise levels up to $10\%$. In comparison with the supervised trained-CNN approach considered in this work, the untrained representation yields substantially smaller reconstruction errors while requiring approximately one-sixth of the computational time. These results demonstrate that fixed random convolutional features combined with regularized coefficient-space learning provide an efficient and robust approach to joint reconstruction in photoacoustic tomography.

items.title: Reynolds Leibniz bialgebras of any weight
items.summary: This paper studies bialgebraic structures associated with a Reynolds Leibniz algebra of weight $λ$, that is, a Leibniz algebra equipped with a Reynolds operator of weight $λ$. We first present equivalent characterizations of Reynolds Leibniz bialgebras of weight $λ$, using matched pairs and Manin triples. Next, we examine compatibility conditions between solutions of the classical Leibniz Yang-Baxter equation and Reynolds operators of weight $λ$, framed in terms of triangular Reynolds Leibniz bialgebras. Finally, building on results of Ayupov {\em et al.}, we classify two-dimensional triangular Reynolds Leibniz bialgebras of weight $λ$.

items.title: Universal norms and de Rham representations
items.summary: The purpose of this note is to show that the computation of the universal norms in Iwasawa cohomology for the $p$-adic cyclotomic extension implies an analogous result for any $p$-adic extension that contains the cyclotomic extension. In addition, we prove a twisted cyclotomic variant, which applies to all Lubin--Tate extensions.

items.title: The Strong Total Cover Problem
items.summary: The Strong Total Cover Problem (STCP) is a novel covering problem defined on a graph $G = (V, E)$, where the objective is to find a minimum-cardinality subset $T \subseteq V \cup E$ such that every element of $V \cup E$ is covered. In this setting, a vertex covers itself and all its incident edges, while an edge covers itself together with its two endpoints. The STCP resembles classical covering problems such as Vertex Cover and Edge Cover problems, and naturally arises as the dual of the total matching problem. In this paper, we investigate the STCP from algorithmic, complexity, and polyhedral perspectives. We first establish close connections between STCP, the Dominating Set Problem, and the Maximum Induced Matching Problem. These relationships provide structural insights, imply the NP-hardness of STCP, and identify graph classes for which the problem is polynomial-time solvable. We then investigate the weighted version of STCP, showing that it remains NP-hard even on complete graphs with binary weights. On the other hand, we present a 2-approximation algorithm, and a polynomial-time algorithm for complete bipartite graphs. On the polyhedral side, we introduce the Strong Total Cover Polytope and derive several families of valid inequalities, some of which are shown to define facets. Finally, we provide a complete linear description of the associated polytope for triangular cactus graphs, revealing an interesting contrast with the considerably more intricate facial structure of the dominating set polytope on cactus graphs.

items.title: Galois measures and the Katz map
items.summary: The purpose of this paper is to explain the proofs of the results announced by Nick Katz in 1977, namely a description of ``Galois measures for Tate modules of height two formal groups over the ring of integers of a finite unramified extension of $\mathbf{Q}_p$''.

items.title: Sieve-free ReLU Bayesian priors with near-minimax posterior contraction
items.summary: We establish fractional-posterior contraction for shallow ReLU networks in Gaussian random-design regression with a $β$-Hölder target, using priors independent of the sample size and smoothness parameters. For any fixed design law $P_X$ on $[0,1]^d$, we obtain contraction in Rényi divergence and, after clipping posterior draws at a bound on the target range, in squared $\mathcal{L}^2(P_X)$ loss at rate $(\log n/n)^{2β/(2β+d)}$. This matches the classical Hölder minimax rate up to a logarithmic factor. These priors have random finite width and use width-dependent uniform or Gaussian weight distributions, or width-independent Student $t$ distributions, including Cauchy distributions.

items.title: Acceleration Survives Heavy Tails and Generalized Smoothness
items.summary: We establish high-probability accelerated convergence guarantees for convex $(L_0,L_1)$-smooth optimization with unbiased stochastic gradients under heavy-tailed noise, assuming a central $α$-th noise moment bounded by $σ^α$, $α\in(1,2]$. Such guarantees are known under classical $L$-smoothness, but extending them through localization over an $O(R)$-radius ball may introduce an $e^{O(L_1R)}$ factor. We avoid this dependence in two ways. First, a two-phase scheme uses \algname{Clip-SGD} to reach a low-curvature regime, after which clipped stochastic similar triangles (\algname{Clip-SSTM}) attains, with probability at least $1-δ$, $f(y_K)-f^\star\le\widetilde{\mathcal O}\big(L_0R^2/K^2+σRK^{-(α-1)/α}\big),$ where $R$ bounds the distance from the Phase-II starting point to a minimizer. Second, a modified deterministic weight schedule allows \algname{Clip-SSTM} to start directly from the initial point, controlling the high-curvature transient before recovering acceleration. With the prescribed initialization, both approaches recover the classical accelerated rate, with $L_1$ confined to an accuracy-independent transient, up to logarithmic factors. The two-phase analysis uses two coupled potentials to preserve the low-curvature regime despite momentum; the one-phase analysis controls the initial high-curvature regime using a modified version of the classical SSTM weight schedule.

items.title: Orthogonal Projections and Assouad Dimension: Resolving Fraser's Questions
items.summary: We examine two questions on exceptional orthogonal projections for Assouad dimension. Let $1\le k<d$ and $1\le q<d$. For a set $F$ contained in a $q$-dimensional subspace $W\subset\R^d$ and containing a nonempty relatively open subset of $W$, we compute both the Hausdorff and packing dimensions of the exceptional $k$-planes as $k(d-k)-|q-k|-1$. In particular, a square in $\R^3$ has a one-dimensional set of exceptional plane projections. This disproves the bound $k(d-1-k)$ in Question 17.8.1 of Fraser's book as stated, for every $2\le k<d$. The planar packing question, Question 17.8.2, is already answered affirmatively by Wu's countability theorem. Using that theorem, we also describe the distinction between planar sets of Assouad dimension at most $1$ and those of dimension greater than $1$ when they are embedded in higher-dimensional spaces. The computations use elementary Grassmannian geometry; we make no claim of a new planar projection theorem or of an optimal bound for arbitrary higher-dimensional sets.

items.title: Distributed Performance Boosting through Neural Control for Plug-and-Play Networks
items.summary: We address the problem of improving the performance of pre-stabilized networked systems subject to plug-and-play (PnP) operations, namely additions or removals of subsystems. While distributed baseline controllers can preserve stability after a PnP transition, augmenting them with expressive neural policies can invalidate the formal stability guarantees. To overcome this issue, we build on recently proposed Performance Boosting controllers based on the Internal Model Control (IMC) principle, which reduce closed-loop stability to a finite $\ell_2$-gain requirement on an auxiliary operator. In the distributed setting, this operator is formed by interconnecting local neural operators that exchange information only between neighboring subsystems. We then derive free parametrizations of this interconnection, namely explicit maps from unconstrained trainable variables to interconnected neural operators satisfying a prescribed network gain bound for every parameter value. The obtained distributed neural controller can therefore be trained by unconstrained gradient-based optimization without stability constraints or projection steps, while retaining the prescribed gain bound at every training iterate. We develop two complementary parametrizations. A neighbor-based compositional parametrization uses local coupling bounds, so that after a PnP event only subsystems whose bounds change need to update their gain parameters. A network-norm parametrization instead uses a bound on the overall coupling matrix and can reduce conservatism, at the price of requiring network-wide information. A PnP DC-microgrid case study shows that the proposed neural layer improves voltage transients under topology changes and load variations while preserving nominal closed-loop stability.

items.title: Bialgebras induced by special left Alia algebras
items.summary: This paper investigates bialgebraic structures associated with special left-Alia algebras. Based on the special left-Alia algebras originally introduced in the study of algebras with skew-symmetric identity of degree 3, we systematically examine the structure of a Nijenhuis left-Alia bialgebra. This bialgebra consists of a compatible pairing between a Nijenhuis left-Alia algebra and a Nijenhuis left-Alia coalgebra. We prove that a Nijenhuis special left-Alia bialgebra, which is constructed from a commutative associative algebra (or a cocommutative coassociative coalgebra) equipped with two commuting linear maps, can be induced from a Nijenhuis commutative cocommutative associative D-bialgebra. This establishes an explicit link between these two families of bialgebraic structures. Furthermore, the paper provides a general method for constructing Nijenhuis operators on arbitrary left-Alia algebras and coalgebras.

items.title: Pencils of projective hypersurfaces, Griffiths heights and geometric invariant theory. II Hypersurfaces with semihomogeneous singularities
items.summary: This paper establishes a formula for the stable Griffiths height of the middle-dimensional cohomology of a pencil of projective hypersurfaces $H$, with semihomogeneous singularities, over some smooth projective curve $C$. This formula appears as Theorem 5.1 in the first part of this paper (arxiv:2506.15334). The proof of this formula relies on the strategy developed in my previous work (arxiv:2212.11019v3) to derive an expression for this Griffiths height when the only singularities of the fibers of $H$ over $C$ are ordinary double points. To deal with general semihomogeneous singularities, we complement this strategy by the construction of a finite covering $C'$ of $C$ such that the pencil $H' = H \times_C C'$ over $C'$ admits a smooth model $\widetilde{H}'$ with semistable fibers with smooth components. This allows us to circumvent the delicate issue of the determination of the elementary exponents attached to the singular fibers of $H/C$.

items.title: Note on the largest prime factors of consecutive integers
items.summary: In this paper, we give an alternative proof of Tao-Teräväinen's results by showing \begin{align*} &\#\{n\leq x:P^+(n-1)<P^+(n)<P^+(n+1)>\max_iP^+(n+a_i)\}\gg x,\\&\#\{n\leq x:P^+(n-1)>P^+(n)<P^+(n+1)>\max_iP^+(n+a_i)\}\gg x, \end{align*} where the $a_i$ are at most finite in number, with $|a_i| = O(1)$. We also obtain some comparison results for five numbers under the Elliott-Halberstam conjecture for friable integers. For any $\varepsilon>0$, we also show \begin{align*} &\#\left\{n\leq x:1\leq \frac{P^+(n+1)}{P^+(n)}<1+\varepsilon\right\}\gg_\varepsilon \frac{x}{\log x}, \end{align*} which improves a previous result $\gg x(\log x)^{-50}$ due to S. Kim (2020).

items.title: The Compactness Theorem for Enriched Logic
items.summary: The framework of enriched logic extends positive logic (also known as coherent logic) from sets to structures internal to a symmetric monoidal closed category $\mathcal{V}$. This framework was developed by Rosický and the second-named author. The main novelty of this logic is that the arities of the function and relation symbols are now objects in $\mathcal{V}$. We prove the compactness theorem for this enriched logic. That is, a set of $\mathcal{V}$-enriched sequents has a model (internal to $\mathcal{V}$) if every finite subset has a model. To achieve this, we define ultraproducts of enriched structures and prove enriched versions of Łos' theorem. We then develop some model-theoretic applications. We start with an enriched version of the model-theoretic method of diagrams, establishing a correspondence between homomorphisms whose domain is some enriched structure $A$ and models of the set $\operatorname{Diag}(A)$ of all enriched atomic formulas with parameters from $A$ that are true in $A$. Combining this with our compactness theorem, we prove amalgamation results, laying the foundations for enriched syntactic types (in the model-theoretic sense). We finish the paper with a collection of examples of $\mathcal{V}$ that our results apply to. Besides recovering the classical case when $\mathcal{V} = \mathbf{Set}$, these include many presheaf toposes, categories of monoid acts, the category of abelian groups and related additive categories, categories of (small) enriched categories, and the categories of posets and pseudometric spaces.

items.title: A Generalized Half-Singleton Bound for List Decoding of Insertion/Deletion Errors
items.summary: We derive an upper bound on the rate of a linear code capable of list decoding from insertion and deletion errors. Subsequently, we show that a linear code can list decode from at most $n - \frac{L}{L+1}k + 1$ insdel errors with fixed list size $L$, and that this bound is strict when the code does not contain the all-ones vector. We also provide a simple construction of codes achieving the optimal rate for any given list size capable of correcting a single insdel error. All the results hold for linear codes over finite fields of size $q \geq 3$.

items.title: Indiscernible Extraction in Theories with Bounded $k$-splitting
items.summary: Hanson introduced the class of theories with bounded $k$-splitting, a higher-arity notion of stability, and proved an indiscernible extraction result for those theories assuming the existence of a $k$-ineffable cardinal. In this article, we show that the conclusion of Hanson's theorem is equivalent to the weaker assertion that there exists a weakly compact cardinal, as well as prove additional indiscernible extraction results for these theories in ZFC. Finally, we show that Hanson's construction of total bounded ultraimaginary Morley sequences in theories with bounded $k$-splitting follows from ZFC.

items.title: A Rockafellar theorem for cyclically quasi-monotone maps: The regular non-vanishing case
items.summary: In this paper, we study the connection between cyclic quasi-monotonicity and quasi-convexity, focusing on whether every cyclically quasi-monotone (possibly multi-valued) map is included in the normal cone operator of a quasi-convex function, in analogy with Rockafellar's theorem for convex functions. We provide a positive answer for locally Lipschitz, non-vanishing maps in any dimension, as well as for general multi-maps in dimension $1$. We further discuss connections to revealed preference theory in economics and to $L^\infty$ optimal transport. Finally, we present explicit constructions and examples, highlighting the main challenges that arise in the general case.

items.title: On the tangent bundle and the divisor theory of a general matroid
items.summary: Extending classical algebro-geometric constructions to arbitrary matroids, we construct a $K$-class $T_M\in K(M)$ for every loopless matroid $M$. When $M$ is realizable by a linear subspace $L$, $T_M$ recovers the $K$-class of the tangent bundle of the wonderful compactification $W_L$. We derive two formulas for the total Chern class of $T_M$ (one combinatorial and one geometric) and show that the associated Todd class agrees with the Todd class appearing in the matroid Hirzebruch--Riemann--Roch formula. To develop a positivity theory entirely at the combinatorial level, we introduce the notion of a "fake effective cone", a combinatorial analogue of the classical effective cone, and use it to characterize big and nef divisors in $A(M)$. Finally, we define the $β_S$ classes, obtained from Cremona conjugates of the classical $α_S$ classes, and study their properties to provide a rich and computable family of combinatorially nef divisors.

items.title: Harnack-type inequalities for nonlocal doubly nonlinear parabolic equations
items.summary: We establish intrinsic Harnack inequalities for nonlocal doubly nonlinear parabolic equations in the slow-diffusion range: \begin{equation*} (u^q)_t+ \operatorname{P.V.} \int\limits_{\mathbb{R}^N}\frac{|u(x, t)-u(y, t)|^{p-2}(u(x, t)-u(y, t))}{|x-y|^{N+sp}}\,dy=0,\quad s\in(0,1),\quad 0<q < p-1. \end{equation*}

items.title: A configurational numerical viscosity for thermodynamically compatible finite volume schemes of compressible multiphase flows
items.summary: We consider the fluid subsystem of a variationally derived hyperbolic thermodynamically compatible (HTC) model of compressible multiphase flows. Its total energy is in general not convex in the natural state variables, so a scalar numerical viscosity acting on them need not produce non-negative entropy. Reformulating the equations in terms of the volume fractions separates changes in the amount of each phase from changes in its intrinsic state. This guides the construction of a configurational numerical viscosity in phase variables, in which the energy is convex, while the scheme retains the structure of the HTC model. At the semi-discrete level, the new schemes satisfy: I) local conservation of the phase masses, the mixture momentum and the total energy; II) a cell entropy inequality whose production is non-negative face by face and phase by phase, with no convexity assumption in the evolved variables and no clipping; III) positivity of the partial densities and volume fractions under explicit time-step conditions; IV) exact preservation of contact equilibria; V) equivalence with a scheme for the density-weighted volume fractions. The key ingredients are: i) an exact decomposition of the jump of each phase across a face into a configurational part, dissipated with the material speed, and an intrinsic part, dissipated with the acoustic speed; ii) an exchange form of this dissipation between neighbouring cells, with non-negative weights; iii) a side-wise transfer of the dissipation to the evolved variables through the chain rule of each cell, which turns the energy defects into Bregman divergences of the single-fluid energies; iv) a thermodynamic correction of the reversible part built in the phase variables. Properties I)-V) are proved and verified numerically, including a shock tube in which the Rusanov viscosity produces negative entropy and a shock-water column interaction.

items.title: Mean Field Games for Renewable Energy Development
items.summary: We propose a mean field game (MFG) framework to model the evolution of renewable energy production in competitive electricity markets. Producers interact through the spot price while optimising their profits under production, installation, and capacity adjustment costs, as well as the generation uncertainty. We first formulate the market as an $N$-player stochastic differential game and analyse its mean field game limit as $N\to\infty$. We characterise the representative producer's optimal control via forward-backward stochastic differential equations (FBSDEs) derived from the stochastic maximum principle and determine the corresponding equilibrium spot price. We establish existence and uniqueness of solutions to the FBSDEs and prove that the MFG admits a unique equilibrium, which yields an $ε$-Nash equilibrium of the $N$-player game. We then extend the model to a Stackelberg MFG to incorporate the role of a social planner. The planner's optimisation problem leads to an extended Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) system, for which we prove existence and uniqueness of viscosity solutions. Finally, we implement a deep learning-based numerical scheme to approximate the equilibrium and investigate the impact of policy interventions on capacity dynamics. Our results highlight how optimal subsidy design depends on prevailing market conditions and can mitigate both capacity shortages and overproduction.

items.title: Characterization of spatial topological chaos for bistable lattice equation
items.summary: In this paper we extend the description of spatial topological chaos for bistable lattice equations in a small diffusion regime. We generalize the Keener's proof and show that stationary solutions are topologically conjugate to biinfinite sequences on a three-symbol alphabet. We provide a priori estimates for the values of stationary solutions and use them to show that there are exactly two monotone stationary fronts (up to a translation). Finally, we apply the localization of all stationary solutions to characterize their stability and get the existence of unique stable and unstable monotone fronts (up to a translation).

items.title: Critical branching random walks on $\mathbb{Z}^2$: local survival probabilities and Yaglom limit theorems
items.summary: We consider a branching random walk on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ with critical offspring of mean $1$ and spatial motion governed by the jumps of a lazy simple random walk. For every site $x\in\mathbb{Z}^2$, we obtain a uniform asymptotical estimate for the local survival probability, i.e., the probability that there are particles at $x$ at large time $n$. Using Stein's method, we establish a Yaglom-type theorem for the number of particles at $x$ at time $n$ when $x$ is at distance of order $\sqrt{n}$ from the origin. Moreover, at the position occupied by a typical particle at time $n$, the number of particles at that site, normalized by $\log n$, converges in law to a Gamma distribution, thereby confirming a conjecture of Lalley and Zheng [Ann. Probab. 39 (2010), 327-368]. Finally, we prove that, conditional on local survival, the total number of particles at time $n$, divided by $n$, also converges weakly to a Gamma distribution.

items.title: On the complexification of $ q $-deformations of compact semisimple Lie groups
items.summary: For the quantised algebra of functions on a simply connected compact semisimple Lie group, we study the relationship between the primitive spectrum, topologically irreducible representations by bounded operators on Hilbert spaces, and quantum holomorphic evaluations induced via the Drinfeld double. In terms of the Joseph stratification of the primitive spectrum, we prove a sharp dichotomy: primitive ideals in homogeneous strata always arise as kernels of topologically irreducible representations by bounded operators on a Hilbert space, whereas those in inhomogeneous strata do not admit any such realisations. We further show that, unlike in the classical situation, quantum holomorphic evaluations typically fail to be topologically irreducible, and that their kernels do not determine the primitive spectrum. Finally, we describe the Iwasawa decomposition of the Drinfeld double in terms of polynomial functions, extending work by Podleś-Woronowicz for the quantum Lorentz group to all complex semisimple quantum groups, and clarifying the structure of quantum holomorphic evaluations.

items.title: An introduction to algebraic groups
items.summary: We review the theory of abelian varieties and, more generally, algebraic groups, with a view toward arithmetic applications. We discuss their models over the rings of integers of number fields, their reductions modulo primes, their torsion points (together with their natural Galois action), and the interplay of these notions through characteristic polynomials of Frobenius.

items.title: On Mbekhta's conjecture and pseudo-Fredholm operators on Banach and Hilbert spaces
items.summary: We give negative answers to Mbekhta's conjecture \cite[p.~261]{Mbekhta} and to a related conjecture on pseudo-B-Fredholm operators \cite[p.~202]{AZO}. A sufficient condition for pseudo-Fredholmness on Banach spaces is established. It yields a characterization on Hilbert spaces in terms of the closedness of $\cc(T)$, $\cc(T)+\qn(T)$ and $\Ran(T)+\qn(T)$, as well as characterizations of pseudo-B-Fredholm and pseudo-B-Weyl operators on Banach spaces. A counterexample on a separable Banach space shows that the three closedness conditions do not characterize pseudo-Fredholmness in general. We also construct two operators having the same analytic core, quasinilpotent part, and kernels and ranges of all powers, although only one is pseudo-Fredholm. Moreover, a semi-B-Fredholm operator on a Banach space need not be a direct sum of a semi-Fredholm operator and a nilpotent operator, answering the question raised in \cite[p.~113]{AznayKato2023}. Finally, the three closedness conditions in the Hilbert-space characterization are shown to be independent.

items.title: Weighted configurations and the nonexistence of arithmetic ball quotient compactifications
items.summary: We prove that, for every $n\ge9$, no ordered GIT quotient of $n$ points on $\mathbb P^1$ with positive rational weights smaller than one and of total weight two is isomorphic to the Baily--Borel compactification of an arithmetic complex ball quotient. The weights may lie on stability walls, and the lattice may have torsion and ramify along divisors. No compatibility with a prescribed period map is assumed. The proof compares homomorphisms from the tangent bundle to line bundles of negative degree with normal bundles of arithmetic fixed subvarieties. We describe these homomorphisms through coincident marked points and prove vanishing statements for their kernels. The comparison, together with integrality of Chern classes and the invariant theory of finite reflection groups, gives the nonexistence theorem without a Fano assumption on the GIT quotient.

items.title: Seven ordered points and the nonexistence of arithmetic ball quotient compactifications
items.summary: We prove that the ordered GIT quotient of seven points on $\mathbb P^1$ with equal weights is not isomorphic to the Baily--Borel compactification of any arithmetic complex ball quotient. Together with our companion paper and the known positive examples, this determines the equal weight case for every $n\ge6$: such a realization exists precisely for $n=6,8$. The lattice and the algebraic isomorphism are unrestricted, and torsion and divisorial ramification are allowed. The proof combines arithmetic reductions with identities involving Chern classes of fixed subvarieties and intersection inequalities for nef divisors on the GIT quotient. The final comparison includes all fixed components and requires no bound on the degree of an individual fixed curve.

items.title: Almost Sharp Equivalence between Approximate Message Passing and Low-Degree Polynomials
items.summary: We prove a sharp lower bound for growing-degree polynomial estimation in the symmetric rank-one matrix estimation problem. The observation is \[ \boldsymbol{Y}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}} \boldsymbolθ \boldsymbolθ^{\top}+\boldsymbol{W}, \] where the coordinates of $\boldsymbolθ$ are independent with a common, fixed sub-Gaussian distribution $π_Θ$ satisfying $\mathbb E[Θ]\neq0$, and $\boldsymbol{W}$ is symmetric with independent standard Gaussian upper-triangular entries. For every such prior, we give an explicit finite-dimensional bound implying that every sequence of polynomial estimators of degree $D(n)=o(n^{1/60})$ has normalized mean-square error with limit inferior at least $\mathbb E[Θ^2]-q_{\mathsf{amp}}$, the limiting error of Bayes approximate message passing (AMP). This extends the constant-degree equivalence of Montanari and Wein~\cite{montanari2025equivalence} to growing degree under the same prior assumptions. Combined with their polynomial approximation of fixed-iteration AMP, the bound identifies the exact limiting low-degree MMSE whenever $D(n)\to\infty$ within this range. It thereby answers the growing-degree AMP-equivalence question discussed in~\cite{wein2025computational, maleki2026high} for nonzero-mean sub-Gaussian priors in the stated degree range. We also obtain a moment-dependent finite-dimensional lower bound for any nonzero-mean prior with all moments finite. The proof bounds low-degree MMSE using \emph{conditional} joint cumulants and a refined application of Jensen's inequality. The conditional cumulants are defined using an auxiliary Gaussian channel $\boldsymbol{R}$ calibrated to the AMP fixed point. This retains signal dependence that is lost in unconditional cumulant bounds and produces the cancellations needed for quantitative control as the degree grows.

items.title: Regularity, depth and Serre depth of symbolic powers of complementary edge ideals
items.summary: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph and let $I_c(G)$ denote its complementary edge ideal. In this paper, we study the Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity, the depth and Serre depth for $(S_{2})$ of the symbolic powers of $I_c(G)$. We derive explicit formulas for $\operatorname{reg} I_c(G)^{(k)}$ and $\operatorname{reg} I_c(G)^{(k)}/I_c(G)^k$ for every $k\geq1$, in terms of the number and the sizes of the connected components of $G$. As applications, we determine their asymptotic behavior, and completely characterize the symbolic powers of complementary edge ideals having linear resolutions. We then investigate the symbolic depth function $k\mapsto\operatorname{depth} S/I_c(G)^{(k)}$. We determine explicitly its values for $k=2,3,4$, and establish bounds for the asymptotic depth. More generally, for an arbitrary squarefree monomial ideal $I$, we compare the local cohomology modules of $S/I^{(k)}$ for different symbolic powers, and derive corresponding inequalities for the depth and the Serre depth. Applying this to complementary edge ideals, we obtain $\operatorname{depth} S/I_{c}(G)^{(t)}\geq\operatorname{depth} S/I_{c}(G)^{(k)}$ for $k\geq 2t-1$, despite the fact that the symbolic depth function need not be non-increasing. Finally, we characterize complementary edge ideals satisfying Serre's condition $(S_r)$, and determine the Serre depth for $(S_{2})$ of all symbolic powers of complementary edge ideals. In particular, we obtain combinatorial characterizations of Serre's condition $(S_{2})$ and of the Cohen-Macaulayness of $S/I_{c}(G)^{(k)}$ for every $k\geq 1$.

items.title: Weak action representability of $2$-nilpotent groups
items.summary: In this article, we investigate the representability of actions of the category $\mathsf{Nil}_2(\mathsf{Grp})$ of $2$-nilpotent groups. We first provide an algebraic characterisation of derived actions in $\mathsf{Nil}_2(\mathsf{Grp})$ in terms of the group $\operatorname{Aut}_c(X)$ of central automorphisms of an object $X$. We also characterise the morphisms $B \to \operatorname{Aut}_c(X)$ that define an action of $B$ on $X$ in $\mathsf{Nil}_2(\mathsf{Grp})$. We then show that $\mathsf{Nil}_2(\mathsf{Grp})$ is not action representable, and that the existence of a weak representation is related to the amalgamation property. We prove that the category $\mathsf{Nil}_2(\mathsf{Grp})$ is weakly action representable, by exhibiting a strong amalgam of a suitable family of abelian subgroups of $\operatorname{Aut}_c(X)$: an explicit weak representing object of $X$ is the abelian group $\operatorname{Hom}(X/[X,X],\operatorname{Z}(X))$. Finally, we show that $\mathsf{Nil}_2(\mathsf{Grp})$ is not locally algebraically cartesian closed.

items.title: Optimal estimates for the $\ell^p$-Lipschitz constants of deep random ReLU neural networks
items.summary: This paper studies the $\ell^p$-Lipschitz constants of ReLU neural networks $Φ: \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$ with random parameters for $p \in [1,\infty]$. The distribution of the weights follows a variant of the He initialization. In the case of zero-bias networks, we derive matching high-probability upper and lower bounds for wide networks that differ at most by an absolute constant. The bounds reveal two remarkable phenomena. First, the bounds grow root-logarithmically in terms of the depth of the net. Second, the behavior of the $\ell^p$-Lipschitz constants varies significantly between the regimes $p \in [1,2)$ and $p \in [2,\infty]$. For $p \in [2,\infty]$, the $\ell^p$-Lipschitz constant behaves similarly to $\|g\|_{p'}$, where $g \in \mathbb{R}^d$ is a standard Gaussian vector and $1/p + 1/p' = 1$. In contrast, for $p \in [1,2)$, the $\ell^p$-Lipschitz constant aligns more closely with $\|g\|_2$. For networks with possibly nonzero biases, we obtain the same lower bounds without assumptions on the bias distributions. For symmetric bias distributions with bounded densities, we also derive high-probability upper bounds for the $\ell^p$-Lipschitz constants. For fixed sub-exponential bias distributions, these upper bounds differ from the lower bounds by a factor that has square-root dependence on the depth and logarithmic dependence on the width.

items.title: Models of Arbitrary Sets
items.summary: There is a growing literature on arbitrary objects as other types of mathematical objects, besides particular mathematical objects. In this paper we study arbitrary sets in the context of ZFC set theory. An arbitrary object is one that is determined by a state space across which it varies and by its instantiations. We compare two semantic strategies. First, we analyse the possibility of modeling arbitrary sets using direct powers of a ZFC structure. This yields a natural setting, but one where Extensionality and, crucially, the full Separation scheme fail. Second, we consider structures composed of arbitrary sets using a direct power construction evaluated in a Boolean-valued semantics. Within this setting, we develop the cumulative hierarchy of arbitrary sets, arbitrary ordinals, cardinals, and filtrations of the structure of arbitrary sets. The final section develops a combinatorial interpretation in terms of independent assignments across a fixed state space. Its connection with the iterative conception is then discussed.

items.title: A Complexity Dichotomy for Edge Subdivision to $H$-Free Graphs
items.summary: For a fixed graph $H$, \HFS\ asks whether at most $k$ edge subdivisions can make an input graph contain no induced copy of $H$. We establish a complexity dichotomy for every fixed nonempty $H$: the problem is polynomial-time solvable if every component of $H$ is a subdivided star or a subdivided bistar and at most one component is a subdivided bistar; it is NP-complete otherwise. In every NP-complete case, the Exponential Time Hypothesis rules out a $2^{o(k)}n^{O(1)}$-time algorithm. For every fixed $H$, the problem admits a $2^{O(k)}n^{O(1)}$-time algorithm.

items.title: The Smith-Toda complex V(4) exists for p >= 11
items.summary: We show that the Smith-Toda complex V(4) exists for all primes p >= 11. This improves on the recently announced result by OpenAI that V(4) exists at the prime 1009.

items.title: Regular Additive Scalar Invariants of ${\mathcal N}=1$ Hyperbolic Spin Supertriangles
items.summary: We classify regular cyclic scalar invariants of non-degenerate hyperbolic ${\mathcal N}=1$ spin supertriangles which are additive under geodesic subdivision. After fixing the spin lift, the common-first gauge (introduced in earlier work by the second-named author and further developed here) gives a complete $3|4$ modulus of such supertriangles.. The space of additive scalar invariants is proved to have superdimension $3|1$: ordinary hyperbolic area in degree zero, two even generators in degree two, and one odd generator in degree three; the degree-one and degree-four sectors vanish. One degree-two generator is the fermionic first variation of body area, equivalently the nilpotent correction from ordinary body angle defect to super angle defect. The degree-three generator changes sign under reversal of the spin lift, while the other generators are fixed, so ordinary supertriangles carry only three even invariants.

items.title: Non-Existence of thick bubble rings at low Weber numbers
items.summary: We examine the existence of thick bubble rings within the framework of the free-boundary capillary Euler equations, focusing on the regime of low Weber numbers. Although spheroidal bubbles are known to approach a spherical shape in this limit, the possibility of thick bubble rings persisting at low Weber numbers has remained uncertain. In contrast to the ordinary Euler equations, which admit thick vortex ring solutions, our analysis reveals that the free-boundary capillary Euler equations do not support thick bubble rings at low Weber numbers. This distinction highlights the significant impact of surface tension on the behavior of vortex rings in the capillary regime.

items.title: Synthesis of the Transient Behaviour of Optimization Algorithms for Strongly Convex Objective Functions
items.summary: We study the transient behavior of first-order optimization methods for unconstrained minimization of smooth and strongly convex objective functions. These methods are modelled as linear systems over finite-time intervals embedded in feedback with the gradient nonlinearity. By characterizing the function class through discrete-time Zames-Falb integral quadratic constraints, we employ a robust $\mathcal{H}_2$ control framework to obtain convex semidefinite programs certifying tight worst-case bounds on the terminal distance to the optimizer. Building on the same formulation, we derive a convex synthesis procedure for a transient-optimal method that achieves the optimal finite-horizon bounds and guarantees error reduction over any prescribed number of steps. The framework naturally extends to delayed gradient measurements, enabling both transient performance analysis and synthesis of optimal algorithms under feedback delays.

items.title: SALTO: Solver-Anchored Lifted Transfer Operators for Nonlinear Event Inference
items.summary: Learned dynamical models can accurately predict trajectories while producing unreliable sensitivities when differentiated or transposed, limiting their use in inverse problems and scientific decision-making. Classical adjoints provide exact local derivatives, but a single adjoint cannot represent the nonlinear response of a system to a family of finite-amplitude perturbations. We introduce SALTO (Solver-Anchored Lifted Transfer Operators), a Koopman-based framework for inferring finite-amplitude sources. In the lifted space, the nonlinear dynamics are approximated by a linear propagator, and its transpose carries each sensor backward in a single solve. The result is a reusable lifted adjoint that predicts the measurement produced by any candidate localized event with one encoder pass and an inner product. To give the model the simulator's exact local behavior, SALTO imposes three structural constraints: it anchors the physical-state dynamics to the simulator's linearized propagator, centers the learned observables so that they vanish to second order at the reference state, and uses a block-triangular lifted propagator. These constraints guarantee that the model reduces to the simulator's tangent dynamics and classical adjoint as the amplitude vanishes, while the learned observables carry only the finite-amplitude correction. On three nonlinear PDE systems, SALTO predicts the measurements of finite-amplitude sources to within 2-8% where the classical adjoint is in error by 41-165%, recovers source position and intensity from sparse sensors nearly as accurately as inversion through the solver, and samples the joint posterior of two interacting sources, matching the solver's posterior on reaction-diffusion at a twentieth of its cost. One trained model serves new sensor layouts and measurement times with a single backward solve.

items.title: Multilevel Gaussian Processes with Applications to Inverse Problems
items.summary: We present a multilevel Gaussian process (GP) regression framework for approximating functions that are accessible only through a hierarchy of approximations of increasing accuracy and computational cost. One example is the response surface of a parametrized partial differential equation, where the hierarchy arises from the resolution of the numerical solver. Modeling level increments independently with Matérn-kernel GPs and allocating samples flexibly across discretization levels yields substantial computational savings over single-level GP regression. We derive $L^2$ convergence rates for the posterior mean and variance, accounting for maximum likelihood estimation of the marginal variance and for kernel misspecification. When increment regularity or solver cost is unknown a priori, an adaptive sequential-design algorithm with cost-adapted active learning criteria allocates samples across levels. We apply the surrogate to Bayesian inverse problems, for which Hellinger distance bounds between the true and approximate posteriors are known. Numerical experiments illustrate the theoretical rates and the resulting computational savings.

items.title: A $\mathrm{GL}_3$ level analog of Selberg's result for $S(t)$
items.summary: Let $π$ be a spherical cuspidal $\mathrm{GL}_3$ newform of prime level $N$ and trivial central character, and define $S(t,π)=π^{-1}\arg L(1/2+\textrm{i}t,π)$. Assuming the generalized Riemann hypothesis for $L(s,π)$, we establish an asymptotic formula for each fixed weighted moment of $S(t,π)$ as $N\to\infty$, for fixed $t>0$. Consequently, under the same weights, $S(t,π)/\sqrt{\log\log N}$ converges in distribution to a centered Gaussian distribution of variance $1/(2π^2)$. The key input is a weighted orthogonality formula derived from the Kuznetsov formula of prime level.

items.title: On an Instance of the Small Cohen-Macaulay Conjecture II
items.summary: We show that any $d$-dimensional local ring $A$ with a dualizing complex, $\mathrm{depth} A=d-1$, and cyclic deficiency module $K^{d-1}(A)$ admits a maximal Cohen--Macaulay module. It is constructed as the unique nonzero cohomology module of the cone of the derived morphism induced by a surjection $A\to K^{d-1}(A)$. This gives new cases of the small Cohen--Macaulay conjecture.
