The training objective is primarily the minimization of MSE, with the variants that jointly impose surface smoothness, and that penalize the presence of static-arbitrage, which are all economically meaningful constraints. Across in-sample and out-of-sample stocks, our diffusion model outperforms the VolGAN benchmark in reducing arbitrage violations, improving stock risk prediction, and aligning explained variance ratios by the first three principal components. The fact that the model extrapolates well to stocks that are excluded from training indicates that the learned dynamics can be shared across stocks. These findings support a universal conditional diffusion as a credible framework for multi-stock implied volatility surface scenario generation.

items.title: Same Text, Different Numbers: The Divergence of LLM-Based Measures
items.summary: Researchers increasingly use generative large language models (LLMs) to convert corporate text into empirical variables. We examine the extent to which LLM-based textual measures are invariant to model choice using thirteen measures, including sentiment, management clarity, uncertainty, answer specificity, and climate and political risk. Seven LLMs from different providers score earnings call transcripts of S&P 500 companies on these constructs. Cross-model rank correlations average only 0.52, and transcript-level differences common across providers account for only 34% of total score variation. Cross-model disagreement does not predict subsequent analyst or market disagreement, consistent with a substantial model-specific component rather than common ambiguity in the underlying disclosure. Model choice significantly affects downstream inference, with coefficient magnitudes, signs, and statistical significance varying substantially across models. Averaging across providers makes transcript rankings more stable for most constructs, but score levels remain sensitive to the models included in the ensemble. LLM-generated variables should therefore be treated as model-contingent measurements and validated across providers.

items.title: Financial Fragility in Societies of LLM Agents: Coordination Failures and Stabilizing Mechanisms
items.summary: Individually protective decisions can produce avoidable collective failures. As large language model (LLM) agents take on greater roles in financial decision-making, financial AI safety must therefore be considered not only at the level of individual agents, but also at the level of the systems they jointly create. We study this problem with FRAIL, a controlled experimental framework that places LLM agents in three dynamic financial environments---bank runs, debt rollover, and reward crowdfunding---where agents' decisions reshape the financial conditions faced by others. Across seven leading LLMs, we find widespread collective fragility even when no agent is instructed to destabilize the system: 77\% of baseline bank-run episodes and 83\% of debt-rollover episodes end in failure. We then compare three interaction mechanisms based on compensated commitments, centralized commitment agreements, and participant-led coalitions. All three improve aggregate outcomes, but no single mechanism performs best across all financial structures. Across mechanisms, successful stabilization shares a common temporal pattern: broad commitment forms early, before defensive behavior becomes self-reinforcing. Our findings show that individually capable agents do not automatically form safe financial systems, highlighting system-level evaluation and interaction design as central problems for financial AI safety. Code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/FinFrail-CF26.

items.title: A note on markets with semi-static trading strategies
items.summary: We consider a discrete-time financial market model where, in addition to finitely many dynamically traded assets, there are also (possibly infinitely many) static options to choose from. We introduce the concept of small cones of random variables and present a sufficient condition for the attainable positions in the market to be closed in probability. A fundamental theorem of asset pricing is shown in the present context. Utility maximization will also be considered. We will provide economically meaningful examples of infinite dimensional small cones to demonstrate the pertinence of our approach.

items.title: Multi-Jurisdictional Legal Identity Assurance for Capability Gating: A Design-Science Proposal for Tiered, Reusable Identity Assurance of Natural, Juridical, and Machine Entities
items.summary: Identity assurance is the cost a digital system pays for dishonesty and uncertainty: it exists to make acts attributable when not everyone can be trusted at their word. A common way to pay that cost is flat maximum verification, asking each participant to meet a single high level of identification at entry, before any capability is exercised. Paid on everyone, it over-collects, excludes participants who cannot meet a bar they never needed to clear, taxes every interaction with the cost of the rarest high-risk case, and binds the strength of identification to the activity it unlocks. Existing frameworks compound this by fixing a small number of per-credential levels inside a single legal space and binding each verification to the institution that performed it, leaving cross-border reuse and the tension between data erasure and evidentiary retention unaddressed. This paper develops, as a design-science proposal, a tiered and reusable model of identity assurance for natural, juridical, and machine entities across jurisdictions. Reading the problem through systems theory, where a system changes only when an entity acts, the model holds the assurance state apart from the capability gate that consumes it, so that identity demand follows the act and the weight of its consequences rather than mere presence: a participant may take part with minimal disclosure and supply more only as an act requires. It comprises a typed entity taxonomy, a two-axis coordinate of disclosed assertion scope and source of information, jurisdiction as a time-indexed attribute of the entity, and reliance recorded as bitemporal, liability-allocated, point-in-time snapshots. Requirements are derived from anti-money-laundering, electronic-identity, and data-protection law, and the proposal is evaluated against flat maximum verification, per-credential level-of-assurance designs, and institutional reusable-KYC reliance.

items.title: PixSim: a calibrated open-source simulator of instant-payment fraud, recovery and interdiction under analyst capacity constraints
items.summary: Brazil's Pix settles about 5.9 billion instant, irreversible transfers a month. A fraudulent transfer can be recovered only while the funds remain in a traceable account, and in 2025 the Central Bank's recovery mechanism (MED) returned 9% of accepted contested value. Interdiction therefore has to happen before settlement, by routing each transaction to pass, human review or block, under a finite analyst team and a regulatory hold window. To our knowledge no public simulator jointly models irreversible settlement, a regulated recovery mechanism, downstream fund dispersal and capacity-constrained review. We present PixSim, an open-source simulator of the Pix rail with these elements, calibrated to Banco Central do Brasil open data, with every parameter sourced, calibrated to one published observable, or registered as an assumption. With the model frozen, full-scale runs reproduce the 2025 recovery rate within 0.006 and its decomposition within 0.02; the February-April 2026 window is reported as a misfit and the May 2026 tracing regime as a projection. On a benchmark with a payer-side scorer, four reference policies and ten scenarios, within the simulated mule model: recovery after settlement is constrained by dispersal speed; staffing by the arrival profile cuts a fixed rule's alert expiry from 52% to 2% at constant hours; halving the team removes a fixed threshold-and-block rule's advantage over a queue-aware rule, on loss and on loss plus false-block harm (+0.106 of victim value, positive on all twenty paired seeds), while a reversal at two thirds of the team was not confirmed on independent seeds; and a synthetic scorer of held-out AUC 0.82 cuts lost value by about a quarter. Code and data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22948895

items.title: SPX-VIX Risk Computations Via Perturbed Optimal Transport
items.summary: We propose a model independent framework for generating SPX and VIX risk scenarios based on a joint optimal transport calibration of their market smiles. Starting from the entropic martingale optimal transport formulation of Guyon, we introduce a perturbation methodology that computes sensitivities of the calibrated coupling using a Fisher information linearization. This allows risk to be generated without performing a full recalibration after market shocks. We further introduce a dimension reduction method based on perturbed optimal transport that produces fast and stable risk estimates while preserving the structural properties of the calibrated model. The approach is combined with Skew Stickiness Ratio(SSR) dynamics to translate SPX shocks into perturbations of forward variance and VIX distributions. Numerical experiments show that the proposed method produces accurate risk estimates relative to full recalibration while being computationally much faster. A backtesting study also demonstrates improved hedging performance compared with stochastic local volatility models.

items.title: On the Impact of Insurance on Households Susceptible to Random Proportional Losses: An Analysis of Poverty Trapping
items.summary: The trapping probability is studied for households' capital assuming that losses are proportional to the accumulated capital. We consider households without insurance and those purchasing proportional insurance. Parameter conditions under which poverty trapping is not certain in both cases are derived. For the uninsured model, a new closed-form expression for the trapping probability is obtained when the remaining proportion of capital after a loss has a beta distribution, showing that the trapping probability decays algebraically as the initial capital increases. When insurance is purchased and the remaining proportion is uniformly distributed, the trapping probability is computed by solving a non-local integro-differential equation. Our results show that insurance can prevent otherwise certain trapping in some cases, although it may increase trapping risk for households with initial capital barely above the poverty line, while reducing trapping risk for households with higher initial capital.

items.title: Two-Regime Risk Measures under Convex Loss
items.summary: We study a two-regime summary of a real-valued loss distribution. The two representative levels and the boundary between them are chosen by minimizing a convex residual loss. When the distribution has an atom at the boundary, assigning that atom to the lower or upper regime can give different optimized costs. Taking the better whole-atom assignment yields the lower-semicontinuous cutoff profile. We prove epi-convergence of this profile under a loss-adapted \(ψ\)-weak topology and obtain convergence of minimum values and outer stability of optimal cutoff sets. Under a unique finite atom-free limiting cutoff, positive regime masses, and unique conditional centers, the two fitted levels and a canonical one-jump representation converge as well. We also examine the resulting summary from the viewpoint of monetary risk axioms, establish explicit failures of external monotonicity and subadditivity, and give finite-support algorithms with conditional error control. A four-scenario model illustrates the cutoff geometry and the role of ties and atoms.

items.title: The Cross-Section of Stock Returns and AI Exposure
items.summary: We study 380 trillion tokens of realized AI consumption across more than four hundred LLMs. We build a high-frequency AI factor and show that a long-short strategy based on firms' AI exposure earns significantly positive returns. The average strategy return is larger based on intensive, frontier-oriented AI consumption but smaller based on casual or open-weight usage. Internationally, the return spread is significant in developed countries but insignificant in emerging markets. Examining occupational AI exposure, we find more positive exposure in occupations intensive in nonroutine interactive tasks and more negative exposure in those intensive in nonroutine analytical tasks.

items.title: Insider Purchases Far Below the 52-Week High: Decomposing the Disclosure Reaction in Microcap Equities
items.summary: Purchases reported under transaction code P on SEC Form 4 by insiders of U.S. equities with an estimated filing-date capitalization of USD 30 million to USD 500 million (13,534 lines, 1,192 issuers, 2018-2024) are followed by a first-day abnormal return that rises steeply with the stock's distance below its 52-week high: 4.13% in the quintile farthest below the high against 0.86% nearest it (two-way clustered t = 9.77); random non-event days of the same issuers show 0.14%. Five tests with decision rules fixed in advance characterize the gradient. Most of it is scale: the beaten-down stocks are 3.10 times as volatile, and with a full set of controls the raw gap fails its pre-specified bar (0.94 points, t = 2.11). Per unit of the stock's own volatility the reaction is 2.51 times as large far below the high (t = 7.49), 1.28 to 3.50 on other estimators, though a variance-weighted slope shows none. The gradient is larger than for insider sales by the same issuers and for positive earnings surprises as a class; against the strongest surprises the difference is imprecise. Dropping purchases with a concurrent 8-K leaves the raw gradient intact (t = 7.13), but the per-risk gradient no longer clears the controls (t = 2.52). The reaction runs for two to three sessions; the 29-day drift is imprecise (two-way t = 1.70) and a calendar-time portfolio that skips the first day earns no significant alpha. The analysis quantifies sensitivity to price adjustment and benchmark specification: mixing price bases misassigns run-up buckets, and carrying the estimation-window intercept supplies 57% of the 30-day gradient under that benchmark. A gradient-boosting classifier (test AUC 0.676) is indistinguishable from logistic regression. A separate large-cap extension schedules USD 29,075,559 a year of buyer-cluster flow but fails every matched-comparison gate.

items.title: Affine Pricing Models from Group Quantization and Holonomy
items.summary: The analytic tractability of affine pricing models is usually expressed through two complementary formulations: a coordinate-space pricing operator and an exponential-affine transform representation governed by generalized Riccati equations. We develop \emph{Affine Holonomy Group Quantization} (AHGQ) as a geometric framework in which these two formulations arise from the same underlying structure. The construction separates the affine pricing symbol into a homogeneous quadratic sector and a complementary affine sector. The first generates a finite-dimensional symplectic transport and a centrally extended Lie group, while the second is represented by a multiplicative holonomy carried by a thin-path groupoid. Their combination determines an affine Poincaré--Cartan form. Its characteristic dynamics reduce in momentum variables to the generalized Riccati system and its scalar amplitude, whereas the coordinate representation recovers the standard affine pricing operator. Representative Gaussian and square-root models illustrate the construction. The contribution is structural: AHGQ gives a common geometric origin to the coordinate and transform representations of continuous-path, time-homogeneous affine pricing models.

items.title: Stability of Change-of-Numéraire Reweighting: An Exact Wasserstein Boundary
items.summary: Reweighting a probability law by a positive numéraire and pushing forward the payoff-to-numéraire ratio yields the change-of-numéraire reweighting: the swap-rate law under the annuity measure, the numéraire-inversion involution of martingale optimal transport, and the population form of self-normalized importance sampling. We characterize exactly when it is Wasserstein-stable. Along weakly convergent inputs with uniformly integrable numéraires and a strictly positive limiting numéraire mean, convergence of the reweighted laws is equivalent to a uniform integrability condition, computed under the inputs, on one explicit family in the payoff and numéraire. At first order the numéraire cancels, the sole obstruction being payoff mass where the numéraire vanishes; absent such mass, prices and first moments pass to the limit under a uniformly integrable payoff alone, with no assumption on the reciprocal numéraire. Two-atom examples with bounded inputs attain the threshold exactly. Applications characterize a standing moment assumption in the transport literature and delimit which annuity-measure statistics survive.

items.title: SENSE: Semantic Neural Speech Synthesis from Brain Dynamics via Spatial Graph Encoding
items.summary: Reconstructing speech from non-invasive brain signals offers a promising pathway for restoring communication in individuals who are cognitively intact but unable to speak. Existing EEG-to-speech approaches formulate this task as acoustic reconstruction, optimizing waveform fidelity while ignoring whether the generated speech preserves high-level semantic content. In this work, we revisit this formulation and argue that EEG signals carry not only acoustic but also semantic information. We identify two key limitations of prior methods: (1) the neglect of spatial relationships between EEG electrodes, and (2) the failure to exploit the semantic structure of the N400 paradigm, where congruent and incongruent trials reflect distinct semantic processing. We propose SENSE(Semantic-EEG Neural Speech SynthEsis), which combines a graph-based EEG encoder over electrode geometry with EEG Semantic Conditioning (ESC), aligning EEG to a pretrained semantic space using only congruent trials. On the N400 dataset, SENSE consistently outperforms prior methods on both acoustic and semantic metrics, and model-internal channel attribution suggests distributed reliance on auditory, sensorimotor, and centro-parietal regions, consistent with known speech-perception neuroscience. In the unseen-subject setting, SENSE trained on only two subjects already surpasses the strongest baseline trained on all eighteen subjects in word error rate, and matches it on acoustic metrics with as few as eight subjects.

items.title: The Impact of Demand Forecasting on Delay and Jitter in DVB-Based Beam-Hopping LEO Networks
items.summary: In LEO satellite networks utilizing beam hopping (BH), resource allocation plans must be committed well in advance. This inherent operational delay necessitates predicting future user demand during the planning phase. Such predictive agility is particularly crucial for military applications, where unpredictable tactical environments demand low-latency, resilient communication links. However, existing forecasting models are typically evaluated based on standalone accuracy, ignoring their cross-layer impact on overall network performance. To address this gap, we evaluate two distinct demand forecasting solutions within a comprehensive, full-stack LEO satellite simulation compliant with DVB-S2X standards. Beyond prediction accuracy, we examine how incorporating user demand forecasts into BH plan generation impacts key network metrics, particularly delay and jitter. We evaluate these forecasting solutions alongside a static allocation baseline. Our results demonstrate that forecast-based dynamic planning reduces delay by 10-40% across the beams under certain load conditions compared to static allocation methods. Crucially, marginal improvements in predictive accuracy do not translate into proportional network metric gains. While the evaluated forecasting solutions differ by 14-16% in Normalized Mean Square Error (NMSE), this discrepancy yields less than a 1% reduction in delay and produces nearly identical jitter characteristics. These findings suggest that when designing user demand forecasting solutions for practical LEO deployments, prioritizing system scalability may be more valuable than chasing minor accuracy enhancements.

items.title: Lyapunov Exponents in Power Systems: A Survey of Theory and Applications in Stability, Control, Forecasting, and Protection
items.summary: Lyapunov exponents (LEs) are fundamental metrics from nonlinear dynamical systems theory that quantify the average exponential rate of divergence or convergence of nearby trajectories in phase space. Over the past three decades, LEs have emerged as powerful tools across a wide range of power system problems, including transient and voltage stability assessment, chaos detection and mitigation, short-term load and renewable energy forecasting, and fault diagnosis. This paper presents a comprehensive review of these applications, covering more than 165 publications spanning from the early demonstrations of chaos in simplified machine models (1990s) to the most recent data-driven and machine-learning-augmented approaches applied to inverter-based resource (IBR)-dominated grids (2024--2026). The review is organized into four principal application domains: (i) stability analysis and real-time monitoring, (ii) chaos characterization and control, (iii) forecasting and predictability analysis, and (iv) protection, fault diagnosis, and condition monitoring. For each domain, we trace the evolution of methods, compare model-based and data-driven LE estimation strategies, identify key benchmarks and validation gaps, and outline the most pressing open research problems.

items.title: Anytime-Valid Certification of Robustness Margins for Safe Control via E-Values
items.summary: Robust control uses the error between a known model and the true system as a robustness margin. However, this error is usually unknown: conservative estimates restrict feasibility and performance, while underestimates can result in violations of the control property. We estimate this robustness margin from online data using e-values, a statistical tool for hypothesis testing, in the setting of discrete-time control barrier functions (CBFs). Here, we measure the robustness margin as the difference between the observed CBF and the model-based CBF prediction. We then design a robust CBF controller in three steps by: (1) selecting a set of candidate margins, (2) obtaining validity certificates for these candidates via sequential tests based on e-values, and (3) updating the CBF controller with the smallest certified candidate. The deployed tests accumulate evidence against the hypothesis that an exceedance risk, the probability of the robustness margin exceeding the candidate margin, remains at or above a pre-specified failure probability $α$. Our tests are anytime valid and thus enable the use of certified candidates in the CBF controller, guaranteeing that the probability that the exceedance risk of a certified margin exceeds $α$ is at most a user-chosen confidence $δ$. We validate our approach on navigation problems across different environments with visualizations in NVIDIA Isaac Sim.

items.title: MIXSim: A multiclass first order traffic model with composition-dependent dynamics for mixed-autonomy urban networks
items.summary: This paper presents a novel multiclass first order macroscopic traffic model for mixed-autonomy in signalized urban networks, called MIXSim. Human driven vehicles (HDVs) and Connected and Automated Vehicles (CAVs) are represented as separate classes while origin-destination information is retained through commodity specific states. The local vehicle class composition and class specific driving behaviour characteristics determine the parameters of a composition-dependent triangular fundamental diagram. At signalized intersections, the composition of movement demand additionally determines the saturation flow rate, while the realized movement flow is constrained by demand, effective green time, and downstream receiving capacity. Numerical experiments investigate different CAV penetration levels and CAV time gaps, together with alternative signal control strategies. The numerical experiments illustrate how changes in CAV penetration and CAV time gap affect network performance under the tested conditions, and demonstrate the use of MIXSim for comparing signal control strategies across different mixed traffic regimes.

items.title: Packet Loss Analysis Under Doppler Effects and Reinforcement-Learning-Based Resource Allocation for Direct-to-Satellite LoRaWAN
items.summary: Long range wide area network (LoRaWAN) has a long communication range and low power consumption, making it a potential technology for direct-to-satellite (DtS) Internet of Things (IoT) connectivity. However, packet collisions and Doppler impairments brought on by satellite motion can greatly increase the packet loss ratio (PLR) in large-scale DtS-IoT networks. In this paper, we study resource allocation in DtSIoT LoRaWAN by first developing an analytical PLR model that simultaneously takes Doppler impairments and packet collisions in the temporal and frequency domains into account. In order to maximize resource allocation, the generated PLR is then used as the reward function for two reinforcement learning (RL) schemes: deep Q-network (DQN) and proximal policy optimization (PPO). Simulation results validate the analytical PLR model against Monte Carlo simulations and demonstrate significant improvements over random resource allocation. At a target PLR of 3*10^-2, while random allocation supports only 100 end devices (EDs), PPO and DQN support approximately 650 and 690 EDs, respectively, representing nearly a seven-fold increase. Furthermore, for 800 EDs, PPO and DQN increase the total number of transmitted packets by 106.7% and 88.0%, respectively, compared with random allocation.

items.title: Public Battery Field Data
items.summary: Battery systems and algorithms are developed and evaluated primarily on laboratory cycling data, but fielded battery systems are subjected to duty cycles, temperatures, and measurement conditions that cannot be reproduced in a lab. Field data from batteries in service has begun to appear in public releases attached to individual papers, but each release has its own format, units, labels, and other gaps that make it difficult to compare against others. We present a curated collection of 35 public field-data releases from 27 research groups, covering applications that span passenger EVs, buses, light electric mobility, grid-scale storage, distributed storage, consumer electronics, industrial robotics and satellites. Where the releases are complete enough to measure, this heterogeneous collection contains 256 GB of data from at least 149,188 lithium-ion cells, 3,187 batteries, 115.6 MWh of energy storage capacity, and 3,040 unit-years of service. Critically, it also contains 6,465 labeled or reported faults, which provide greater visibility into what real battery performance and safety issues look like outside the lab. We release a public repository of metadata and code for each of the field datasets. For each dataset it provides a registry entry with sources, license and access links, checksums to confirm a download is complete, a metadata table, and code for how to load it. We also report where released datasets differ from their papers. We hope the collection can help serve researchers (human or otherwise) as a useful platform for improving battery field diagnostics, fault detection and health estimation. Better field evidence can also feed back to improve manufacturing quality, inform second-life screening and residual-value estimates, and broadly accelerate electrification.

items.title: Evolution Toward Sensing-Enabled RAN: Practical Bistatic Sensing via Uplink
items.summary: This paper considers uplink channel state information (CSI)-based sensing as an opportunistic approach to enabling sensing in cellular networks, with minimum required modifications to the infrastructure. A practical sensing signal processing procedure is presented, combining 5G positioning function with multi-antenna array processing for passive target localization. The approach is validated through simulation and practical experiments with a software-defined radio-based setup, utilizing open-source software frameworks and commercially available hardware components. Results demonstrate feasibility of the uplink CSI-based sensing for detection, localization and tracking of moving targets over local areas.

items.title: Net-Zero Power UAVs: Facilitating Quantum HRLLC in Multi-Hop UAV Repeaters
items.summary: In this paper, we propose a novel joint optimization framework for autonomous, quantum-enabled UAV repeater networks designed to support hyper-reliable low-latency communications (HRLLC) in challenging environments such as post-explosion chemical plant operations. The proposed system uses a symmetric dual-UAV architecture with three sequential quantum channels operating under strict energy harvesting (EH) constraints. We formulate a highly challenging non-convex mixed-integer non-linear programming (MINLP) problem. This model jointly determines qubit allocation, 2-D uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) spatial positioning (distance and altitude), and transmit powers to minimize the total decoding error. Crucially, our framework explicitly models real-world quantum physics, including decoherence, gate imperfections, and entanglement degradation. Since the objective function is demonstrably non-convex, to efficiently solve the MINLP, we propose a quantum-resource-optimized GA (QRO-GA). The results of our numerical simulations show that the QRO-GA yields better results than benchmark methods and it is highly efficient, with the convergence speed significantly increasing with the total qubit allocation. Convergence is achieved in as few as 5 iterations for higher qubit allocation. Moreover, the results reveal a critical U-shaped tradeoff, proving that an optimal latency distribution within a strict $80\ μ$s transmission window is strictly required to maintain HRLLC reliability. In addition, we find that the QRO-GA successfully optimizes the 2-D UAV positioning to minimize total decoding error. Finally, it balances consumed and harvested power to achieve net-zero power UAVs system.

items.title: Exploiting the Flexibility of LLM Inference for Frequency Regulation Service
items.summary: While the widespread deployment of Large Language Models (LLMs) has significantly driven up power demands in computing clusters, the unique execution characteristics of LLM inference offer a novel opportunity to utilize these clusters as controllable loads. In this paper, we investigate the potential of LLM inference cluster to provide frequency regulation services through inference request scheduling. First, we model the problem as a hierarchical Markov decision process that includes request-to-replica dispatching and token-level resource allocation. Then, we introduce a reward redistribution network to address the temporal asynchrony between millisecond-level scheduling decisions and second-level frequency regulation signals. Furthermore, we develop an optimization framework based on a mean-field approximation to enable coordination among a large number of replicas under high request concurrency. Simulations using real-world data demonstrate that the proposed approach accurately tracks frequency regulation signals without compromising service-level objectives.

items.title: QIEN: Quantum-Inspired Energy-Neutral UAV Trajectory for WPT-Enabled Industrial HRLLC
items.summary: This paper introduces Quantum-Inspired Energy-Neutral (QIEN) UAV Trajectory for WPT-Enabled Industrial HRLLC, a novel framework for mobility-integrated trajectory and resource optimization in solar-powered uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) relay systems supporting autonomous mining robots in post-disaster environments. We formulate a mixed-integer nonlinear program (MINLP) that jointly optimizes UAV trajectory, finite blocklength allocation, transmit power, and wireless power transfer (WPT) over discrete time horizons to maximize aggregate data throughput. The system operates under strict extreme hyper-reliable low-latency communication (HRLLC) constraints, energy sustainability requirements via solar harvesting, and continuous robot power delivery. To solve this large-scale optimization problem, QIEN employs a hybrid Cooperative Quantum-behaved Particle Swarm Optimization (Co-QPSO) algorithm using quantum tunneling mechanisms and a heterogeneous swarm architecture. Our simulation results demonstrate that the proposed QIEN framework significantly outperforms benchmark algorithms, achieving successful convergence while maintaining energy-neutral operation and satisfying all reliability, power, and mobility constraints.

items.title: Diversifying Moving Target Defense Against Adaptive Attacks Through Factorized Diffusion
items.summary: Proactive defense offers a means to enhance power-system cybersecurity through controlled modifications of system configurations. One example is moving target defense (MTD), which uses distributed flexible AC transmission system (D-FACTS) devices to perturb transmission-line reactances against stealthy false data injection attacks. Existing MTD methods primarily rely on deterministic optimization, producing a single perturbation plan for each operating condition. However, repeated or highly correlated plans may expose predictable system configurations that attackers can learn and exploit. To address this limitation, this paper reformulates MTD as a conditional generative problem that produces diverse, secure, and physically feasible perturbation candidates. Learning such a distribution is challenging because MTD decisions jointly involve selecting branches, determining perturbation magnitudes, and coordinating adjustments across the network. To make this problem tractable, we factorize the decision distribution into three sequential conditional stages: branch selection, magnitude allocation, and continuous refinement. Graph-conditioned diffusion models are employed to capture the discrete and continuous decisions while accounting for network dependencies. Furthermore, a - objective is incorporated into diffusion training to favor candidates with desirable defense effectiveness and operational costs. Numerical studies on the IEEE 118- and 300-bus systems show that the proposed framework achieves AC feasibility comparable to that of optimization-based MTD baselines and higher - values, while reducing online computation time by an order of magnitude. The generated candidate pool remains effective under changing operating conditions and device availability, providing diverse high-value alternatives for flexible online cyber defense.

items.title: Advances in Wavelet Denoising for Communication Signals: From Parameter Selection Toward Data-Driven Optimization
items.summary: Wavelet denoising suppresses nonstationary, impulsive, and interference-like disturbances in communication signals, but efficacy depends on coupled choices of transform, mother wavelet, decomposition level, thresholding rule, and shrinkage function. Pairing communication experiments with a PRISMA-aligned synthesis of 2020-2025 studies from ten sources, coded by parameter focus and domain (biomedical, industrial, geophysical, communication), this review traces a shift from defaults to similarity-, sparsity-, entropy-, energy-, sub-band-SNR-, and task-loss-driven selection, but finds communication evidence scarce. We benchmark DWT, SWT, and WPT on an impulsive-noise OFDM channel under SNR gain, MSE, BER, EVM, and real-time feasibility, with Friedman and Wilcoxon tests, efficiency-index ranking, and assessment of embedded DSP/FPGA constraints. As waveform-fidelity gains need not improve hard-decision performance, the Unified Decision Framework prioritises receiver-level validation over fidelity surrogates, validated on synthetic pilot-aided OFDM and measured IEEE 802.11n channels. On the synthetic link, the configuration attains the lowest channel-estimation NMSE, significantly outperforms a fixed-parameter wavelet $(p < 10^{-11})$, and is statistically indistinguishable from the strongest classical baseline in BER; on measured channels it attains the lowest BER and EVM. The supported claim is the lowest estimation error at statistically equivalent bit-error performance, and it is conditional on the disturbance being structured or impulsive, since under AWGN alone wavelet thresholding yields no systematic BER improvement. Within these limits the framework generalises to held-out data and adapts to the observed channel, recasting wavelet denoising into a reproducible, communication-aware design methodology extensible to deep-unfolding architectures.

items.title: Distributed Online Learning for Time-Critical Communication in 6G Industrial Subnetworks
items.summary: Reliable and timely delivery of emergency alarms is critical for 6G industrial in-X subnetworks, particularly in dense and dynamic environments where multiple devices may simultaneously detect the same event and contend for limited radio resources. This scenario, known as medium access with a shared message, poses significant challenges for conventional random access protocols due to collisions and stringent trans- mission deadlines. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a distributed deep contextual-bandit-based random access pro- tocol that minimizes the probability of alarm delivery deadline violations. The proposed protocol enables each local access point (LAP) to autonomously learn its transmission strategy through a lightweight deep neural network (DNN), without requiring knowledge of the number of active LAPs or explicit inter-LAP coordination. A contention-signature acquisition mechanism is introduced to provide contextual information about network contention, enabling distributed and adaptive channel-access decisions. Moreover, an online learning mechanism allows LAPs to continuously refine their transmission strategies based on feedback from previous alarm transmissions. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed protocol outperforms benchmark random access schemes, particularly under high-contention con- ditions, improving the probability of timely alarm delivery by at least 8% with 30 subnetworks and up to 21% with 60 subnetworks.

items.title: Sensing-Driven Secure Transmission with Mobile Eavesdropper Tracking in RIS-Assisted ISAC
items.summary: The mobility of potential eavesdroppers (Eves) poses a critical challenge to physical-layer security (PLS) in integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems, since rapidly varying Eve positions lead to time-varying eavesdropping channels and outdated security decisions. To address this challenge, this paper investigates sensing-driven secure transmission for reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted ISAC systems with a maneuvering Eve. To this end, by exploiting the dual functionality of the ISAC waveform, a multi-view angle estimation method jointly exploiting the base station (BS) and RIS is developed based on MUSIC and maximum likelihood estimation (MLE), enabling three-dimensional (3D) Eve localization, whose accuracy is characterized by the Cramer-Rao lower bound (CRLB). Subsequently, an interacting multiple model extended Kalman filter (IMM-EKF) with out-of-sequence measurement (OOSM) compensation is employed to track and predict the maneuvering Eve. Based on the predicted trajectory, the time-varying eavesdropping channel is updated, and the transmit beamforming and RIS phase shifts are jointly optimized subject to a sensing CRLB constraint. Furthermore, an alternating optimization (AO) algorithm integrating fractional programming, semidefinite relaxation (SDR), and Riemannian manifold optimization is developed to solve the resulting non-convex problem. Finally, numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in accurately tracking maneuvering Eves and enhancing secure transmission in dynamic ISAC environments.

items.title: Temporal vs Spectral Resolution in CSI Reporting for Wi-Fi ISAC
items.summary: CSI feedback is fundamental to proposed uses of Wi-Fi sensing such as human activity recognition (HAR); but it also constitutes significant overhead as resources must be allocated away from data communications. Wi-Fi CSI extraction can be explored along two dimensions in IEEE 802.11bf: reporting intensity, i.e., temporal resolution, and number of reported subcarriers, i.e., spectral resolution. We explore periodic and IEEE 802.11bf threshold-based reporting at matched rates, and uniform decimation and block-mean grouping at matched report sizes. We further propose reporting the mean CSI accumulated since the last report. Using the 802.11bf report size as the metric, we evaluate the accuracy-cost tradeoffs on three public datasets with our proposed model, a convolutional neural network combined with a gated recurrent unit and temporal pyramid pooling. The proposed periodic reporting with mean payload and block-mean grouping improves accuracy by up to 53 percentage points at equal CSI overhead cost. Temporal resolution is generally more cost-effective than spectral resolution. With only at most 7.7% of full-CSI feedback cost, the proposed scheme achieves 96-98% of full-CSI accuracy.

items.title: Pilot-Based Sensing With OFDM and AFDM: A Resource-Matched Performance Comparison
items.summary: As a waveform candidate for next-generation wireless systems, affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) has often been compared with orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) under different configurations, while a systematic comparison of their pilot-based sensing performance remains lacking. This paper establishes a comparison with the same bandwidth, frame duration, pilot energy, and reserved-resource overhead. OFDM-random, OFDM-fixed-comb, and OFDM-shifted-comb pilots are compared with AFDM pilots surrounded by guard resources using aperiodic ambiguity functions without cyclic prefix/chirp-periodic prefix (CP/CPP) and cyclic ambiguity functions with CP/CPP, followed by target detection experiments. The results show that OFDM-fixed-comb exhibits low range sidelobes but periodic range ambiguity peaks, while AFDM and OFDM-shifted-comb effectively suppress zero-Doppler range ambiguities. Within the common unambiguous region, all pilot configurations for both waveforms exhibit similar detection thresholds in strong-target detection, while structured OFDM and AFDM pilot placements outperform OFDM-random in weak-target detection. At high mobility, the AFDM receiver using the discrete affine Fourier transform (DAFT) can resolve integer Doppler beyond the conventional slow-time maximum unambiguous velocity, outperforming the tested conventional OFDM and AFDM receivers at the increased search complexity. These results separate the effects of waveform, pilot placement, and receiver processing, providing a basis for AFDM and OFDM pilot-based sensing design.

items.title: ConQUESTA: Topology-Aware Post-Training Structural Pruning of Quantum Neural Networks
items.summary: Deploying quantum neural networks (QNNs) on sparse hardware requires preserving task accuracy while reducing compiler-induced two-qubit gates, SWAPs, and depth. We present ConQUESTA (\underline{C}onstrained \underline{Qu}antum \underline{E}ntangler \underline{S}election with \underline{T}opology \underline{A}wareness), a post training pruning framework that combines task saliency with compiler cost, screens candidate entanglers, and searches complete pruning masks under an explicit accuracy constraint. Unlike one-shot ranking, each mask is transpiled as a whole across multiple coupling topologies. Across 4-, 6-, and 8-qubit QNNs and eight model seeds at 55% pruning, ConQUESTA achieves mean resource reductions of 61.6% on Breast Cancer, 72.0% on Digits01, and 82.2% on Iris, exceeding the strongest matched simple baseline by 3.5, 1.7, and 8.9 percentage points, respectively. Fixed-mask recovery raises feasibility from 16/24 to 22/24 runs. In a fixed-k=4 scaling study on a scaling probe of 4 to 12-qubits, the raw mask space grew from 495 to 12.1M while the evaluated masks increase only from 189 to 305. Resource-weight changes alter depth/routing priorities with at most a 0.44-point mean validation shift.

items.title: AWM: An All-in-One Wireless Foundation Model for Multi-User Channel Acquisition and Localization Without Downstream Tuning
items.summary: Wireless foundation models (WFMs) seek to unify diverse wireless tasks and scenarios, yet existing methods still rely on task- or scenario-specific components or deployment-time fine-tuning. This paper presents an all-in-one wireless model (AWM), a WFM that unifies multi-user channel acquisition and localization, despite their distinct data modalities and functional objectives. We reveal that user location and channel state information (CSI) at different frequencies can be viewed as attribute-specific measurements of the same wireless link. By introducing in-scenario same-attribute reference pairs as prompts, AWM converts heterogeneous attributes into alignable relativity representations, formulating intra-band channel interpolation, inter-band channel prediction, and wireless localization as unified wireless-state transformations. Further, a multi-task MateFormer is developed to perform source-attribute relativity extraction, cross-attribute relativity alignment, and target-attribute synthesis within a unified architecture, avoiding task-specific output heads or downstream fine-tuning. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of model unification, including substantial gains from cross-task knowledge sharing, seamless generalization to unseen scenarios, and an efficient closed-loop service for mobile users.

items.title: Joint Subcarrier and Power Allocation for Localization-Oriented Multi-Carrier Underwater ISAC Systems
items.summary: Multi-carrier underwater integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) realizes concurrent acoustic communication and localization, yet the frequency selectivity of the acoustic channel creates uneven positioning capabilities across subcarriers. This paper proposes a localization-oriented subcarrier and power allocation scheme for multi-anchor underwater ISAC systems. We build a unified orthogonal subcarrier multiplexing framework and derive closed-form Cramer-Rao bounds (CRBs) under frequency-selective channels with colored noise. We derive a subcarrier-level localization information contribution from the time of arrival Fisher information, which enables localization-oriented resource allocation. We derive several theoretical properties regarding the distance and frequency dependence of the localization information metric, and establish a distance-frequency matching principle. These results provide a theoretical foundation for localization-oriented resource allocation and guide the design of a low-complexity greedy algorithm that improves positioning accuracy. Specifically, the algorithm iteratively allocates subcarriers to minimize the residual positioning-error objective, thereby improving positioning accuracy while satisfying communication quality-of-service (QoS) constraints. Simulations verify that our method yields much lower positioning error bound than uniform, random and high-frequency-first subcarrier allocation in symmetric or asymmetric topologies while guaranteeing communication QoS, achieving superior communication-localization tradeoffs.

items.title: Vector-field-guided constraint-following control for path following of uncertain mechanical systems
items.summary: Achieving dynamics-level control is a critical yet challenging problem for accurate, high-speed geometric path-following of uncertain robotic systems. This paper proposes a vector-field-guided constraint-following control framework for geometric path following of uncertain mechanical systems. The key idea is to encode vector-field guidance as a velocity constraint, enabling a unified force/torque control design for a class of fully actuated and underactuated systems with desired paths that may be self-intersecting. A global, explicit error estimate connects constraint-following accuracy to path-following performance with convergence guarantees. An adaptive robust extension further addresses heterogeneous time-varying uncertainties with unknown bounds and ensures ultimately bounded path-following error. Applications to an underactuated aircraft system and a fully actuated manipulator system demonstrate the effectiveness and advantages of the framework.

items.title: Full-Domain Coupler: A Wireless Native Neural Backbone for Channel Representation and Deduction
items.summary: Data representation is a fundamental issue in deep learning. However, as wireless data scales and deeply couples across many physical domains such as time, space, and frequency, existing wireless artificial intelligence (AI) technologies lack dedicated representation solutions. Instead, they mainly rely on stitching general-purpose networks, a tool-driven paradigm that inevitably results in structural redundancy and bottlenecks in information flow. To fill this gap, this paper proposes Coupler, a wireless native-AI neural backbone designed for representation learning of channel state information (CSI)--the pivotal data in wireless systems. Leveraging the revealed physical insights of channel tensors, Coupler decomposes representation learning into individual domains on a layer-by-layer basis, and then couples the learned domain-specific features through a dimension-staggered cascade. This full-domain interleaved learning architecture enables superior parameter efficiency and fine-grained multi-domain feature fusion. Based on this backbone, we use the complex-domain multilayer perceptrons (CMLPs) as spatial and frequency domain learners, while employing three optional mechanisms--convolution, attention, or gating--to capture temporal dependencies. This results in a series of efficient channel learning schemes with diverse functionalities and extreme lightweights, showcasing the compactness, versatility and flexibility of Coupler. We evaluate these schemes on channel deduction, a general representation task encompassing channel estimation, interpolation, prediction, and feedback. Extensive experimental evaluations validate their significant performance gains and robust applicability even for real-world measured data, demonstrating the potential of Coupler as a promising basic architecture in the design of wireless foundation models.

items.title: Enabling Tidying Tasks in Robotic Vacuum Cleaners via a Geometry-Induced Self-Locking Deployable Linkage
items.summary: Robotic vacuum cleaners must extend their functionality within tight limits on size, cost, and durability. Deployable linkages with few actuators meet these limits, but their backdrivability makes it difficult to hold a load-bearing posture without continuous motor torque. We introduce a two-stage deployable linkage that locks through its own geometry. At full deployment, an internal three-link subchain approaches a collinear, near-singular configuration in which the input-output transmission ratio tends to zero; plate loads therefore leave only a small residual back-driving torque, which drive-train friction and a lightweight magnetic detent absorb. A single actuator performs deployment and locking, a passive chassis-mounted trigger releases the lock for retraction, and a second actuator adjusts only the deployment height. We integrate the mechanism into a commercial robotic vacuum cleaner and validate it through a 100-cycle repeatability test, a quasi-static load test in which the locked plate held 50 N with the motor de-energized, and 140 pushing-type tidying trials on seven household objects against a commercial arm-equipped vacuum robot. We derive the analytical holding condition and discuss its limits as an intermediate design point between passive compliance and articulated manipulation.

items.title: UniPolar: Joint Image and Polarimetric Restoration under Compound Degradations via Physical Consistency Learning
items.summary: Polarimetric image restoration aims to recover polarization angle images and reliable polarimetric quantities from degraded observations. Beyond visual fidelity, it also requires preserving the physical relationships underlying reliable polarimetric estimation. However, existing methods typically address either device- or environment-induced degradations in isolation, limiting their applicability to color polarization filter array (CPFA) imaging, where both often coexist. Such compound degradations jointly perturb image intensities and cross angle polarization differences. Consequently, improved image fidelity alone does not necessarily ensure accurate Stokes, DoLP, and AoLP recovery. To address this challenge, we propose UniPolar, a coupled Image Stokes framework for joint image polarimetric restoration from compound-degraded CPFA observations. Specifically, UniPolar employs two complementary streams to reconstruct four polarization-angle images and directly predict Stokes difference components. To coordinate these streams, Degradation Conditioned Cross Domain Interaction combines Dual Domain Frequency Interaction for frequency selective evidence exchange with Degradation Conditioned Modulation for condition adaptive feature correction. Furthermore, at the output level, Image Stokes Physical Consistency Learning aligns image derived and directly predicted Stokes components while regularizing angular fidelity and the physical feasibility of DoLP. On the compound-degradation benchmark, UniPolar achieves average image and DoLP PSNR of 31.522 dB and 24.097 dB, respectively, with an average AoLP error of 16.833 degree. These results underscore the importance of jointly considering visual fidelity and polarimetric reliability, offering a physically grounded perspective on learning based restoration under compound degradations.

items.title: Opportunities for Direct-to-Cell Polarization MIMO in the Downlink of a LEO Satellite Footprint
items.summary: A single low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite offers almost no spatial degrees of freedom, but its two polarizations can carry a second layer to the handset. The downlink spectral efficiency is mapped over the footprint of a satellite at 330 km altitude above Munich. The channel is a cascade of Jones factors including the phased-array payload, Faraday rotation, a dual-polarized land mobile satellite channel and a standardized handset antenna element at three attitudes. For a handset with boresight to zenith and 6 dB SNR, ideal precoding selects rank 2 with probability of at least 0.95 within 340 km of the nadir point. With closed-loop precoding, such a handset on the nadir track is in rank~2 during 99% of a pass. Upright handsets also select rank 2 wherever they face the satellite, and rank selection improves the mean spectral efficiency over the footprint by up to 49%.

items.title: TransNSNet: A Transformer-Enhanced Multi-Scale Adversarial Framework for CT-to-PET Image Synthesis
items.summary: This study investigates CT-to-PET image synthesis using TransNSNet, a Transformer-enhanced multi-scale adversarial framework. A paired CT-PET dataset was curated from the public non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) Radiogenomics collection through patient screening, slice-level matching, preprocessing, and patient-level train-test separation. The proposed framework generates PET-like predictions at multiple spatial scales and applies coarse-to-fine reconstruction supervision, while TransPatchGAN introduces contextual feature interaction into adversarial evaluation. A progressive ablation study compares Pix2Pix, NSNet-Base, NSNet-D, and TransNSNet. Image-level performance was summarized over a fixed convergence window (epochs 80-101) from one training run per model. TransNSNet achieved the best mean value in nine of ten metrics, whereas NSNet-Base achieved the highest visual saliency-induced index. For fixed-fraction high-intensity regions, NSNet-D was marginally higher in slice-level recall and balanced accuracy, but the equal-weight patient-level values were nearly identical and the highest Dice values shifted to TransNSNet. These differences were small relative to between-patient variability. In the separate adaptive patient-level analysis (n=10), no pairwise model difference remained statistically significant after Holm correction. TransNSNet also had a substantially smaller parameter footprint than the original next-scale models. These findings indicate promising image-quality trends, but they do not establish statistical superiority or clinical validity; synthesized PET-like images should not be interpreted as substitutes for clinically acquired PET.

items.title: Grouped Sparse Bayesian Estimation for Near-Field Massive MIMO Channels
items.summary: This paper studies near-field massive MIMO channel estimation based on an electromagnetic channel model with limited pilots. Starting from Maxwell's equations, we derive the homogeneous background response and the scattering response in the spatial and wavenumber domains. It is found that a compact scattering cluster produces a localized receive--transmit transverse-wavenumber block across finite apertures, thereby yields a block-sparse NLOS channel coefficient matrix in the wavenumber domain. Considering the spatial non-stationarity of large-scale antenna arrays, we introduce visibility factors at the transmit and receive sides of the channel model. To solve the non-stationary sparse channel estimation problem in the wavenumber domain, we propose a visibility-aware block-sparse Bayesian channel estimation algorithm. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves lower channel-estimation NMSE than benchmark schemes.

items.title: Teleoperation Operational Design Domain based on Minimal Risk Maneuver Capability
items.summary: This article discusses the concept of an Operational Design Domain (ODD) designed specifically for teleoperated road vehicles. For this purpose, the ODD concept designed for automated driving is adapted for teleoperation. As teleoperation becomes more common in regular traffic, the question arises under which operating conditions such vehicles are able and allowed to drive. Currently, these conditions are selected primarily based on network performance. From a safety perspective, it is difficult to base such a selection on a reliable connection because it is almost impossible to guarantee sufficient reliability. With this in mind, the ODD concept designed for automated driving is adapted for teleoperation: A concept is proposed for basing the ODD for a teleoperation system on the capability of the teleoperated vehicle to perform a minimal risk maneuver using a dedicated system designed solely for this purpose. This concept is then demonstrated using a use case example.

items.title: FlashReFocus: Interactive Image Refocusing in Seconds
items.summary: Single-image refocusing changes the focal plane and depth of field of a photograph after capture. It is inherently interactive: users try many focal points and blur strengths on one image, so each edit should be fast and change only the blur. Recent generative methods, however, rerun large diffusion models for every edit. We observe that the two sub-problems differ in kind: recovering the all-in-focus image is ill-posed and needs a generative prior, whereas rendering blur is largely determined by depth and the focal plane. We therefore propose FlashReFocus, which runs diffusion once per photograph and renders every edit with a lightweight network. To address the ill-posed restoration, a one-step diffusion deblurrer with a decoder refiner recovers fine detail efficiently while balancing fidelity and perceptual quality. For precise control, the renderer is conditioned on an explicit defocus map and uses defocus-bias attention, which lets pixels at similar defocus share information without interference from pixels at other depths; in-focus content stays unchanged, and editing the map yields tilt-shift and two focal planes. To further test generalization to unseen cameras, we collect 3CReal, a three-camera benchmark of 89 pairs. FlashReFocus achieves the best perceptual fidelity for zero-shot bokeh rendering on EBB! and 3CReal, refocuses 148.3x faster than GenRefocus, and takes about half a second per further edit, 462x faster.

items.title: Phased Ultra Massive Array (PUMA)
items.summary: This paper proposes a novel multiple-access framework, termed the phased ultra massive antenna array (PUMA), which exploits the distinctive spatial flexibility of fluid antenna systems (FAS) at the user equipment (UE). Building upon fluid antenna multiple access (FAMA) and compact ultra-massive antenna array (CUMA), PUMA incorporates a phased array for signal aggregation. This architecture enables the UE to inherently mitigate co-user interference within the spatial domain without necessitating channel state information (CSI) for precoding at the base station (BS) or complex interference cancellation at each UE. A primary advantage of PUMA lies in its hardware efficiency: by implementing phase shifting and signal combining in the analog domain, it achieves high antenna gain while requiring only a minimal number of radio-frequency (RF) chains, potentially a single RF chain. Comprehensive theoretical analysis of the achievable data rate is provided, complemented by extensive simulations that validate the framework. The results demonstrate that PUMA markedly outperforms FAMA and CUMA architectures, particularly for UEs with a single RF chain, offering a robust and scalable solution for interference-insensitive massive connectivity in sixth-generation (6G) systems.

items.title: A flexible language model-assisted electronic design automation framework
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are transforming electronic design automation (EDA) by enhancing design stages such as schematic design, simulation, netlist synthesis, and place-and-route. Existing methods primarily focus these optimisations within isolated open-source EDA tools and often lack the flexibility to handle multiple domains, such as analogue, digital, and radio-frequency design. In contrast, modern systems require to interface with commercial EDA environments, adhere to tool-specific operation rules, and incorporate feedback from design outcomes while supporting diverse design flows. We propose a versatile framework that uses LLMs to generate files compatible with commercial EDA tools and optimise designs using power-performance-area reports. This is accomplished by guiding the LLMs with tool constraints and feedback from design outputs to meet tool requirements and user specifications. The framework is used to evaluate case studies on operational transconductance amplifiers, microstrip patch antennas, and FPGA circuits.

items.title: Residential Peak Load Reduction via Direct Load Control under Limited Information
items.summary: Thermostatically controlled loads and electric vehicles offer flexibility to reduce power peaks in low-voltage distribution networks. This flexibility can be maximized if the devices are coordinated centrally, given some level of information about the controlled devices. In this paper, we propose novel optimization-based control schemes with prediction capabilities that utilize limited information from heat pumps, electric water heaters, and electric vehicles. The objective is to flatten the total load curve seen by the distribution transformer by restricting the times at which the available flexible loads are allowed to operate, subject to the flexibility constraints of the loads to preserve customers' comfort. The original scheme was tested in a real-world setup, considering both summer and winter days. The pilot results confirmed the technical feasibility but also informed the design of an improved version of the controller. Computer simulations using the adjusted controller show that, compared to the original formulation, the improved scheme achieves greater peak reductions in summer. Additionally, comparisons were made with an ideal controller, which assumes perfect knowledge of the inflexible load profile, the models of the controlled devices, the hot water and space heating demand, and future electric vehicle charging sessions. The proposed scheme with limited information achieves 43.3 % and 27.8 % of the potential average daily peak reduction that the ideal controller with perfect knowledge would achieve in summer and winter, respectively.

items.title: IMU-Aided Motion Compensation of RSS Measurements for Dynamic Visible Light-Inertial Localization
items.summary: Visible Light Positioning (VLP) offers high-precision indoor positioning using existing LED infrastructure. However, in VLP systems using Photodiodes (PDs) as receivers, rapid movement of the PD causes measurement inaccuracies as the Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT) processing yields averaged rather than instantaneous Received Signal Strength (RSS) values. To address this challenge, we propose an RSS correction algorithm that integrates Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) data with VLP observations to compensate for motion-induced distortions. Our approach leverages IMU-derived motion parameters to model the temporal variation of optical signals during the DFT window, enabling instantaneous RSS estimation. The algorithm is embedded within both tightly and simply coupled VLP/INS integration frameworks that estimate the pose of the moving receiver. This work targets highly dynamic indoor navigation. Simulations validate the correction model, and total-station-tracked experiments confirm reduced RSS discrepancies against model references. Across eight held-out high-dynamic handheld trials with peak translational and angular speeds of 2.25 m/s and 284 deg/s, correction reduces the pooled 3D position and PD-normal inclination root mean square errors relative to the LiDAR/IMU reference with a shared IMU by 56.0% and 71.9%, respectively. Both datasets and source code are publicly available.

items.title: Prospect Theoretic Approach to Pursuit-evasion Differential Games with Risk Aversion and Probability Sensitivity
items.summary: This paper considers pursuit-evasion (PE) differential games in which the pursuer's and evader's irrational perceptions of environmental uncertainty lead to deviations from rational controllers. Firstly, the equivalent irrational behavioral models of risk aversion and probability sensitivity are established using Cumulative Prospect Theory (CPT). Secondly, sufficient conditions for capturability are established in terms of irrationality parameters. Finally, the CPT-Nash equilibrium is analyzed by Brouwer's fixed-point and self-consistency theorem. The new results reveal that irrational behaviors benefit the pursuer in some cases and the evader in others. Certain captures that are unachievable under rational behaviors can be achieved under irrational ones. By bridging irrational behavior with game-based control, a theoretical foundation is established for human-machine control systems.

items.title: Entropy-Based Wireless Technology Recognition
items.summary: Wireless Technology Recognition (WTR) enables identifying wireless technologies from received radio signals and is important for spectrum monitoring and management systems. Existing approaches either rely on handcrafted signal features with limited robustness or computationally intensive Deep Learning (DL) models operating on high-dimensional In-phase and Quadrature (IQ) samples or spectrograms. In this paper, we investigate a different hypothesis: wireless technologies can be distinguished through the temporal evolution of their local time-frequency complexity. To capture this behavior, we propose a lightweight WTR framework based on two-dimensional dispersion entropy. Entropy values are extracted from successive spectrogram regions to characterize the evolution of local spectrogram complexity throughout a transmission and summarized into a compact feature representation for classification using a Multilayer Perceptron (MLP). The framework is evaluated on seven wireless technologies, namely IEEE 802.11ah, IEEE 802.15.4 SUN-FSK, IEEE 802.15.4 SUN-OFDM, LoRa, IEEE 802.11n, LTE, and 5G NR, at Signal-to-Noise Ratios (SNRs) ranging from -20 dB to 40 dB. Experimental results show that the proposed approach consistently outperforms IQ-based and Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT)-based Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) baselines, particularly at low and moderate SNRs. Averaged across all evaluated SNR levels, it achieves 82.73% accuracy, corresponding to improvements of 23.8% and 14.6% over the IQ-based and STFT-based CNN approaches, respectively. Furthermore, the approach maintains its recognition advantage with data-augmented training while requiring substantially shorter training times. The results demonstrate that temporal evolution of local spectrogram complexity provides a robust technology-specific fingerprint and an effective, computationally efficient representation for WTR.

items.title: Robust Design of Sensing-Assisted Secure Transmission for RIS-Aided ISAC System under Eavesdropper 3D Positioning Uncertainty
items.summary: Localization errors in estimating the position of a potential eavesdropper (Eve) pose a critical challenge to secure transmission in reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems. To address this issue, this paper proposes a sensing-assisted robust secure transmission framework that exploits ISAC sensing to characterize the positioning uncertainty induced by these errors. The RIS is partitioned into a reflection region and a sensing reception region, supporting sensing and communication through spatial separation. By jointly exploiting observations collected at the base station (BS) and the RIS sensing reception region, maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) is employed to estimate the arrival angles, from which Eve's three-dimensional (3D) position is obtained through cross localization. The resulting localization Cramer-Rao lower bound (CRLB) is then used to construct an ellipsoidal uncertainty region around the estimated position. A two-stage optimization strategy is developed. In Stage I, the sensing beamformer and RIS reflection coefficients are jointly optimized to improve localization accuracy. In Stage II, the resulting positioning uncertainty is incorporated into a robust secure transmission design, where the communication beamformer and RIS reflection coefficients are jointly optimized to maximize the worst-case secrecy rate. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms benchmark schemes without RIS assistance and with random RIS configurations in terms of secrecy performance. The proposed framework effectively mitigates secrecy performance degradation caused by localization errors in Eve's position.

items.title: Coherent but Discordant: Rotate, Don't Invert, to Backpropagate Through an Aging Channel
items.summary: A channel can be almost perfectly coherent and still teach a transmitter the wrong direction. In physical ("over-the-air") backpropagation, the receiver sends its loss gradient back through the reciprocal channel; when the terminal moves in between, mobility does not merely add noise to the returned gradient, it rotates it. Under a scalar conditional mean model the rotation is set by the phase of the temporal correlation, so coherence, which measures only its magnitude, is the wrong ruler: in simulation, channels with absolute value of rho greater than 0.9 drive uncorrected training to 51.7% accuracy, while phase correction restores 92.5%. Arrays add a twist. Near zeros of the trace correlation, scalar correction fails even with rho known exactly, yet most of the information is still there: noise has moved it onto neighbouring antennas. Re-indexing the ports by the displacement, with zero digital feedback, recovers the lost performance in simulation, and so does rotating the returned seed with the unitary polar factor of the conditional mean operator, never inverting it; aligning each antenna's phase with its own past makes things worse. An exact array identity explains all three. The lesson fits in one line: correct the rotation, not the stretch.

items.title: Wait to Learn: Lobes and Dead Zones in Physical Backpropagation over an Aging Single-Antenna Channel
items.summary: Sometimes the best way to correct an aged gradient is to wait. In physical backpropagation, a receiver returns its loss gradient through the reciprocal channel. With a single moving antenna, the mean gradient returned at the antenna is the true one counter-rotated by the phase of the temporal correlation. In simulation, uncorrected training fails in negative correlation lobes and revives in positive ones. At correlation zeros the return is independent of the forward channel, so no linear correction has a mean to recover; near them, more calibration barely helps, but holding the return until the next correlation extremum does.

items.title: Keep Pace to Learn: Movable Antennas Restore the Backpropagated Gradient Under User Mobility
items.summary: When a mobile terminal takes part in over-the-air training, its own motion rotates the gradient that travels back through it; a movable antenna that keeps pace with the terminal rotates it back---without any channel estimate. We give a speed law: under a scalar conditional-mean model of the physical return, landing the residual displacement inside the first positive lobe of the spatial correlation keeps the conditional mean gradient a descent direction, which, given sufficient travel, fixes a critical actuator-to-terminal speed ratio. We further prove a bias--jitter law: under the same scalar conditional-mean model and with zero effective bias, independent zero-mean Gaussian jitter of any finite amplitude scales the conditional mean gradient without reversing its direction, whereas a sub-wavelength systematic bias can reverse it. This result motivates prioritizing bias calibration to preserve gradient direction. Simulations on 3GPP CDL-A channels show that an antenna keeping pace with the terminal achieves near-CSI accuracy without digital channel correction, reaching 98.58 % compared with 98.59% for the ideal-CSI reference. The simulations also show that partial compensation can support learning when the residual displacement falls within a later positive correlation lobe, so a faster actuator does not necessarily yield higher accuracy. Separate positioning simulations show a sharp accuracy loss under systematic bias but little degradation under zero-mean Gaussian jitter of comparable spatial scale.

items.title: A Traffic-Aware QoS-Energy Consumption Tradeoff Study for Integrated 6G TN & NTNs
items.summary: Motivated by the Hypercell concept, we extend BLASTER to investigate the trade-off between network quality of service (QoS) and terrestrial energy consumption in integrated terrestrial and non-terrestrial networks. We compare one low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite at 600 km with 1-, 4-, and 9-high-altitude platform station (HAPS) deployments at 20 km under a 24-hour traffic profile. Increasing the number of HAPS improves traffic offloading and enables additional terrestrial base station shutdowns. The 9-HAPS configuration reduces terrestrial energy consumption by 34.1% over the full day, compared with 26.0% for LEO. At the same QoS, the 9-HAPS configuration achieves 20% additional terrestrial energy savings relative to LEO, while substantially improving cell-edge throughput.

items.title: Open-H-RF: A Large-Scale Ultrasound Raw Channel Dataset Initiative
items.summary: Medical ultrasound is a widely accessible, real-time imaging modality, yet progress in data-driven ultrasound research is constrained by the scarcity of large, open collections of raw channel data. Existing public datasets are predominantly based on reconstructed images, while the smaller number of open raw channel datasets is generally specialized to individual reconstruction or imaging tasks, limiting the development of general-purpose methods and foundation models that operate directly on ultrasound signals. While interpretive tasks can be performed on reconstructed images, many of the key technical challenges in ultrasound imaging, such as aberration correction and reverberation reduction, require the raw channel data itself. We introduce Open-H-RF, a community-driven open dataset initiative comprising approximately 40 TB of medical ultrasound raw channel data in 19,332 acquisitions, contributed by 38 institutions across academia and industry, spanning in-vivo, phantom, and simulated data. Each dataset is annotated with a number of supported tasks, ranging from generalized reconstruction, speed-of-sound estimation, and aberration correction to blood flow imaging, motion estimation, quantitative ultrasound, and image interpretation. Open-H-RF provides a unified, self-contained data format that captures raw channel data together with the acquisition, probe, metadata, and reconstruction information required for reproducible processing across scanners and acquisition schemes. The corpus is publicly hosted under a permissive CC BY 4.0 license and can be streamed programmatically and selectively at scale. By bringing heterogeneous ultrasound data into a common representation, backed by modern data infrastructure, Open-H-RF lowers the barrier to working with raw channel data and aims to open medical ultrasound research to new communities. See https://open-h.github.io/Open-H-RF.

items.title: LWMa: Distributed Deployment of an Angle-Delay-Domain Wireless Foundation Model for Multiple Tasks
items.summary: The growing diversity of wireless services in sixth-generation (6G) wireless communication systems calls for reusable channel representations that support multiple tasks across different propagation environments. However, deploying such representations between user equipment and the base station in frequency-division duplexing systems faces uplink feedback constraints. This paper proposes a distributed framework based on an angle-delay-domain large wireless model (LWMa) for multiple tasks. LWMa exploits angle-delay structure and delay truncation to improve feature extraction and reduce computational cost. A scenario-specific network inspired by Perceiver IO (input-output) compresses embeddings for channel reconstruction tasks, while other tasks use a low-dimensional compact global embedding. Embedding reconstruction training followed by channel-quality-guided fine-tuning preserves information useful for downstream processing. Simulations demonstrate that the proposed method supports effective channel reconstruction and multiple tasks under limited feedback with reduced deployment complexity. Further evaluations show that the recovered embeddings generalize to additional tasks and support split inference.

items.title: Integrated sensing and communications in the 3GPP New Radio: sensing limits
