items.summary: Surface reflectance products derived from optical satellite may exhibit systematic inconsistencies across acquisition dates, because atmospheric correction is generally performed independently for each image. Such residual biases distort the temporal behavior of invariant ground targets and reduce the reliability of multitemporal surface reflectance analysis. This study proposes Deep Multitemporal Generalized Canonical Correlation Analysis (DeepMGCCA), an unsupervised deep multiview pseudoinvariant feature learning framework that integrates Deep Generalized Canonical Correlation Analysis (GCCA) with Multivariate Alteration Detection (MAD) to identify deep-pseudoinvariant features (DIFs) for the removal of surface reflectance biases across multitemporal satellite observations. Unlike conventional MAD-based approaches that rely on linear GCCA, the proposed framework replaces date-specific linear projections with a shared convolutional encoder. The framework learns deep invariant features (DIFs) directly from pixel-weighted canonical variates via iterative reweighting strategy, while a reconstruction regularizer preserves surface reflectance information and prevents degenerate collapse from suppressing genuine temporal variability. Experiments were conducted on four annual Landsat-8/9 and Sentinel-2 acquisitions across four regions of interest (ROIs) to evaluate four DIF-based harmonization transforms. A monotone piecewise-linear transform derived from DIFs quantiles consistently achieved the largest bias reduction, lowering the between-date spectral angle by up to 2.54 and RMSE by 0.015, and raising PSNR by up to 4.04~dB. These findings demonstrate the potential of deep invariant feature learning for multitemporal surface reflectance bias removal while highlighting the importance of preserving physically meaningful temporal and spectral information during nonlinear representation learning.

items.title: Physical AI: A Survey of Models, Learning, Systems, and Open Challenges
items.summary: Physical AI aims to enable intelligent systems to perceive, reason, act, and learn through interaction with the physical world. Unlike purely digital intelligence, physical agents must operate under partial observability, uncertain dynamics, embodiment constraints, and real-time requirements, while their actions continuously reshape the environment and subsequent observations. Recent advances in foundation models and robot learning have expanded the capabilities of physical agents, yet achieving reliable autonomy requires more than improvements in individual models. This survey presents a comprehensive, system-level review of Physical AI, organized around the closed-loop process of physical interaction. We examine the foundations and recent developments in task representations and memory, predictive and action-generating models, data and learning methods, embodiment and control, computing systems, evaluation, and safety. Beyond reviewing individual advances, we investigate how these components interact and collectively shape the capabilities and limitations of Physical AI systems. Building on this integrated perspective, we identify fundamental challenges in generalization, resource-efficient learning and execution, reliable state tracking, safety, recovery, and continual adaptation. We argue that advancing Physical AI requires moving beyond isolated model performance toward integrated systems capable of robust, efficient, safe, and autonomous physical interaction under changing real-world conditions.

items.title: Tokenized Joint Source-Network Coding for Loss-Resilient Video Streaming
items.summary: For decades, conventional video streaming systems have relied on packet-level forward error correction (FEC) codes and retransmissions to ensure reliable video delivery. However, in real-time communications, FEC is inherently inefficient under unknown and time-varying packet-loss conditions, while retransmission can incur excessive latency and fail to meet stringent playout deadlines. Emerging deep joint source-channel coding (DeepJSCC) provides an alternative by learning channel-noise-resilient representations, yet its tight coupling with the physical layer makes it difficult to integrate into today's layered network architectures and protocols. In this paper, we propose TokJSNC, a simple-but-effective tokenized joint source-network coding paradigm for packet-loss-resilient video streaming. Rather than first compressing video into a compact bitstream and then protecting it with packet-level FEC, TokJSNC directly encodes video into variable-length discrete token-stream, whose transmission rate is jointly adapted to video content complexity and network conditions. By exploiting the spatiotemporal correlations among learned video tokens, TokJSNC enables robust video reconstruction over a wide range of packet-loss rates without explicit FEC or retransmissions. Consequently, TokJSNC brings the JSCC-like graceful degradation property to the network layer while remaining compatible with existing network architectures and transport protocols. Experimental results show that TokJSNC maintains an average playback frame rate above 22 fps even at a 70% packet-loss rate, whereas the best-performing baseline drops below 12 fps. Overall, TokJSNC establishes a practical pathway for repurposing modern generative video tokenizers for loss-resilient streaming, while providing a fundamental framework for video token communications.

items.title: Really Need Recursion? Revisiting One-pass Registration with Multi-level Multi-space Contextual Guidance
items.summary: Deformable image registration is a fundamental challenge in medical image analysis. Recent deep learning-based methods typically adopt either one-pass architectures that complete registration in a single network iteration, or recursive architectures that refine registration through multiple passes. While recursive methods often improve accuracy, they incur substantial computational overhead and slower inference speed. In this paper, we challenge the necessity of recursion for high-performance deformable registration and propose M2CG, a one-pass registration network with Multi-level Multi-space Contextual Guidance. It performs multi-step progressive pyramid registration within a single iteration, guided at each step by contextual cues from three levels (previous, current, and subsequent steps) and four spaces (image space, image feature space, segmentation space, and segmentation feature space). Our M2CG supports both unsupervised (without any labels) and semi-supervised (with segmentation labels for partial training data) registration, and has achieved state-of-the-art performance across two well-benchmarked inter-/intra-patient medical registration tasks with eight public datasets. Our findings suggest that the current reliance on recursion may stem from the absence of sufficient contextual cues that comprehensively characterize the remaining distance to the target alignment.

items.title: Case-Specific Priors-Guided Multimodal Fusion for Prognosis Prediction in Head and Neck Cancer
items.summary: Accurate prognosis prediction for head and neck cancer typically necessitates integrating highly heterogeneous clinical and pathological evidence by sophisticated multimodal fusion. However, existing fusion techniques are usually grounded in case-generic clinical rationales about complementary synergies across modalities, underestimating case-specific variance. In this study, we propose a prognosis prediction framework that explicitly incorporates Case-specific Priors to guide Multimodal fusion (named CPM). It leverages broad medical knowledge of LLMs to characterize each case's (case-specific) intra-modal contexts and inter-modal relations, as well as case-generic multimodal rationale, as priors, enabling three-stage priors-guided multimodal fusion: (i) Intra-modal Context-guided Calibration (IntraCC) that leverages case-specific intra-modal priors to guide feature calibration within each modality; (ii) Inter-modal Relation-guided Interaction (InterRI) that leverages case-specific inter-modal priors to guide pair-wise feature interaction in modality pairs; and (iii) Multimodal Rationale-guided Aggregation (MultiRA) that leverages case-generic multimodal priors to guide final feature aggregation over all modalities. On the well-established HANCOCK challenge dataset involving four distinct medical modalities, our CPM achieved a mean AUC of 83.98% for predicting 5-year overall survival and 2-year recurrence-free survival, improving upon the baseline by 7.58%, pioneeringly demonstrating the effectiveness of LLM-derived medical priors in guiding multimodal fusion for prognosis prediction. The code is available at https://github.com/yuelin421/CPM.

items.title: VoxTurn: Answering Several Turn-Taking Questions in One Pass with One Model
items.summary: A cascaded voice agent must decide, throughout each silence of its user, whether the user has finished their turn: answering too early cuts the user off, answering too late makes the agent slow. It often needs related decisions too: will the user soon go on, is speech during its own turn an interruption or a backchannel, is a sound speech at all. With open detectors, each extra decision costs another model or another call, and on the 14-language eot-bench they cut users off in more than a quarter of mid-turn pauses. Because they are trained on segmented utterances, this mismatch is the largest single source of error. We present VoxTurn, a 0.8B speech LLM that casts these decisions as multiple-choice questions, scores the hidden state of each option, and answers any set of them in one forward pass with a block-isolating attention mask, exactly as if asked one at a time. Trained on real conversational pauses with labels derived from their timing, and re-queried while a silence lasts, VoxTurn reaches 11.5% false cut-offs in English at a 300 ms latency budget, comparable to two commercial detectors, and a 14-language mean of 19.9%, the lowest among open models, at 8.3 ms per decision. In Pipecat and LiveKit it cuts off 17% and 9% of turns, and it ranks fifth of 24 in TurnBench end-of-turn detection without any TurnBench training data. The model, code and framework plugins are released.

items.title: End-to-End Learned Image Coding: From Rate-Distortion Optimization to Practical Deployment
items.summary: End-to-end learned image coding (LIC) has achieved substantial improvements in rate--distortion (R--D) performance, yet practical deployment requires addressing a broader set of system-level constraints. This article provides a deployment-oriented review of LIC, with particular attention to the transition from high-performance neural compression models to practical codecs. We first summarize the basic end-to-end coding framework, including learned transforms, quantization, entropy modeling, and R--D optimization. We then review practical extensions that are increasingly important for deployment, including variable-rate coding and rate control, integer-precision inference and cross-platform consistency, robustness and communication resilience, lightweight and hardware-aware implementation, and standardization and interoperability. To study these issues under a common setting, we further introduce TinyLIC as an open benchmark and reproducible case study for rate--distortion--complexity analysis. Experimental results illustrate the trade-offs among compression efficiency, computational complexity, numerical consistency, and robustness. In particular, TinyLIC with approximately 10 KMACs/pixel decoding complexity substantially outperforms the H.265/HEVC image-profile anchor on Kodak, while the 50 KMACs/pixel configuration achieves performance comparable to the H.266/VVC image-profile anchor on several test sets. The review highlights practical constraints and design trade-offs that remain central to the deployment and interoperability of learned image codecs. Materials are accessible at https://njuvision.github.io/TinyLIC.

items.title: CRUX: Clinical-Text Anchoring for Cross-Institutional CT-Pathology Fusion in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer Survival Prediction
items.summary: Accurate prognosis in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) benefits from integrating computed tomography (CT) and histopathological whole-slide images (WSIs), which capture complementary macroscopic and microscopic disease characteristics. Fusing these modalities is difficult: their features come from different pretrained foundation-model encoders and lack spatial correspondence, and both are sensitive to institution-specific acquisition and staining, causing multimodal models to overfit site-specific artifacts and generalize poorly. We present CRUX (CRoss-modal Unification via teXt anchoring), a fusion framework that uses clinical text---encoded by a biomedical language model---as an institution-invariant semantic anchor. Because clinical variables follow standardized classification systems, their embeddings occupy a representation space that is consistent across institutions, providing a stable reference frame for aligning heterogeneous imaging features. CRUX introduces a text-mediated cross-modal bridge in which CT- and pathology-derived text-query summaries exchange information within a compact text semantic space through a learnable hub token, avoiding direct image-space cross-attention that would propagate domain-specific artifacts. We evaluate on 2,157 NSCLC patients from five hospitals, holding out one hospital (N=446) entirely for external validation. CRUX attains an external concordance index (C-index) of 0.761, the highest among all unimodal, bimodal, and trimodal configurations. Notably, direct CT-WSI fusion degrades under distribution shift, whereas text anchoring restores and improves cross-institutional generalization. These results indicate that language-model-encoded clinical text is an effective structured prior for robust, generalizable multimodal cancer prognosis.

items.title: Denoising Rather Than Gap Filling: Missing-Data Handling in Sparse Outdoor BLE Positioning
items.summary: Received signal strength indicator (RSSI) positioning outdoors has one to two orders of magnitude fewer anchors than the indoor systems its methods come from. In the ten-day cattle-tracking deployment reported here, four gateways cover $4{,}302\,\mathrm{m}^2$, or $0.93$ anchors per $1000\,\mathrm{m}^2$. An animal is heard by $0.99$ gateways per second on average, so the observation vector for a given second is almost never complete. How the gaps are filled is therefore a first-order design choice, not a preprocessing detail. Filling at all is worth $8.1\,\mathrm{m}$, $96\%$ of the improvement the hold-length setting can deliver and a $29\%$ error reduction. How long a value is then held is worth the remaining $4\%$, from four seconds to unbounded. Once a value is available, the gain comes from removing noise rather than rebuilding the lost sample: a filtered channel estimate improves on a held raw sample, whereas filling backwards from future samples makes it worse. As that mechanism predicts, smoothing strength has a real interior optimum that is costly to miss in either direction. A smoother allowed to read the future gains only $0.55\,\mathrm{m}$, one fifteenth of what filling is worth, which bounds what any offline method can add. Three method families do not apply here for structural reasons rather than poor performance: two or more of the four channels are live in only $25\%$ of seconds, so the cross-channel structure generative imputation must learn is largely unobserved.

items.title: Evidence Field for Histopathology: Cross-Centre Evaluation and Replayable Spatial Decisions
items.summary: Histopathology classifiers must transfer across acquisition sites while exposing evidence that can be checked independently. Evidence Field couples learned image measurements and spatial classification with a native covering-program record. We evaluate this architecture on all 455,954 released CAMELYON17-WILDS patches, using patient-separated source partitions and two held-out hospital centres. Eighteen from-scratch fits compare four Evidence Field objectives with residual convolutional and compact vision-transformer classifiers. Checkpoints, temperatures and review thresholds are selected using source validation. The source-selected paired-cross-entropy ensemble achieves areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.9356 and 0.9453, with accuracies of 84.46% and 86.77% at the two held-out centres. Corresponding convolutional values are 0.7352 and 0.7656, and transformer values are 0.8502 and 0.7924. Evidence Field has 10,550 trainable parameters per member and additionally returns selected covers, signed region and interaction terms, contextual dependencies and independently reconstructible predictions. Patient-cluster intervals, calibration, source-fixed review policies and recorded training resources characterize the results. A 340-image, three-member audit reconstructs probability mixtures and 6,120 class programs under three rigid views. The evaluation supports cross-centre discrimination and reproducible computation for these implemented models; unequal family tuning, previously examined public targets and limited patient groups constrain broader interpretation.

items.title: Slip-Induced Fall Suppression During Cornering for a Remotely Operated Motorcycle with a Rear-Wheel-Swing Mechanism
items.summary: Slip-induced falls when riding motorcycles are difficult to avoid even for expert riders and represent a major cause of single-vehicle accidents. Despite their prevalence, no practical solution has yet been proposed to suppress this phenomenon. We previously introduced a motorcycle model applicable to systems with both front- and rear- wheel steering. In this paper, we extend that model and formulate the suppression of slip-induced falls as an optimization problem that distributes assistive control inputs according to vehicle speed and road surface conditions. To evaluate the proposed method, we developed a remotely operated motorcycle and conducted experiments under two scenarios: slalom driving on a low-friction surface at 5.5 m/s, and turning maneuvers on synthetic ice to simulate driving over manholes on rainy days. The results demonstrate that our approach successfully suppresses falls under these challenging conditions.

items.title: Superfast Spectral Compressed Sensing with Quadratic Convergence
items.summary: In this paper, we study the spectral compressed sensing problem of recovering a spectrally sparse signal from linear compressive measurements. Exploiting the low-rank Hankel structure associated with the signal, we formulate a nonconvex fixed-rank optimization problem with a Hankel regularization. We propose a Superfast Iterative Hard Thresholding (SIHT) algorithm, where each iteration consists of a tangent-space least-squares update followed by a fixed-rank hard thresholding projection. SIHT is the first nonconvex algorithm with provable quadratic convergence for spectral compressed sensing. For random Gaussian measurements, it achieves exact recovery in the noiseless case and stable recovery in the noisy case with near-optimal sample complexity. To efficiently implement SIHT, we develop a parameterized conjugate gradient method for solving the least-squares subproblem, endowing SIHT with state-of-the-art computational and memory efficiency. Numerical experiments are provided to validate our results.

items.title: Orientation-Aware Deep Learning Framework for RSSI-Based Indoor Localization in RIS-Aided mmWave Systems
items.summary: Reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-aided millimeter wave (mmWave) systems provide directional measurements of received power for indoor localization, but device orientation changes the fingerprints. This work proposes an orientation-aware dual-stream gated (O-DSG) deep learning framework for received signal strength indicator (RSSI)-based indoor localization. An orientation classifier estimates device orientation from RSSI, so inference needs only received power. An embedding of the predicted angle and posterior entropy controls feature modulation and soft expert gating. Parallel convolutional and statistical streams are fused through bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) processing and temporal attention. Single-user measurements in an indoor laboratory at 28 GHz under non-line-of-sight (NLoS) conditions yield a median localization error of 0.141 m, a 25.8% improvement over the closest evaluated baseline (supplied with the measured orientation), and 92.3% orientation classification accuracy across four discrete classes. In spatial regions withheld from training, O-DSG has an average median error of 0.247 m, against 0.392 m for a validation-selected sequence model. A separate offline evaluation constructs non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA)-style power mixtures from the single-user measurements and measures localization accuracy and computational scaling with up to eight emulated users whose power contributions overlap, under the specified mixture model.

items.title: From Individual Songs to Music Corpora: Evaluating Explainable Harmonic Decision-Making on HookTheory
items.summary: Automatic melody harmonization is often evaluated through individual compositions or data-driven corpus models. This study examines whether an explainable harmonic decision model developed for individual songs can be applied to independently collected human annotations without changing its rules. We evaluate a frozen Explainable Melody Harmonizer (EMH) on selected HookTheory excerpts containing aligned melody and chord annotations. EMH generates chord sequences from melody alone using explicit criteria for melodic compatibility, harmonic function, persistence, cadence, meter-aware segmentation, and Viterbi-like optimization. Human chords are withheld during generation and used only for post-hoc comparison. Nineteen excerpts yielded 439 evaluable harmonic segments. Exact chord agreement reached 20.50%, chord-root agreement 31.66%, and harmonic-function agreement 47.62%, with functions assessed relative to the key inferred by EMH. Decision-level analysis identified 203 segments (46.24%) where the human chord lay outside the model's candidate vocabulary and 146 (33.26%) where it was available but not selected. These findings distinguish representational limitations from differences in chord selection without treating the human reference as the only musically valid solution. The study demonstrates a reproducible, interpretable approach to corpus-based evaluation of harmonic decision-making.

items.title: Deep Learning for Forest Plantation Mapping in Godavari Districts of Andhra Pradesh, India
items.summary: Small-area forest plantations play a vital role in the socioeconomic well-being of farmers in Southeast Asia. Most plantations are established on former agricultural land, often on land less suitable for agriculture. Plantations that are converted from natural forest have adverse impacts on biodiversity. Mapping small-area plantations is thus important to understand the dynamics of forest cover in Southeast Asia and to study the social, economic, and ecological effects of this important land cover and land use change. While the small size of forest plantations makes it difficult to detect them using moderate resolution satellite sensors, the problem is exacerbated by the high degree of mixing between plantations, surrounding vegetation, and other land covers, which often show variegated responses in satellite signals across space and time. In this paper, we study the problem of mapping small-area forest plantations in East and West Godavari districts of Andhra Pradesh, India using deep learning methods. Remotely sensed cloud-free data from the Harmonized Landsat Sentinel-2 S10 product were classified using a pixel-level neural network and training data labeled using a field-based survey in concert with expert aerial photo interpretation. We compare the performance of deep learning methods with a baseline random forest classifier in our study region of 21543 sq. km over a period of 3 years and analyze the differences in the results across land cover classes and seasons.

items.title: LWM-TF: A Wireless Foundation Model on 5G NR Time-Frequency Resource Grids
items.summary: Received OFDM grids preserve both pilot and payload observations, yet wireless foundation models are rarely pre-trained on them. We introduce LWM-TF, a 9.58M-parameter factorized masked autoencoder pre-trained on complex 5G NR uplink grids taken after the FFT and before channel estimation. Each block attends first across OFDM symbols and then across resource blocks and receive antennas, and the mask follows the same two axes. Because the payload phase is unpredictable, the model reconstructs the normalized log-power of each masked token and predicts its scale separately; ablations show that the two terms are complementary and that this target outperforms complex-signal reconstruction. The encoder is pre-trained on 850,496 physical uplink shared channel (PUSCH) slots from a 10^6-slot dataset simulated with the NR transmit chain under various channel conditions. With the encoder frozen, linear probes classify modulation, predict CRC success, and detect UE mobility. On a separately generated test set, 16 labeled slots per class give 0.85 modulation accuracy, 0.82 CRC area under the ROC curve (AUROC), and 0.73 mobility AUROC, ahead of a supervised CNN on every paired draw. With 10,000 labels the probes reach 0.94, 0.96, and 0.92, well above engineered receiver statistics, and detect mobility where the CNN stays at chance. Without any impairment labels, distances in the frozen feature space flag unseen waveform impairments with 0.78 macro AUROC, against 0.68 for receiver statistics. A single pre-trained encoder thus provides receiver features that transfer across tasks, most strongly when labels are scarce.

items.title: TTS-Q: Perception-Guided Post-Training Quantization of Text-to-Speech Diffusion Transformers
items.summary: Zero-shot text-to-speech (TTS) can clone a voice from seconds of audio. Yet the quality comes from billion-parameter diffusion transformers whose size and multi-step sampling put them out of reach of the on-device, assistive, and real-time applications that need them most. Post-training quantization (PTQ) shrinks such models without retraining, but it has been built for language and vision, not speech. At 4 bits, a strong quantizer leaves intelligibility close to full precision but consistently erodes speaker timbre, so error rates stay low while the voice drifts from the target speaker. We ask why quantization hurts speech, where the damage lives, and whether it can be repaired without retraining. To find out, we run the first 4-bit weight-and-activation (W4A4) PTQ study of a TTS diffusion transformer at 1B and 3.5B. The timbre cost comes from both the weight and the activation quantization, but only the activation part has the timestep structure a precision schedule can exploit. We therefore introduce TTS-Q, which selects hard-to-quantize items from task-matched calibration candidates and applies a budget-balanced mixed-precision schedule that assigns higher precision to late-step feed-forward activations. TTS-Q recovers timbre best at both scales, at no cost to intelligibility. Separately, the deployed calibrated-W4A4 reference reduces peak memory on GPU, providing a practical reference for resource-constrained TTS deployment.

items.title: BOLT: Universal Classifier Training via a Bayes-Error Upper Bound
items.summary: This work introduces a novel approach to compute a universal upper bound on the Bayes error rate (BER) from classifier-output samples, which serves as a Bayes-error-related performance criterion for the underlying classification task. We show that the bound is tight in the binary case and characterize the max-sum gap that appears in the aggregate multiclass formulation. Based on this bound, we define a new loss function, called Bayes optimal learning threshold (BOLT), for training parameterized classifiers. For each data sample, the BOLT loss computes a term whose expectation upper-bounds the Bayes error, so that during training the model parameters can be updated toward minimizing this bound. Numerical experiments with both synthetic and real-world datasets show that, in the reported settings, BOLT training often attains lower held-out classification error than cross-entropy training.

items.title: Adaptive Dead-Zone Dual Sliding Mode Observer for Reliable Electrochemical Model-Based SOC Estimation
items.summary: Accurate state-of-charge (SOC) estimation is essential for safe and efficient lithium-ion battery operation. Electrochemical models provide physically grounded SOC estimates, but nonlinear voltage dynamics and coupled state-parameter errors can destabilize online adaptation. This paper proposes an adaptive dead-zone dual sliding-mode observer (ADZ-DSMO) based on an improved extended single-particle (IESP) model. A state SMO estimates SOC-related states, while a parameter SMO updates dominant model parameters. An online-computable, Lyapunov-guided adaptive boundary selectively gates parameter updates while the state observer remains active at every sampling step. Validation on a Panasonic NCR18650PF cell under 1C and 3C constant-current discharge and the Urban Dynamometer Driving Schedule (UDDS) and New European Driving Cycle (NEDC) profiles shows lower SOC estimation errors than conventional dual SMO and the IESP-based dual extended Kalman filter (DEKF). Compared with DEKF, the proposed observer provides faster recovery from a 30% initial SOC bias. Selective parameter updating reduces the average per-step computation time compared with the always-updating dual SMO. Temperature tests and capacity-based, model-generated aging cases further assess robustness. These results support adaptive gating as a means of reducing error propagation and computational overhead in electrochemical-model-based joint state-parameter estimation.

items.title: Integer-Free Control Synthesis for Signal Temporal Logic via Ranked Implicants
items.summary: This paper proposes an integer-free method for control synthesis of nonlinear discrete-time systems under finite-horizon Signal Temporal Logic (STL) constraints. Instead of introducing integer variables, we consider the discrete choices of the specification in a ranked order and solve a standard nonlinear program for each selected choice until a satisfying trajectory is found. We first define implicants as sets of timed atomic constraints whose joint satisfaction is sufficient to satisfy the specification. A reference trajectory obtained from a smooth approximation of the STL robustness is used to rank these implicants. Fixing one implicant turns the problem into a standard nonlinear program with no auxiliary weights or bilinear terms. If the solution does not satisfy the specification, the next implicant will be considered. We prove soundness and completeness of our method relative to the nonlinear programming solver. Numerical evaluation on nonlinear multi-agent systems shows that our proposed method identifies satisfying trajectories where the exact continuous reformulation fails, and moreover, it is faster than a mixed-integer formulation of the same specification.

items.title: MIDI-REPA: Improving Text-to-Music Generation with Symbolic Representation Alignment
items.summary: State-of-the-art text-to-music models increasingly rely on scaling model capacity, data, and compute, while still learning musical structure directly from dense audio. Yet melody, rhythm, harmony, and structure can be represented compactly in symbolic form. We introduce MIDI-REPA, a representation-alignment framework that derives MIDI supervision from automatic music transcription (AMT) to align intermediate representations of a flow-matching DiT. Building on the 122M-parameter FluxAudio-S baseline from the 2026 ICME Academic Text-To-Music Challenge, we investigate what, where, and when to align. Aligning a MuScriptor-derived piano roll with an early DiT layer throughout the full flow trajectory performs the best. Without additional training data or techniques, MIDI-REPA remains competitive on the ATTM objective metrics while remaining trainable on a single RTX 3090 in about 31 hours. Our results highlight symbolic supervision as a simple and inexpensive learning signal for improving text-to-music generation. We release our transcription pipeline, JamendoMIDI, training code, and audio samples at https://midi-repa.vaclis.net.

items.title: Adaptive Prescribed Performance Trajectory Tracking for Uncertain Autonomous Underwater Vehicles With Input Saturation
items.summary: Accurate trajectory tracking is essential for autonomous underwater vehicles operating with uncertain hydrodynamics and limited thruster authority. This paper develops a low-complexity adaptive prescribed performance controller for uncertain underwater vehicle dynamics with coupled and saturated inputs. The proposed method adapts the performance functions directly through the mismatch between the requested and saturated control inputs, enlarging the performance funnels only when the available actuation cannot meet the nominal specifications. A coupled invariant-set analysis establishes boundedness of all closed-loop signals, prescribed bounds on the filtered tracking errors, and explicit feasibility conditions. Comparative simulations on a BlueROV2 underwater vehicle show that the adaptive design maintains prescribed performance during a figure-eight maneuver, whereas conventional prescribed performance control loses feasibility under input limits. A real-time pool experiment further demonstrates stable trajectory tracking and the practical implementation of the proposed method on an underwater robotic platform.

items.title: Probing Neural Audio Codecs with Speaker Traits and Speech Characteristics
items.summary: Neural audio codecs are increasingly used for low-bitrate speech coding and serve as tokenizers for speech language models, yet it remains unclear how their codebook hierarchies encode speaker traits and speech characteristics. We systematically study 17 multi-codebook neural audio codecs across seven traits: sex, age, accent, voice quality, emotion, speech flow, and non-verbal sounds. For each codec, we reconstruct speech using partial codebooks and use machine listeners to compare trait predictions on each reconstruction. We measure prediction agreement with reweighted Cohen's \k{appa}, and define trait depth as a proxy for the codebook depth by which each trait is encoded and recoverable. Overall, sex has the shallowest trait depth, followed by speech flow, whereas voice quality and age group require deeper stacks; emotion, accent, and non-verbal sounds fall in between. Within each trait, speech-flow classes are at relatively similar trait depths, whereas emotion, accent, and non-verbal sounds differ more. Additionally, we explore how certain codec design choices relate to trait depths. These findings show that codebook hierarchies are trait-dependent and may not exhibit uniform coarse-to-fine structures, motivating trait-specific codec evaluation and design for future applications.

items.title: Congestion Price Uncertainty From Interconnection Queue by Monte Carlo Sampling
items.summary: The generation interconnection queue adds discrete uncertainty to power grid congestion price estimates on the project planning timescale. The conventional approach to this uncertainty is to make an informed guess of the single or few most likely configurations of generators that interconnect. In this paper, we show that Monte Carlo sampling is a more effective alternative. Given an estimate of the joint probability distribution of generator interconnections, a small number of samples yields good estimates of the congestion distribution. Crucially, this problem is not about rare events, but rather about the expected congestion over the worst times of the year, which makes congestion a common outcome over the distribution of interconnection events. We give empirical results on a 2000-bus network, averaging price outcomes from security-constrained DCOPF over eight different loading scenarios. For each line and contingency of the network, we estimate the full distribution as well as mean price and probability of exceeding a price threshold. Single-point estimates are unreliable and can be misleading about whether a line is likely to be congested. Combining the top k probability configurations yields improved estimates; however, sampling the same number from a distribution gives a more robust result of similar accuracy, as well as error estimates. Including correlation in the distribution model introduces small changes, showing that standard Bernoulli distributions suffice in most cases. The sampling approach is also applicable to large-load interconnection and should be of interest for planning both generation and large-load projects.

items.title: Objective-Aware Policy Orchestration for O-RAN Service Provisioning
items.summary: O-RAN enables the deployment of heterogeneous control and provisioning algorithms through open interfaces and programmable intelligent controllers. However, most existing intelligent O-RAN solutions rely on a single optimization strategy designed for a fixed operational objective, limiting their ability to adapt when network conditions or operator priorities change. This paper proposes an objective-aware policy orchestration framework that selects the most appropriate provisioning policy for each control window based on the current network context and operator objective. The framework orchestrates a portfolio of heterogeneous provisioning experts using contextual-bandit learning. Two policy selectors, Linear Thompson Sampling and a Bootstrap Tree ensemble, are evaluated against static provisioning policies and a deterministic rule-based orchestrator. Experimental results show that learning-based policy orchestration can effectively adapt policy selection to varying operating conditions, improving overall objective-aware performance while preserving the modularity of existing provisioning algorithms.

items.title: Tile-Based Phase Unwrapping with Reliability-Ordered Joining and Residual-Weighted Multipath Averaging
items.summary: Phase unwrapping recovers a continuous phase map from measurements known only modulo 2π, in the presence of noise and discontinuities. We propose a tile-based method that combines local spectral reconstruction, reliability-ordered tile joining, and residual-weighted multipath averaging. Each tile is reconstructed by a discrete cosine transform (DCT) least-squares solve, and robust measurements along tile borders guide their joining along a spanning tree. We repeat this reconstruction on shifted tile grids and on rotated and reflected copies of the image, which changes tile borders and joining paths. A residual-weighted average combines the resulting reconstructions, which are computed in parallel and averaged on the fly without being stored. We also introduce the corrected circular rewrapping error, a congruence measure: after removing a global phase offset, it measures how far the rewrapped reconstruction is from the observed phase. It applies to least-squares and path-based methods, even without an unwrapped reference. Used with reference-based errors, it separates agreement with the measurement from recovery of the correct number of cycles. Experiments on radar-interferometric, magnetic-resonance, holographic, and constructed phase images compare our method with seven reference algorithms. Among the methods that complete every test image, ours has the lowest mean fraction of pixels with an error above π. On the images all methods complete, it lies on several speed-accuracy Pareto fronts. Error maps also reveal isolated cycle errors that average scores or congruence alone can hide.

items.title: From Global to Local: Hierarchical Probabilistic Verification for Reachability Learning
items.summary: Hamilton-Jacobi (HJ) reachability provides formal safety guarantees for nonlinear systems. However, it becomes computationally intractable in high-dimensional settings, motivating learning-based approximations that may introduce unsafe errors or overly optimistic safe sets. In this work, we propose a hierarchical probabilistic verification framework for reachability learning that bridges offline global certification and online local refinement. We first construct a coarse, conservative under-approximation of the reach-avoid safe set using scenario optimization, providing an efficient global probabilistic certificate. We then introduce an online local refinement module that is structurally anchored to the global certificate and recovers regions excluded by the global verification. This refinement reduces conservatism while focusing computation on critical regions of the state space. Integrated with a condition-based switching mechanism between a learned reachability policy and a model-based controller, the proposed framework improves success rates in goal-reaching tasks with safety constraints, as demonstrated in drone-racing simulation experiments.

items.title: Digital Twin-Conditioned RSS-Fingerprint Localization in Cell-Free Millimeter-Wave Networks
items.summary: Digital twins (DTs) can generate dense synthetic fingerprints for localization via ray tracing, yet the sim-to-real domain gap limits their direct use, particularly in cell-free millimeter-wave (mmWave) deployments where distributed geometries and blockage-induced sparsity widen the mismatch. We propose DT-conditioned (DTCond), a framework that fuses real and DT beam-domain fingerprints as complementary inputs through per-domain encoders, learnable per-access point (AP) attention, and calibrated uncertainty. We derive oracle and pipeline Cramér-Rao bounds (CRBs) for DT-aided fingerprint localization, proving that DT information strictly tightens the positioning bound whenever spatial structure is preserved, with a heteroscedastic refinement that tightens the bound by a further 9.1%. On a real 28 GHz cell-free testbed, the deployable two-stage pipeline, which reads the DT fingerprint at a coarse k-nearest neighbor (k-NN) estimate, achieves 0.284 m mean error against 0.313 m for real-only k-NN. With the DT fingerprint read at the true position (oracle input), DT conditioning achieves 0.186 m mean error, validated through a ten-method ablation against domain-adaptation (DA) and transfer-learning baselines, and a 48% improvement on unseen regions. Multi-user self-attention provides 31-41% per-user gain for emulated simultaneous users, and progressive calibration reduces the measurement budget by 50%. As a use case, localization drives network configuration in closed loop. Between beam sweeps, a DT updated from measured RSS and read at the tracked position estimate selects the 3 of 81 beam pairs that each AP trains. With 49 calibration anchors in the update, the mean beam-selection loss stays below 1 dB over 2 m of motion, whereas reusing the last sweep loses 2.7 dB after 1 m.

items.title: Range Ambiguity Identification and Elimination by Leveraging Temporal Broadening Effect for THz Sensing
items.summary: High pulse repetition frequency (PRF) operation improves Doppler unambiguous sensing but reduces the maximum unambiguous range of a terahertz (THz) pulsed radar. Echoes from targets beyond this range can be incorrectly associated with subsequent transmitted pulses, causing the targets to appear at shorter ranges. This paper proposes a receiver-side framework that exploits the THz-specific temporal broadening effect as a distance-dependent signature to resolve range ambiguity. For each detected echo, the receiver applies broadening-matched filtering with references corresponding to candidate target ranges. The filter outputs are combined across pulses with Doppler compensation, and the largest normalised combined response identifies the ambiguity order needed to recover the true target range. The selected reference is then reused to reduce mismatch loss in subsequent range and velocity estimation. Simulations under known atmospheric conditions, with targets occupying distinct apparent-delay bins, demonstrate reliable range recovery beyond the conventional unambiguous interval. Range estimation errors conditioned on correct ambiguity-order identification, together with the reported velocity estimation errors, approach their corresponding derived Cramér--Rao bounds. The method preserves a fixed transmitted pulse shape, PRF, and sampling rate, at the expense of a higher signal-to-clutter-plus-noise ratio requirement for ambiguity identification relative to the evaluated diversity-based techniques.

items.title: Planning to Learn: Real-Time Robust Adaptive Control on the GPU with Guaranteed Future Learning
items.summary: Robust adaptive control is vital for keeping robots safe while actively reducing uncertainty in unfamiliar settings. However, traditional methods are often conservative since they fail to account for guaranteed future parameter learning during planning and struggle to scale to high-dimensional systems. In this work, we present A-SLS, a learning-aware robust adaptive model predictive control (RAMPC) framework based on system-level synthesis. A-SLS forecasts future parameter uncertainty and preserves correlations between process disturbances, parameter error, and estimate updates to construct tight, guaranteed reachable sets that account for future information gain. We also develop a GPU-accelerated A-SLS solver to enable real-time performance. Across nonlinear robotic systems, A-SLS reduces reachable-tube conservativeness, maintains real-time performance, and scales to whole-body control for a quadruped with 61 states, 8 uncertain parameters, and 12 control inputs. We further demonstrate the approach on hardware, where a physical Crazyflie drone learns an uncertain dynamics parameter online to stabilize on the fly.

items.title: Resilient and Efficient Aerial Wireless Sensor Networks Using Pinching-Antenna Systems
items.summary: This paper proposes a pinching antenna system to enhance the connectivity and efficiency in aerial wireless networks. The algebraic connectivity of the network's graph is maximized by optimizing the placement of the pinching antenna elements in the uplink and downlink waveguides. The number of deployed unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) is minimized while maintaining a minimum network connectivity indicator. A heuristic pinching antenna placement algorithm is designed to maximize the network connectivity. An iterative UAV deployment algorithm is also designed to find the minimum number of UAVs, their placement locations, and the pinching antenna placement. Simulation results show that the considered pinching antenna system improves network connectivity and efficiency.

items.title: Co-designing a Layered Control Architecture
items.summary: Layered control architectures (LCAs) are ubiquitous in complex engineering systems. However, in practice they are largely designed ad hoc and mostly dictated by the experience of the designer. This is because there is currently no systematic and practically applicable theory available to holistically design LCAs. Hence, systematically reasoning about the optimality, stability, and feasibility of the LCA design is not possible. We set a first step toward such a theory by presenting a framework for co-designing a two-layer LCA for a linear time-invariant plant. The resulting co-design problem optimizes over architectural design variables (e.g., reduced order model dimension and sampling ratio between the layers) and tuning-based design variables (e.g., the numerical values of the feedback gain or the matrices of the reduced order model), all subject to constraints that ensure stability, feasibility, and compute properties of the closed-loop LCA. The proposed formulation allows to make informed tradeoffs along the Pareto front traced over different axes of optimality, e.g., speed, accuracy or computational effort. We demonstrate the effect of making various tradeoffs in a simple numerical example.

items.title: CIViC: Evidence Gates for Audio-Conditioned Visual Prediction on Proxy Tasks
items.summary: Removing audio can shift a visual predictor's output without showing whether the task uses the intended audio information. We introduce Conditional Input and Visual Interpretation Checks (CIViC), a four-gate protocol that links an interpretation to an intervention, held-out task comparison, or endpoint control. We demonstrate CIViC on actor-disjoint face-raster tests, a synthetic audio-feature mixture, and source-video-disjoint SpeakerVid proxy tasks. In the static face-raster test, cross-actor audio replacement meets the registered detection rule with a small effect; on a separate temporal endpoint, constant-audio fits score better than audio-trained fits in four matched seeds. In the synthetic mixture, the condition-augmented fit has higher 1,000-step RMSE than the audio-only fit (0.1807 vs. 0.1707), with the gap shrinking during training. In the SpeakerVid proxy, the five-feature-zero fit (five low-level audio summaries zeroed; identity, dialogue, and condition inputs retained) has lower whole-frame grayscale RMSE than aligned audio across four held-out conditions and five paired seeds, while aligned audio has lower segment-drift error. The results show that output activation, held-out error, and endpoint controls support different interpretations across these proxy tasks.

items.title: Optimally Trading Energy for Information through Speed Trajectory Optimization of Sustainably Powered Mobile Robots
items.summary: Sustainably powered mobile robots enable long-duration observational missions by harvesting energy from the environment. However, effective autonomy requires the robots to make decisions as to how to allocate this energy to maximize information quality over time. In this paper, we study a persistent (infinite-horizon) speed trajectory optimization problem that is posed as a periodic optimal control problem in which a robot repeatedly traverses a fixed closed path, coupling a super-linear propulsion cost with dynamic information gain and decay. Using the information-theoretic quantity of clarity as an information metric, we first derive the necessary conditions for optimal control. We then derive a number of specialized follow-on properties, which characterize (i) the nature of the optimal control when points on the path are of varying importance and when they are of equal importance, along with (ii) a high-speed information limit that is approached when energy reserves approach infinity. We illustrate the information-optimal speed trajectories on a simple example in order to showcase key trends that are followed under the optimized speed profile. This is followed by a simulation study based on the persistent characterization of salinity in the Chesapeake Bay, illustrating the practical merit of applying the results from this work.

items.title: Clarity-Driven Adaptive Mission Planning for a Solar-Powered Autonomous Surface Vessel
items.summary: This paper presents a comprehensive methodology, backed by simulation and experimental results, for an adaptive mission planning strategy that is mathematically grounded in the maximization of the information-driven quantity of clarity. In particular, the methodology introduced in this work addresses the use of sustainably powered autonomous surface vessels (ASVs) to perform scientific missions that prioritize locations of maximum interest. Because these locations of maximum interest are not known a priori but are rather identified based on in-situ measurements, online adaptation is essential for mission planning. Furthermore, the reliance on a limited-power renewable resource requires an adaptation strategy that maximizes information gathering subject to mobility restrictions imposed by the renewable resource. Our approach addresses these challenges through a clarity-driven ergodic search, where clarity represents a mathematical quantity that has been rigorously linked to differential (information) entropy. In our approach, a target clarity map is adapted online to reflect the prioritization of certain areas based on in-situ measurements, and an ergodic path planner continually re-plans based on the target clarity map and ASV speed limitations (driven by the renewable propulsion source). Focusing on a solar-powered ASV, we present simulations and experiments conducted at Jordan Lake, North Carolina, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

items.title: SNOAR: Self-training with Noise filtering, Observation adding, and Remixing for Speech Denoising Without Clean References
items.summary: Unsupervised speech denoising methods such as MixIT and noisy-target training can be trained directly on noisy recordings, avoiding the sim-to-real gap of synthetic training data, but remain well below supervised performance. Teacher--student self-training, as in RemixIT, narrows this gap by remixing a teacher's estimates into new mixtures that supervise a student; however, since the student is trained only toward the teacher's estimates, teacher errors, in particular over-suppressed speech, are never recovered and propagate as the teacher is updated from the student. We propose SNOAR, a self-training framework that corrects the teacher's estimates before use: the noise leaked into its speech estimate is removed by differential noise filtering (DNF), and part of the noisy observation is added back in to restore suppressed speech and attenuate artifacts. We show that the two corrections depend on each other, as without DNF the loop collapses to the identity mapping. Compared to RemixIT, SNOAR is more stable along training and outperforms it in signal-based, perceptual, and word error rate metrics, reaching 97\% of the SI-SDR improvement of a fully-supervised topline on WHAM!; on real CHiME-3 recordings, it improves every metric of three different teachers, while RemixIT degrades their perceptual quality.

items.title: Zero-Shot Spoken Language Understanding with SLAM-ASR: What Do Monolingual ASR-Trained Linear Projectors Enable?
items.summary: The SLAM-ASR framework connects the features of a frozen speech encoder as input to a frozen LLM decoder to enable speech transcription. In this work we ask whether this training-on speech transcription-provides the LLM with the capability to also perform spoken language understanding (SLU) tasks, by training monolingual projectors on 11 languages. When prompted to answer a yes/no question about the input speech, the mean instruction following rate (IFR) is 49.8%. When not following the instruction, these models default back to transcription. The transcription quality-measured by the character error rate (CER)-is not sufficient to predict IFR. Remarkably, when the model is instructed to answer the topic question as a single digit option, the mean IFR rises to 81.3%. Our models score a mean 23.2% topic balanced accuracy (BAcc) against 14.3% chance. However, the same decoder scores a mean 71.5% BAcc when using reference transcripts as text input. This indicates a failure of the projector to transfer information for the SLU tasks.

items.title: Analog RF Computing for Integrated Data and AI Flows Over Wireless Networks
items.summary: Many resource-constrained edge devices require artificial intelligence (AI) services but are not powerful enough to store or execute neural networks (NNs). Analog radio frequency (RF) computing addresses this limitation by letting a base station (BS) multicast a waveform encoding NN weights to different clients. Each client then multiplies the received weight-encoded waveform with its locally generated input-encoded waveform through a passive mixer in its RF frontend, thereby realizing the matrix-vector multiplications (MVMs) needed for AI inference with an extremely low power and memory requirement. This can enable telecom operators to provide AI inference services to the edge devices connected to their networks. In practice, however, this multicast AI flow must share the spectrum, power, and spatial resources with other data flows. This paper considers a multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO) downlink scenario and studies the resulting relative aggregate data rate reduction from integrating the multicast AI flow with the unicast data flows. We formulate a joint beamforming problem for the data and AI flows to maximize the aggregate data rate subject to computing accuracy, client energy, total power, and hardware-related constraints. We develop a weighted minimum mean-square error (WMMSE)-based algorithm to solve the problem. Numerical results based on 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) channels show that the relative aggregate data rate reduction from integrating an AI flow with data flows is below 5% in representative settings. This indicates that telecom operators can use analog RF computing to provide edge AI services while providing data communication services simultaneously.

items.title: A Response to the Reply Presented in "A Fair Comparison of Sliding-Mode and Immersion-and-Invariance Observers"
items.summary: In response to the reply presented in [Muñoz-Vázquez and Sánchez-Torres(2026)], this technical report extends the experimental evaluation of position-feedback velocity observers and adaptive tracking controllers for a pendular system with nonlinear friction reported in [Cervantes-Pérez et al.(2026)]. The immersion and invariance (I&I) adaptive control scheme proposed in [Romero et al.(2025)], whose gains are tuned according to the guidelines presented in [Ortega et al.(2025)], is compared with a control scheme employing the adaptive modi?ed super-twisting observer of [Dávila et al.(2006)], whose observer gains are selected according to the guidelines proposed in [Muñoz-Vázquez and Sánchez-Torres(2026)]. Although these "tuning guidelines" attenuate chattering in certain scenarios, the experimental results reported here show that they do not eliminate it in general.

items.title: The MPB Corpus: A Dataset of Melody, Rhythm, Harmony, and Melody-Harmony Relationships in Brazilian Popular Music
items.summary: PLEASE CHECK AND REFER TO THE PUBLISHED VERSION OF THIS PAPER ON https://doi.org/10.5334/tismir.357 This paper presents the MPB Corpus, a dataset of Brazilian Popular Music (Musica Popular Brasileira, MPB) comprising derived symbolic annotations for 500 pieces across four musical parameters -- melodic contour, melodic rhythm, harmony, and the melody-harmony relationship -- making it the most comprehensive dataset to date for computational musicology of Brazilian music. It is released under a CC-BY-4.0 license in an open, machine-readable tabular format, with documentation and reproducible analysis code. Because the annotations were derived from copyrighted musical scores, the corpus contains no audio recordings or score-level representations such as MIDI or MusicXML; it nonetheless provides a reusable resource for MIR research on a culturally significant repertoire that remains underrepresented in existing datasets. To support the encoding process, we introduce analytical models for capturing rhythmic and melodic information, along with tailored visualizations and summary metrics. Finally, we present a brief exploratory analysis illustrating the dataset's potential for formulating and addressing musicological questions about the genre.

items.title: Navigation by Skylight Polarization via Rayleigh Model Optimization on a Road Vehicle
items.summary: Reliable absolute heading estimation is critical for road-vehicle navigation, particularly when magnetic, inertial, or GNSS-based references are degraded. This paper presents a skylight polarization navigation method that estimates vehicle heading by globally optimizing a Rayleigh sky model against measurements from a division-of-focal-plane polarimetric camera. The proposed framework combines a pinhole camera model, a single-scattering Rayleigh polarization model, and a solar position algorithm to synthesize the expected full image angle of polarization distribution for candidate vehicle states. A degree of polarization weighted root mean square error objective function compares measured and simulated polarization patterns, allowing the estimator to use all available sky information while attenuating low confidence pixels caused by clouds, buildings, foliage, and other depolarizing occlusions. Experimental evaluation is performed using three urban road vehicle trajectories collected with a roof mounted polarimetric camera and a high precision dual-antenna GNSS/INS reference system. Results show sub-degree RMS yaw error across all trajectories, ranging from $0.718^{\circ}$ to $0.889^{\circ}$. Compared with representative feature-based and model-based polarization navigation methods, the proposed approach reduces RMS heading error by up to 87% and demonstrates improved robustness to partial sky occlusion.

items.title: Electrical Power Grid Reliability Assessment Exposed to Straight Line Winds
items.summary: Maintaining the resilience and reliability of electrical power grids under weather driven disturbances is a critical challenge for modern power system planning and operation. Among weather driven hazards, tornadoes and hurricanes are mostly considered for research purpose overlooking straight line winds despite its significant contribution to transmission line outages and cascading effects. Accurate modeling of these events is essential for operational decision making, and long term infrastructure planning and investment. This research explores the probabilistic risk assessment of transmission lines under straight line winds and their impacts on system level performance. The approach examines the probability of transmission towers failure, transmission lines outages, cascading effects, and identify critical transmission lines. The IEEE 118 bus system was utilized to validate the proposed approach and to demonstrate how wind induced component failures propagate throughout the network, affecting power grid reliability.

items.title: Optimal Demand Response-Based Energy Management for Campus Buildings with Battery Energy Storage Systems: A Case Study of the ELB Building
items.summary: Buildings account for a significant portion of global electricity consumption, making demand response (DR) an effective strategy for reducing energy costs and improving grid flexibility. This paper presents an optimal energy management framework for a campus building that integrates demand response and battery energy storage systems (BESS) to minimize electricity costs while satisfying operational constraints and occupant comfort requirements. The proposed optimization model schedules building loads and battery charging/discharging based on time-varying electricity prices and building demand profiles. The framework is validated using the Engineering Laboratory Building (ELB) at the University of Michigan-Dearborn as a real-world case study. Four operating scenarios are investigated: (i) baseline operation, (ii) demand response without battery energy storage, (iii) battery energy storage, and (iv) demand response with battery energy storage. Simulation results demonstrate that demand alone reduces the building's electricity cost by approximately 12% compared with conventional operation. When battery energy storage is incorporated, the total electricity cost reduction increases to approximately 26%, highlighting the significant economic benefits of coordinated demand response and energy storage scheduling. The results demonstrate that integrating battery energy storage with demand response substantially enhances the operational flexibility of campus buildings and provides an effective solution for cost-effective and sustainable building energy management.

items.title: A comparative assessment of global building and settlement datasets across geographic and settlement contexts
items.summary: Global building and settlement products increasingly support population mapping, exposure assessment, and urban monitoring, yet comparative evidence remains fragmented across representations, geographic contexts, and evaluation methods. We benchmark seven global or near-global products against harmonized reference building footprints across 135 study areas. Our representation-aware framework integrates complementary measures of detection, geometric agreement, and aggregate quantity accuracy with stratified analyses of settlement characteristics, evaluation resolution, reference provenance, and temporal alignment. Overture Maps achieved the highest median city-level vector F1 (0.786), while 3D-GloBFP showed the closest aggregate building-area agreement despite weaker detection performance. Raster rankings were scale-dependent: Google Open Buildings Temporal (OBT) performed best at 10\,m (F1 = 0.680), whereas WSF Tracker led at 100\,m (F1 = 0.904) but substantially overestimated reference building area (relative bias = 1.845). Raster accuracy increased with building density ($ρ=0.58$--$0.75$), while smaller candidate footprints were disproportionately associated with vector false positives. Temporal alignment improved WSF Tracker mean city-level F1 by 0.060. These findings demonstrate that product reliability depends on representation, spatial scale, and settlement context, providing a reproducible framework for assessing the suitability of EO-derived urban information for different applications.

items.title: Tourist arrival forecasting with game-theoretic social influence weighting and deep learning
items.summary: In the era of Industry 5.0, data-driven decision-making has become indispensable for planning in service systems such as tourism. This paper proposes a non-linear hybrid approach for forecasting tourist arrivals to Hong Kong from five major source markets before COVID-19 and to Sanya, China, through the COVID-19 shock. The method integrates multiple sources of Internet big data and employs a cooperative game-theoretic algorithm to identify coalitions of opinion leaders on social media, whose content then receives larger weights. The Empirical Wavelet Transform (EWT), applied causally, manages nonstationary attributes, and a Stacked Bi-directional Long Short-Term Memory (Stacked BiLSTM) network tuned by Bayesian optimization generates the forecasts. We prove that the Shapley values of the underlying trust-weighted coverage game have a closed form and that the coalition of maximal synergy can be found exactly in polynomial time. Relative to the same network fed only with past arrivals, Internet big data reduce the one-step-ahead root mean squared error by 4.1-41.7% across the Hong Kong markets and opinion-leader weighting by a further 10.1-49.4%, against 5.3% and 8.7% for Sanya. The approach compares favorably with published benchmarks and remains robust under volatile conditions, which suggests uses in logistics, supply chains and production planning.

items.title: Optimization via a Control-Centric Framework
items.summary: Optimization plays a central role in intelligent systems and cyber-physical technologies, where speed and reliability of convergence directly impact performance. In control theory, optimization is the foundation of widely-used design methodologies such as linear quadratic regulation, $H_\infty$ control, and model predictive control. In contrast, this paper develops a control-centric framework for optimization itself, where algorithms are constructed directly from Lyapunov stability principles rather than being proposed first and analyzed afterward. A key element is the stationarity mapping, which encodes first-order optimality conditions and enables Lyapunov-based convergence analysis. By pairing a Lyapunov function with a selectable decay law, we obtain continuous-time dynamics with guaranteed exponential, finite-time, fixed-time, or prescribed-time convergence. The convergence regime thus becomes a design input: choosing among these regimes changes only the decay law, not the algorithm or its analysis. Within this framework, we introduce three feedback realizations of increasing restrictiveness: the Hessian-gradient, Newton, and gradient dynamics. These constructions unify unconstrained optimization, extend to constrained problems via Lyapunov-consistent primal-dual dynamics, and broaden results for minimax and generalized Nash equilibrium seeking problems beyond exponential stability, the last two through centralized solvers. In total, the framework spans six problem classes and four convergence regimes, yielding a unified design recipe across twenty-four combinations, some of which, to the best of our knowledge, have no direct continuous-time counterpart in the prior literature.

items.title: A$^3$PreCore: Robust Rigid Registration for Native FLAIR-Space Brain-Mask Transfer
items.summary: Reliable brain-mask transfer into native fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR) space can fail when T1-to-FLAIR rigid registration is unstable. We developed A$^3$PreCore, a six-degree-of-freedom rigid-registration strategy that aligns the full bias-corrected T1-weighted image to native FLAIR using normalized mutual information while preserving the established T1-space anatomical mask. We also introduced extended quantitative quality control (E-QC), which characterizes mask extent, field-of-view-relative position, FLAIR intensity support, boundary support, inferior morphology, and pairwise geometric disagreement. In 78 participants with paired T1-weighted and FLAIR imaging, A$^3$PreCore was compared with fsl_anat and the Brain Extraction Tool (BET). Gross rigid-body misregistration occurred in 21/78 fsl_anat outputs (26.9%) and 0/78 A$^3$PreCore outputs (exact two-sided McNemar p=9.54 x 10^-7). Among 57 participants without gross fsl_anat misregistration, A$^3$PreCore preserved close agreement (median Dice=0.993; median paired Delta NMI=-0.00007, p=0.429). A$^3$PreCore remained broadly concordant with BET (median Dice=0.955), with less inferior and extracranial extension in representative comparisons. Method-blinded neuroscientists ranked A$^3$PreCore first in 35/40 participants (87.5%). E-QC additionally exposed severe orientation-related disagreement not evident from global descriptors or centroid displacement alone. These findings support A$^3$PreCore as a robust native-FLAIR brain-mask transfer strategy and E-QC as a complementary framework for multidimensional mask characterization and participant-specific geometric quality control.

items.title: FedRIC: Heterogeneity-Aware Federated Learning with Hard Deadline Constraints in Open RAN
items.summary: Open Radio Access Networks (O-RANs) bring intelligence to disaggregated RANs through virtualized platforms and open interfaces, but the stringent latency budgets of the RAN Intelligent Controller (RIC) and heterogeneous traffic conditions make real-time deployment costly. Centralized learning is ill-suited to the RIC due to its computational burden, timing constraints, and communication overhead, motivating Federated Learning (FL) as a distributed alternative. We formulate FL in O-RAN as a Mixed-Integer Nonlinear Program (MINLP) that minimizes communication cost and learning time under heterogeneity in User Equipment (UE) compute, traffic, and channel conditions, and decompose it into a UE Assignment (UA) subproblem and a Computation and Bandwidth Allocation (CBA) subproblem. We then propose FedRIC, a heterogeneity-aware FL framework combining compressed gradient descent, slice-aware resource allocation, and multilevel hierarchical aggregation. Experiments show that FedRIC outperforms FedCOM, FedAvg, and QFedAvg in convergence rate, communication cost, and latency.

items.title: Controller- and Communication-Aware Flexibility Margins for Electric Distribution Networks
items.summary: This paper develops a framework for quantifying operational flexibility in radial electric distribution systems under coupled active- and reactive-load uncertainty. Flexibility is defined as the largest scaling of a prescribed uncertainty set that can be accommodated while satisfying network and actuator limits under a given control architecture. We consider a one-sided Euclidean set for robust demand-growth capability, with a direct extension to bidirectional variations. Under LinDistFlow, controllable distributed resources and feeder-head exchange with the upstream grid jointly balance active-power disturbances, while local Volt/VAR feedback regulates reactive power. The resulting affine closed-loop disturbance response admits exact second-order-cone robust counterparts. For fixed Volt/VAR gains, a convex reformulation jointly optimizes the flexibility margin and active-power participation factors, including feeder-head participation. A sparse load-to-generator feedforward map further captures communication constraints. Numerical studies on the Iowa-240 feeder demonstrate how the amount of control authority and communication structure shape the achievable flexibility margin.

items.title: Is Text All You Need? Text as a Universal Information Bottleneck for Speech LLMs
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) provide a powerful reasoning backbone for speech understanding, but integrating continuous acoustic signals into a pretrained LLM remains challenging. A central design question is how to tie speech representations to the LLM's text input space while preserving the continuous variation needed for different speech tasks. In this work, we propose Convex Gate (C-Gate), a speech-LLM bridge that represents each frame as a convex combination of frozen token embeddings. This architectural convex-hull constraint fixes the output codebook while allowing continuous mixtures learned from task supervision. With a Whisper-large-v3 encoder, a partially adapted Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct decoder, and joint training on speech recognition, emotion recognition, and spoken reasoning, C-Gate performs accurate transcription and emotion recognition, our representative semantic and acoustic tasks, through one shared decoder. On text-only benchmarks, the adapted decoder loses instruction-following and MMLU accuracy and matches or exceeds the original model on GSM8K and HellaSwag. We further design analyses and interventions on the trained model to examine where the bridge sequence carries task information and how the decoder reads it. These findings show how fixed text embeddings can support both semantic and acoustic readouts through continuous speech-conditioned mixtures.

items.title: Quantizer Redundancy and Exact Index Recoding in a Frozen Neural Audio Codec
items.summary: Residual scalar quantization can produce highly dependent indices when successive stages reuse identical, unscaled grids. This case study examines that behavior in a frozen neural audio codec and develops an exact recoding procedure that reduces storage while preserving its decoder inputs. Analysis of the repeated-grid recurrence identifies predictable stage sequences; finite-precision checks motivate preserving every original index through explicit exception records. The model weights and reconstruction graph remain fixed. On the studied 62- and 512-file cohorts, a predictor, adaptive coding and explicit file selection reduce complete stored bytes. The final 512-file rate is 129.591 kbps including headers, 25.943% below an original-index XZ control. Original recorded CPU runs establish bitwise latent and waveform preservation; independent readers verify exact index and metadata recovery in subsequent saved-stream experiments. Later coding choices use previously studied cohorts, and fresh encoding requires generating three alternatives. The engineering result is implementation-specific storage reduction with exact index recovery; the underlying lossy reconstruction quality remains unchanged.

items.title: vst-bench-ml: Auditable Dataset Generation for Audio Plugins
items.summary: Generating datasets with audio plugins requires preserving how each audio observation was produced. vst-bench-ml is a Python package that samples plugin parameters, coordinates rendering through a separately installed host, and records software identities, rendering settings, and output hashes for later verification. A sealed manifest binds this evidence and supports offline integrity checks without loading the plugin. A companion repository provides a sample-free VST3 test plugin, a deterministic offline host, and additional checks linking rendering attempts to recorded outputs. On a pinned macOS arm64 and Python 3.12 stack, functional validation of the pre-release versions reproduced package and host tests. Two runs in fresh processes reproduced the same render-plan hash and all eight expected output hashes, covering four sampled parameter configurations and two fixed MIDI signals; 12 negative cases also passed. Later licensed 0.1.0 release candidates passed producer-run continuous integration and local validation. Version 0.1.1 adds public Git source repositories, package-index installation, and user documentation; a separate release check reproduced the expected plan and output hashes. These checks establish integrity and repeatability within the tested setup; they do not establish portability, scientific suitability, or perceptual quality.

items.title: RRM-GPT: A Framework and Vision for Radio Resource Management Foundation Models
items.summary: Learning-based models for radio resource management (RRM) are typically built for a single function and deployment, so each new setting repeats the development pipeline. RRM decisions, however, share a common structure: each is assembled from interdependent fields, defined by the standard, whose values are selected in view of the network state. We propose RRM-GPT, an autoregressive framework for RRM foundation models that generate these decisions as a language model generates text. An encoder maps heterogeneous network observations into a common token representation, and a decoder emits the decision one field at a time, each conditioned on the network state and the fields already committed. Pretraining on unannotated network logs teaches the model what makes a decision valid and how controllers choose among valid decisions; post-training then adapts it to deployment-specific operator objectives through imitation or reinforcement learning. The framework targets two forms of reuse: a function-specific model reused across deployments, and a model shared across RRM functions that generates their interdependent decisions as one sequence. In a 5G New Radio (NR) case study, we demonstrate that a single model generates complete scheduling grants spanning user selection, timing, link adaptation, resource allocation, and control signaling. The model captures dependencies among grant fields and transfers learned behavior to an unseen scenario without adaptation.

items.title: X-Safe: Embodiment-Agnostic Safeguarding for Robot Arm Manipulation Policies via Action Masking
items.summary: Ensuring safety of learning-enabled robotic manipulation across diverse embodiments and tasks still requires significant manual engineering. For collision avoidance, existing approaches typically rely on embodiment-specific learned safety approximations or simplified robot models together with stopping-based fallback controllers that compromise performance.
